News.title: Afghan national sexually assaulted girl, 14, on Harry Potter family sightseeing tour in London – but he AVOIDS jail
News.content:
VILE FIEND Afghan national sexually assaulted girl, 14, on Harry Potter family sightseeing tour in London – but he AVOIDS jail

AN Afghan national who sexually assaulted a teenage girl on a Harry Potter sightseeing tour has been spared jail.

Abdul Barkeeh Salihi, 24, put his hand on the girl’s bottom when she and her family were in Leadenhall Market, in the City of London, to see the filming location for Diagon Alley.



Earlier the same day, Salihi had slapped the bottom of a 42-year-old woman after following her for a short distance along nearby Lombard Street.

After the sexual assault on the girl, Salihi was confronted by her family at a restaurant in an incident which ended with him throwing a chair through a window.



Salihi, an Afghan national, gave his address to Inner London Crown Court as a hotel in Oxford which has been housing asylum seekers.

He admitted two counts of sexual assault and criminal damage, and was sentenced last week to a £400 fine with a £160 victim surcharge.

Salihi will also be put on the sex offenders register for the next five years.

Police said Salihi carried out the first sexual assault at around 3.30pm on January 28 last year when a woman was walking along the road in the rain, staying close to the buildings for shelter.

Salihi emerged at Mansion House and began to follow the woman, coming up close behind her until she turned and asked if he needed to get past.

Police said Salihi shook his head, then a few moments later slapped the woman’s bottom.



Later that same day, a 14-year-old girl was sightseeing with her family at Leadenhall Market which was used in the original Harry Potter film franchise as the location for Diagon Alley.

The girl had felt a touch on her bottom and turned to see Salihi with a “weird smirk on his face”.

The family went to the Rocca Italian restaurant and saw Salihi enter the same premises, sparking a confrontation where he was pushed towards the counter and accused of sexual assault.

The force said he initially refused to leave when asked by restaurant staff, and then “looked agitated” when he was sat outside.

“Salihi picked up a chair and threw it through a window”, said the police.



“He picked up a second and threw it, but this time it bounced against the glass.

“He was detained by members of the public until police arrived.”

Detective Constable Natalie Schofield, from City of London Police said: “These were deeply distressing sexual assaults committed in broad daylight against two females who were simply going about their daily lives.

“One of the victims was just 14-years-old, making this offending particularly concerning.

“I would like to thank both victims for the immense courage they showed in coming forward and supporting our investigation.

“We know how difficult it can be to report sexual offences, and their bravery has ensured this offender has been held accountable for his actions.”

Salihi pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual assault and criminal damage, and was sentenced on July 13.

News.title: Kremlin breaks silence on new PM Andy Burnham with dig over Ukraine war after Russian warship’s live fire drills near UK
News.content:
THE KREMLIN has broken its silence and slammed new PM Andy Burnham, accusing him of “doing everything possible to continue the war” in Ukraine.

It comes after a Russian warship carried out live-fire drills just 40 nautical miles off the coast of Britain yesterday.



The Russians staged the exercise on Burnham‘s first day in office.

Vladimir Putin said he had no intention of talking to the UK’s new leader any time soon.



And Mad Vlad’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov defended the actions of the Russian frigate that opened fire off the coast of Plymouth on Monday.

Warship Neustrashimy has been escorting Russian shadow fleet tankers through the English Channel.

The frigate was being shadowed by a Royal Navy vessel HMS Iron Duke and its activity is still being tracked “closely”.

A French military aircraft was also tracking the warship and asked it to clarify its intentions.



The Russian warship told the Royal Navy Offshore Patrol Vessel, HMS Tyne, that it intended to fire rounds and asked the vessel to move to a safe distance.

The gunnery activity lasted for 30 minutes in international waters.

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Defence said: “A Russian naval vessel shadowed by the Royal Navy conducted a live-fire weapons exercise in international waters approximately 40 nautical miles south of Plymouth yesterday.



“The Royal Navy monitored that exercise throughout, continues to track the vessel’s activity closely, and stands ready to protect UK national security.”

Kremlin spokesman Peskov claimed: “All actions by our warships are carried out in strict compliance with international law and the law of the sea.

“Therefore, there’s no need to read any hints here.

“However, of course, with the arrival of the new UK Prime Minister, one of his first actions was to declare unconditional support for Ukraine, and, accordingly, the UK’s intention to continue doing everything possible to continue the war.”

The PM and his newly-appointed defence secretary Wes Streeting will have to deal with the ongoing aggression from Russia as activity in UK waters increases.



Burnham spoke to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky on his first day as PM.

And the Ukrainian president made it clear the pair would meet in the “near future”.

He said: “I greatly appreciate that support for Ukraine and our people will continue to be strong.”

“Thank you, Andy. Thank you, Britain!”

It comes after British commandos dramatically stormed a Russian “shadow fleet” oil tanker in June, in a first-of-its-kind mission.



Also in June, a British yacht was shot at by a huge Russian warship 20 miles off the Isle of Wight in a terrifying Channel showdown.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And ealier this month a Russian spy plane swooped dangerously over Britain’s flagship aircraft carrier and dropped tracking buoys in nearby waters.

RAF fighter jets intercepted the Bear-F spy plane after it “repeatedly approached” the HMS Prince of Wales in a high seas showdown off Norway.

News.title: Eight injured after double-decker bus and lorry crash in city centre
News.content:
CRASH HORROR Eight injured after double-decker bus and lorry crash in city centre

EIGHT people have been rushed to hospital after a lorry and double-decker bus crashed into each other.

Emergency services quickly attended the scene on Westgate Road in Newcastle this morning after the horror incident occurred just after 10.15am.



Shocking pictures show the windscreen of the bus has been completely smashed in, as police urge drivers to stay away from the area.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: “Just after 10.15am today (Tuesday), we received a report of a two-vehicle collision on Westgate Road in Newcastle.



“It was reported a bus has collided with a lorry. Emergency services are currently on scene. Motorists are advised to find alternate routes.”

A North East Ambulance Service spokesperson added: “We dispatched four ambulance crews, one specialist paramedic and one clinical team leader to the incident.

“Eight patients were taken to RVI hospital for further treatment and a number of people were treated and discharged on scene.”

Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Service were also in attendance with three fire trucks.

A spokesperson said: “The incident was a road traffic collision involving a double-decker bus and a heavy goods vehicle.

“Our firefighters helped make both vehicles safe and no persons were reported to be trapped.



“Blue light colleagues from Northumbria Police and the North East Ambulance Service were also in attendance with paramedics treating a number of people for what are believed to be minor injuries. Crews left the scene at 10:40.”

A spokesperson for Stagecoach, the bus’ operator, said: “Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this incident.

“We are aware of a collision involving one of our buses on Westgate Road in Newcastle this morning, and our immediate priority is the welfare of our customers, our driver and everyone else involved.

“We are working closely with the emergency services and are assisting the police with their investigation.

“As this is an ongoing incident, it would not be appropriate to comment further at this stage.”

News.title: You can be FINED if your kid kicks their football over neighbour’s garden fence
News.content:
IF your kid kicks a ball over the neighbour’s garden fence, you could be landed with a hefty fine this summer.

Fines can also be issued if you attempt to get the ball back without your neighbour’s permission or cause any damage to their property.

The summer holidays have begun, and with the sun set to continue shining over the next six weeks, it’s likely many kids will be heading into the back garden for a kickabout.



But disputes over footballs flying into next-door’s lawn can be a point of contention between neighbours.



A number of laws could be broken in a dispute over a rogue ball landing in the grass, and fines issued on both sides of the fence.

The High Court has ruled that kid who repeatedly kick footballs over the garden fence and into neighbours’ gardens are breaking common law.

So what are the rules surrounding this issue, and what repercussions can be faced?



What if I go into my neighbour’s garden to get the ball back?

You do not have the right to enter your neighbour’s garden without their permission.

Heading over the fence without their knowledge to retrieve a ball is considered trespassing.

Instead, head to your neighbour’s front door and ask to get the ball back, or alternatively, ask them to throw it over the fence – although there is no legal obligation for them to do it immediately.

What happens if I cause damage to my neighbour’s property with a ball?

If you cause damage to a neighbour’s property, such as break a window or fence, you are liable to cover the cost of any damage.



If a child causes the breakage, it’s up to the parents to take the responsibility.

Neighbours should keep a log of dates, times and any specific damage that has occurred and record the damage through photos if you ever need to seek compensation in a small claims court.

Do I have to give the ball back?

If a football comes flying into your back garden, disrupting your day, you may feel obliged to keep the item to make sure it doesn’t happen again.

Technically, this is considered theft.

Under the Theft Act (1968), anyone who intends to permanently deprive the original owner of an item would be found guilty.



If your neighbours decided to pursue legal action, a fine is the most likely outcome for first time offenders.

However, if you were to damage, deflate or burst the ball, this would no longer be considered theft and instead could trigger criminal damage charges.

If legal proceedings occurred, you would be liable to pay for a new ball, and may even be fined by the courts if the issue escalated.

While a fine is frustrating, the bigger issue in this situation is the fact it could lead to a criminal record.

A theft conviction, even for something as inconsequential as a football, can show up on a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check for years, possibly impacting employment, travel visas and insurance premiums.



What can I do if I think my neighbours are kicking balls into my garden deliberately?

If you believe neighbours are launching balls over the fence with the intent to annoy or intimidate you, the situation escalates from a civil property dispute to a potential criminal matter under the Protection from Harassment Act (1997).

If the situation continues for a period of time and causes you distress, you can involve the local council’s anti-social behaviour (ASB) team or the police, although this should be logged by the non-emergency 101 line.

This situation occurred in 2025 when a couple were awarded damages after complaining that footballs from their neighbouring school were landing in their garden.

Children playing on an outdoor all-weather play area would continually kick balls into the Bakhaty’s garden, with Mrs Bakhaty noting that over 11 months, 170 balls had been kicked onto their lawn.

The couple sued the neighbouring school, and the case was taken to High Court.



The judge dismissed the couple’s request to grant an injunction to stop the use of the play area.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, he did rule that while the all-weather play area did not give rise to “actionable nuisance”, the “frequent projection of balls over the boundary” from the play area was a nuisance.

As a result, the judge ordered Hampshire County Council to pay the Bakhatys £1,000 in damages for a period of time when there was “excess use” of the all-weather play area and when “significant numbers of balls were crossing the boundary fence”.

News.title: Andrew Tate faces indecent child imagery and extreme porn charges after arrest on 32 new counts including rape
News.content:
TATE SHAME Andrew Tate faces indecent child imagery and extreme porn charges after arrest on 32 new counts including rape

ANDREW Tate has been accused of possessing indecent child imagery and extreme porn as part of 32 fresh charges laid against him.

The self-proclaimed misogynist and his brother Tristan were arrested in Miami over the weekend and now face extradition to the UK.



The Tate brothers were hit with 38 new charges in total before appearing at the Wilkie D. Ferguson Jr Courthouse on Monday wearing tan jail uniforms and handcuffs.

Andrew and Tristan, 39 and 38, shackled at the waist and ankles, spoke only when asked if they understood their rights, replying together: “Yes your honour.”



The brothers were detained in Florida on Saturday as they arrived at a bareknuckle boxing event.

Andrew faces 32 new charges, including seven relating to rape and 19 involving extreme pornography and indecent images of children.



Tristan, 38, faces six more, including two rape and sex-trafficking charges.

The brothers have been accused of choking women, sometimes until they fell unconscious, and then raping them.

According to unsealed documents, Andrew allegedly repeatedly choked one woman until she passed out and then raped her at her home in Bedford in 2015.

Another woman alleged Andrew visited her Manchester home before choking her to the point that “she was afraid Tate was going to kill her”.



The complaint also alleged that Tristan regularly choked, beat and raped a woman that he was in a romantic relationship in 2012 and 2013.

The alleged victim claimed he regularly choked her until she passed out, gave her a black eye and whipped her with a belt, causing welts and bruises.

US prosecutors are seeking to extradite them to the UK – with a district judge set to consider whether they meet the conditions over the coming weeks.



The Tates’ lawyer Joseph McBride confirmed that the brothers will fight the move.

Speaking outside court after the hearing on Monday, he said: “Today was about enforcing Andrew and Tristan Tate’s rights and objecting to the extradition process.

“We are of course objecting to extradition because Andrew and Tristan are innocent.”

He claimed his clients are the victims of a “political witch hunt” and are being “attacked for what they say, not what they’ve done”.

The lawyer also branded Britain “a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech” and suggested Donald Trump could intervene in the proceedings, saying “he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense”.



McBride said: “They’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they didn’t commit.

“It’s garbage. It’s a stitch-up job.”

He also said the extradition process would take “around 60 days”.



The brothers will remain in custody in Florida until their next court hearing on July 27.

Andrew and Tristan already faced 21 charges between them relating to three alleged victims, so will now be prosecuted for 59 allegations relating to seven women.

The brothers have previously denied any wrongdoing.

Mr McBride added: “We’ve never seen a scintilla of evidence that indicates that these guys are guilty of anything…You can love them, you can hate them, but nobody should go to jail for free speech, and that is exactly what this is about.

“Make no mistake about it, the United Kingdom was once the greatest empire the world has ever known. It is a fallen nation.



“It is a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech.”

He added: “That is not what democracies and free societies do. That is what communist China and despotic regimes do.

“And we’re going to fight them at every turn, at every corner, because they are American citizens.”

The Tates were born in the US before moving to Luton as children.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They are now based in Romania, where they were initially arrested in 2022.

News.title: Man, 50, found dead inside town centre home as schoolboy, 15, ‘detained’ over ‘murder’
News.content:
A MAN has been found dead inside a home as police launch a murder probe and detain a 15-year-old schoolboy.

Police scrambled to an address in Bolton, Greater Manchester, last month where they found the man, 50, with serious head and chest injuries.

Greater Manchester Police has now launched a murder investigation after he was pronounced dead at the scene on June 30.

The force said that the probe was launched following a post-mortem and the emergence of new information.





A 15-year-old boy has been detained under the Mental Health Act and is due to be questioned.

Officers believe that the incident is isolated and that there is no wider risk to the local community.

Detective Chief Inspector Louise Edwards of the Major Incident Team, said: “Our thoughts remain firmly with the man’s family and friends.

“Following new information coming to light regarding his death, we are now carrying out enquiries to establish the full circumstances surrounding the events of the day he died.



“We’d like to thank members of the community for their patience and understanding as we carry out enquiries in and around the Gray Street area.

“There is no information to suggest there is any wider risk to the public, and we are not seeking anyone else in relation to this incident.

“Anyone who has information that may assist police enquiries and who has not yet spoken to officers is asked to contact Greater Manchester Police on 101, quoting log 3965 of 30/05/26.

“Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously via the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Shocking moment older spectator slaps young sports fan for not standing up during US national anthem in viral video
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment an old man slaps a young sports fan for not standing during the United States national anthem.

In the viral video, the older spectator can be heard yelling “get up” to the younger man during the performance at a Chicago Cubs baseball game.



He then leans down to whisper something in the seated man’s ear, before hitting him aggressively on the back of the head.

Bemused spectators watch on as the young man stands up in shock.



The older spectator then says: “Thank you, thank you so much young man,” as the camera pans away to the field.

Online opinion has been divided over the shocking clip, which has amassed nearly 10 million views on X.



Some users said that the younger man should show some respect for his country, but others deemed the older spectator’s actions too much.

One joked: “Should have made him sing too just for trying to pull that”.

Another wrote: “More people should insist on respect from everyone around them for our country,” alongside an American flag emoji.

But the smack has also provoked outrage from others, who have said it was “evidence of a crime” being recorded.



One commenter wrote: “Old dude had absolutely no right to touch him. A real patriot would have not assaulted that guy.”

Others pointed to the First Amendment, which emphasised US citizens’ rights to freedom of speech and expression.

“It’s his right to sit,” one fumed.

“That’s what this country is about, freedom. He’s still a d–he but this ain’t a dictatorship, either.”

Legal experts noted that the man’s actions could constitute battery, but it appears that no further action has been taken thus far.



It comes a few weeks after the United States celebrated its 250th anniversary with a slew of patriotic events.

UFC fans were left emotional after a stunning performance of the American national anthem kicked off a historic night of fights at the White House on June 14.

The promotion staged UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn in Washington DC, with the event marking a huge celebration for the country.

President Donald Trump, who turned 80 at the event, was in attendance for the landmark card and stood alongside UFC boss Dana White before the action got underway.

And the night opened in spectacular fashion as the Zac Brown Band performed The Star-Spangled Banner.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump was seen saluting during the anthem as the crowd watched on during the patriotic scenes.

The performance was followed by a dramatic flyover while music blasted around the White House grounds.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: Prime Minister sets challenge to ministers as he chairs first Cabinet meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has welcomed his appointments round the Cabinet table at No 10 on a day where he hit the ground running by helping millions of UK families with the abolition of VAT on electricity bills

Andy Burnham is chairing his first Cabinet meeting and told his appointed ministers to examine “all possible ways” to help families struggling with high costs.

In a challenge to his top team one their applause had died down , the new Prime Minister said their task was to "take that little bit of pressure off people's shoulders" and show them help was coming so they could have some hope things were improving.

He told the meeting: "That’s the mission that we’ve got to set ourselves together” and asked his colleagues to look into what their department could do to ease cost-of-living pressures, “big and small,” saying: “We need to be a cost-of-living Government, getting that cost of living down, looking at all possible ways of doing that.”

Burnham started today by making good on his promise for “breathing space” for struggling households, a key plinth of his economic plans unveiled in his maiden speech outside No 10 on Monday. The move will see VAT removed from domestic electricity bills from October 1.

Burnham said: “Westminster has not been working for people for too long, with families struggling with the cost of living. That needs to change. I said I wanted to give people breathing space, and that’s what I’m announcing on my second day as Prime Minister. We’re taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people’s pockets and bring back hope.”

It is estimated that the change will reduce the annual Ofgem price cap by around £45 from October, with companies expected to pass the reduction onto customers.

Chancellor John Healey said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living. Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter". He continued: “This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”

The fully priced plan from Mr Healey comes as Burnham continues to pad out his cabinet, with a number of key appointments made since yesterday, including Ed Miliband receiving the FCDO brief, Angela Rayner returning as Housing Secretary, and Shabana Mahmood staying on as Home Secretary.

News.title: Met Office names 7 areas facing wet weather this week as 15mm of rain forecast
News.content:
Met Office names 7 areas facing wet weather this week as 15mm of rain forecast

Rain is expected to fall in some parts of the UK this week following a scorching spell of dry weather - and the Met Office says more showery conditions may come this weekend

UK weather: Met Office forecasts much needed rainfall

The Met Office says some much-needed rain is to come this week following a spell of scorching temperatures and dry weather.

‌



Last Friday, the national weather agency announced the UK had seen temperatures of 30C or more for 13 consecutive days. It was also revealed that central and south-east England had seen the longest unbroken spell of no recorded rainfall this century - with no rain recorded in either region from July 2 to July 15.

‌



Such dry spells can have disastrous impacts on farming while wildfires have also broken out in many parts of UK - but thankfully some regions should now see showers this week.

‌



View 4 Images Rain is expected in Scotland and Northern Ireland tomorrow (Image: Met Office)

UK weather maps show 41C heatwave and hottest day ever as 10 counties reach 40C READ MORE :

Europe weather maps show 50C heatwave as tourists in Spain face hottest day ever READ MORE :

Met Office forecast for today

In the Met Office’s latest Week Ahead forecast, meteorologist Clare Nasir says “patchy rain” is on the cards today in the “far north and north-west of Scotland”. There will also be “spits and spots” of rain in Northern Ireland.

The central belt of Scotland could hit 25C to 26C, as could South Wales, central England, and the south-east. Although not cold, these temperatures are a far-cry from what we experienced last week.

‌



Met Office forecast for Wednesday

For tomorrow, Ms Nasir says a weather front “will bring the prospect of a little showery rain” once more. The far north of Scotland is in the firing line again, with “10 or 15mm [possible] across the upslopes towards the north-west”.

Eastern parts of Wales as well as central and southern England are expected to be the warmest areas tomorrow, with highs of 25-27C possible across a huge swathe of the UK. Central Scotland could rise to 23C, with 21C coming in Northern Ireland.

View 4 Images Eastern coasts should see some showers on Thursday (Image: Met Office)

‌



Met Office forecast for Thursday

Conditions will be turning more humid for Thursday, with more rain to come too. Ms Nasir said: “Through Thursday there will be a few showery bursts around, coming down the east coast. And one or two showers could develop inland through the morning into the afternoon.”

The Met Office weather maps show rain falling in central England on Thursday. But, Ms Nasir added: “[Any showers] will be scattered and light.”

Thursday is expected to be bright with sunshine for most. Wales, central England and southern England should be warmest once more with 25-26C highs, as parts of Yorkshire reach 24C. Similar temperatures to Wednesday are expected in Scotland and Northern Ireland on Thursday.

‌



View 4 Images Central England could also see some much-needed rain (Image: Met Office)

Met Office forecast for Friday

As for Friday, Ms Nasir said: “We’ll see some showery bursts of rain that will extend across central and northern areas in Scotland. Elsewhere, a fine day with some sunny spells. No meaningful rain away from the north-west this week.”

Temperatures could reach 28C in and around London on Friday. South Wales, the Midlands and Yorkshire should hit 24-25C, with Northern Ireland and central Scotland hovering at around 21-22C.

‌



UK areas facing rain this week

Far north of Scotland

North-west of Scotland

North-east of Scotland

Central Scotland

Northern Ireland

Eastern coasts

Central England

View 4 Images More rain could come this weekend, the Met Office says (stock) (Image: PA)

Met Office forecast for the weekend - possibly more rain

More rain could be on the cards this coming weekend too. The Met Office says high pressure is expected to weaken as we head towards the end of the week, which will allow “weather fronts to become more active and push southwards”.

Article continues below

The national weather agency adds: “This will increase the likelihood of rainfall across central and northern parts of the UK, bringing some much-needed rain to areas that have remained exceptionally dry in recent weeks.”

News.title: Bus crashes into lorry in Newcastle as eight people rushed to hospital
News.content:

A collision between a bus and a lorry in Newcastle city centre has seen eight people rushed to hospital with injuries - a police cordon is currently in place

View 3 Images A bus has collided with a lorry in Newcastle (Image: Chronicle Live)

Eight people have been rushed to hospital after a bus crashed into a lorry in Newcastle city centre.

‌



Emergency services are dealing with the crash, which took place in Westgate Road with a police cordon and a road closure in place.

‌



Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said they were called at 10.17am and sent three crews from Byker Community Fire Station and Hebburn Tri Station to the scene. Northumbria Police urged motorists to find alternative routes due to the collision.

‌



A spokesperson for the force said: “Just after 10.15am today (Tuesday), we received a report of a two-vehicle collision on Westgate Road in Newcastle. It was reported a bus has collided with a lorry. Emergency services are currently on scene. Motorists are advised to find alternate routes.”

View 3 Images Police at the scene of the crash (Image: Chronicle Live)

Met Office verdict on August heatwave as weather maps show 37C scorcher READ MORE :

Iran-backed group declares another crucial strait closed as Middle East war widens READ MORE :

North East Ambulance Service confirmed that eight people were taken to hospital. "We were called to a road traffic incident on Westgate Road in Newcastle on Tuesday 21 July at 10:20am," said a spokesperson, reports ChronicleLive.

‌



"We dispatched four ambulance crews, one specialist paramedic and one clinical team leader to the incident. Eight patients were taken to RVI hospital for further treatment and a number of people were treated and discharged on scene."

A statement from the fire service read: "We can confirm that earlier this morning, three fire appliances attended an incident in Newcastle city centre. The emergency call was received by our Fire Control Team at 10:17 and three crews were dispatched from Byker Community Fire Station and Hebburn Tri Station to Westgate Road in Newcastle.

View 3 Images Eight people were taken to hospital after the crash (Image: Chronicle Live)

‌



“The incident was a road traffic collision involving a double-decker bus and a heavy goods vehicle. Our firefighters helped make both vehicles safe and no persons were reported to be trapped.

“Blue light colleagues from Northumbria Police and the North East Ambulance Service were also in attendance with paramedics treating a number of people for what are believed to be minor injuries. Crews left the scene at 10:40.”

A Stagecoach spokesperson said the company is assisting police in the investigation.

Article continues below

"Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this incident. We are aware of a collision involving one of our buses on Westgate Road in Newcastle this morning, and our immediate priority is the welfare of our customers, our driver and everyone else involved," they said.

"We are working closely with the emergency services and are assisting the police with their investigation. As this is an ongoing incident, it would not be appropriate to comment further at this stage."

News.title: Football journalist shot dead and set on fire in horrific execution in Italy
News.content:
Football journalist shot dead and set on fire in horrific execution in Italy

The burnt remains of football journalist Luigi 'Luca' Esposito were discovered in a remote field in Salerno, Italy, with the 53-year-old also found to have been shot

View 3 Images Luigi 'Luca' Esposito, 53, was found dead by firefighters (Image: Jam Press)

A football journalist has been shot dead and set on fire in an execution that has rocked the sports world.

‌



Friends of Luigi 'Luca' Esposito had grown worried after losing contact with the 53-year-old on Saturday night.

‌



Firefighters were then called to the scene of a blaze at a remote field in Salerno, Italy, where they discovered his charred remains in the early hours of Sunday, July 19.

‌



Prosecutors in Salerno, led by anti-mafia chief Raffaele Cantone, are treating the case as a murder. Officers had recovered bullet casings near Luigi's body at Bivio Cioffi in Salerno and were able to help identify him as his car was discovered nearby.

View 3 Images Luigi was found dead during the early hours of Sunday (Image: Jam Press)

An autopsy is due to confirm the exact cause of death.

‌



Investigators are looking closely at Luigi's private life for possible motives, including financial or passionate disputes. Police are yet to rule out any theories.

The victim, originally from Nocera Inferiore and a passionate Salernitana 1919 fan, ran the website TuttoSalernitana.com.

He also worked as a columnist for La Città di Salerno and as a regular pundit on OttoChannel TV, covering Serie B sides including Avellino and Juve Stabia.

‌



Colleagues said he was outspoken, fearless and full of contacts in the football world.

View 3 Images The 53-year-old's death is being treated as a murder (Image: Jam Press)

OttoChannel director Pierluigi Melillo said: "Luca was a precious collaborator – awkward but never banal, always brave in defending his opinions on football. He was due to be one of our star pundits next season."

‌



Melillo added the team was "shocked and incredulous" at the "horrible execution".

Luigi, who had 15,500 Instagram followers, had two degrees in biology and literature.

His sister said he was a calm man with no known enemies.

Article continues below

Police have not yet made any arrests and an investigation into Luigi's death is ongoing.

News.title: Eight in 10 Brits avoid last-minute plans – as pressure to be 'perfect' to blame
News.content:
Eight in 10 Brits avoid last-minute plans – as pressure to be 'perfect' to blame

New research shows eight in 10 Brits avoid being spontaneous because they worry about having everything perfect, which includes a clean and tidy house.

View 2 Images Nearly half don't want to feel rushed to make plans (Image: Getty Images)

Eight out of 10 Brits shy away from being spontaneous. A survey of 2,000 adults reveals that people want at least a week's notice before making plans. Nearly half (45%) don't want to feel rushed, while others prefer to remain in control of the situation, or simply lack the motivation.

‌



Two thirds (63%) admitted they prefer to plan ahead rather than act on impulse, but for 17% the pressure of getting everything "perfect" is a key reason they put off making last-minute plans altogether. Women are more likely than men to make excuses to wriggle out of last-minute plans, with 42% and 32% respectively.

‌



It emerges that 29% of adults won't invite people round at short notice due to concerns about their home being untidy, and 23% have gone as far as pretending not to be in rather than answer the door.

‌



Despite this, 23% would like to be more spontaneous, and 21% believe it would make life more enjoyable.

View 2 Images Many people have concerns about their home being untidy (Image: Getty Images)

The research was commissioned by Hotpoint as part of its "Just Come Over" Season encouraging the nation to say yes to spontaneity again this summer.

‌



Dr Angharad Rudkin, a clinical psychologist who worked with the appliances brand, said: "What's exciting about the research is what it reveals about appetite, not just avoidance – people actively want to be more spontaneous, and most already sense it would make us happier.

"The barrier isn't desire, it's small, fixable habits: feeling rushed, or believing that a home needs to be 'ready' before anyone's invited round.

"I'd encourage letting go of those habits - and it doesn't take much, saying yes to a last-minute invite, or accepting that your home doesn't need to be perfect, can genuinely shift how connected and fulfilled life feels."

‌



The research revealed that more than a quarter of women (28%) felt that having a tidy home would make them feel more spontaneous, compared to just 19% of men.

Meanwhile, 26% of women said having food and drinks prepared would make them more likely to welcome last-minute guests, a sentiment shared by only 19% of men.

Article continues below

Women were also more inclined to feel spontaneous when their household was running smoothly (23%), versus 18% of men.

Kimberley Garner, from Hotpoint, said: "We've seen 115 years' worth of spontaneous hosting, and this research shows just how much pressure people put on themselves before they'll open their front door.

"Just Come Over Season is about giving the nation the confidence to say yes at short notice – because some of the best get-togethers are the ones nobody planned."

News.title: Best morning routine revealed – but one debate still divides the nation
News.content:
Best morning routine revealed – but one debate still divides the nation

The debate over the best morning routine has finally been put to bed – but there’s still one area where Brits are split down the middle

The Great Wake-Up Debate

Eight in 10 Britons stick rigidly to a set morning routine – but there’s still one everyday question the nation can’t agree on. A poll of 2,000 adults found 83% follow a regular regime to start the day, although the details vary widely from person to person.

‌



More than four in 10 (42%) prefer to shower in the morning, compared with 23% who opt for a night-time rinse – while the rest either have no preference or do both.

‌



It also emerged 34% get up as soon as their first alarm goes off, but 26% admit they hit snooze once or twice before finally rising.

‌



When it comes to morning 'fuel' coffee is the top choice (36%), edging out tea (32%). And nearly half (47%) check their phone within five minutes of waking up, with just 3% managing to avoid looking at their device altogether.

View 2 Images Rob Beckett unpacks the morning habits people refuse to compromise on (Image: HolidayInn)

But one debate remains unresolved: brushing teeth before or after breakfast. The poll found the country is split down the middle, with 45% doing it before eating and the same number (45%) after – while 10% don’t have a set preference.

‌



Holiday Inn Express by IHG Hotels & Resorts commissioned the study and partnered with comedian Rob Beckett, who launched The Great Wake-up Debate – encouraging people to voice their opinion on the proper way to begin the day.

Rob Beckett said: "People will argue about absolutely anything, but morning routines are right up there with the best of them.

"You've got the annoyingly cheerful lot who are up, showered and chatting away before 7am - and then the rest of us, who need a bit of peace before we're feeling properly human.

‌



"What surprised me most is how seriously people take it - tea or coffee can divide a room faster than you can make either."

View 2 Images From what they eat for breakfast to how they get out of bed, Brits have their morning routines set in stone (Image: HolidayInn)

The survey also pointed to the importance of bedtime habits, with almost two thirds (65%) saying how they sleep affects how they feel the next morning. And 49% said they struggle to drift off unless they’re on their preferred side of the bed.

‌



Peace and quiet, a cool room and a duvet topped the list of bedtime essentials. Nearly half (45%) sleep with just one pillow, while 43% prefer a more elaborate three-pillow set-up.

Rob added: “For me, it all comes down to a good night’s sleep and a good brekkie to start the day. I’m a two-soft-pillows kind of guy and, while I’m usually up with the first alarm at home, I’m firmly ‘team lie-in’ when I’m away.

“Even better when there’s free breakfast waiting, like at Holiday Inn Express — you'll find me parked by the bacon and eggs!”

‌



Almost a third (32%) of those polled, via OnePoll.com, said breakfast is the best part of a hotel stay. Meanwhile, 20% said they would book a hotel room without a second thought if they knew there was a comfy bed waiting.

John Wright, VP Mainstream Brands at IHG Hotels & Resorts, said: “The Great Wake Up Debate proves that everyone has their own morning habits and rituals. But what unites us is wanting to start the day feeling our best.

“That’s why we focus on the essentials that matter most to our guests – comfortable beds with a choice of pillows, blackout curtains, bedside charging and our free hot breakfast.

Article continues below

“It’s all about making mornings feel a little easier and helping guests wake up refreshed, recharged and ready for whatever the day brings.”

News.title: Chris Mason: Starmer ally takes swipe at Burnham's first big policy
News.content:
Whenever there is a reshuffle at the top of government, it is worth keeping an eye and an ear on the dislodged, demoted and rejected former ministers. What do they choose to do and say next?

Andy Burnham has started his first full day in the job with a promise to cut VAT from household electricity bills from 1 October.

But already â within hours - he is taking flak from a man who just yesterday was in a senior job in Downing Street working alongside Sir Keir Starmer.

On Monday night, the former Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, Darren Jones, posted a picture on X of him having a beer, external, captioned "thank you and good night. See you September".

If that was meant to suggest a vow of silence it only lasted a little over 12 hours, because at breakfast time this morning came another post, this one unaccompanied by any picture but loaded with political bite.

"Good news that VAT will be cut on electricity bills," wrote Jones.

"It's a simple way for families to save a few quid, and to mechanically help to keep inflation that little bit lower. But the DigitalID program was unfunded. The government will have to set out how it will pay for its new policies at the budget."

Ouch - that will sting in Downing Street.

News.title: London-based civil servants offered move to No 10 North in Manchester
News.content:
Civil servants working for government departments based in London have been offered relocation packages to encourage them to move to the North of England, the BBC understands.

It comes as the first details are emerging about the new No 10 North which has already started work, according to sources close to new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The BBC has been told that the Northern branch of Downing Street will be overseen by cabinet minister and ally of Burnham, Louise Haigh.

Haigh, who is the first secretary of state, is thought to have been asked to lead a new Office for the Prime Minister, which will give her control of key decision- making bodies across government.

Announcing the changes,, external which will also include an AI Taskforce, Leader of the House of Lords, Baroness Angela Smith said No 10 North would be a "dominant driver of the UK's economy".

It is understood that the initial location of No 10 North will be Heron House in central Manchester, in the same building which houses offices for the intelligence service GCHQ. Specialist police officers have been seen guarding the building.

It is likely that the longer term base for No 10 North will be at a new government "Digital Campus" which is under construction in the Ancoats area of Manchester. It is not due for completion until 2032.

However, a good indication of what it could look like comes from a new report, released on Tuesday.

The blueprint has been authored, external by the Re:State think tank which Burnham was involved with until he stepped down as mayor of Greater Manchester.

News.title: Cause of Ann Widdecombe's death not yet established, inquest hears
News.content:
The cause of Ann Widdecombe's death is yet to be established, the opening of an inquest into her death has heard.

The 78-year-old former MP and MEP was found dead at her home in Devon on 9 July with "visible injuries" Exeter Corner's Court heard.

Senior coroner Philip Spinney said a post-mortem examination had taken place and "at this stage the precise medical cause of death has yet to be established".

Joshua Kerry, 28, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, has arrived at Westminister Magistrates' Court where he is due to appear charged with her murder.

Spinney, senior coroner for Devon, Plymouth and Torbay, said the inquest was now adjourned "until the conclusion of the criminal proceedings".

Widdecombe was found unresponsive in her home by an employee who carried out a welfare check due to her being "uncontactable", the hearing heard.

Emergency services were called, but she was pronounced dead at 12:20 BST on Thursday, 9 July.

Kerry was first arrested on suspicion of murder two days after former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, Widdecombe, 78, was found with serious injuries at her home in Haytor, Devon.

He was later re-arrested on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

The investigation, which remains ongoing, has been led by Counter Terrorism Policing South East, supported by Devon and Cornwall Police.

News.title: Parts of the UK move closer to drought
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995. England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

England has received only 3% of its long-term average July rainfall with the south and east of England seeing no rain at all. Wisley in Surrey has seen 33 consecutive dry days.

Rainfall so far this summer has been below average across the UK as a whole, but there has been large regional contrast.

Up to the middle of summer - 15 July - parts of eastern and north-eastern England had received just 26% of their total expected summer rainfall. Areas of northern and western Scotland had more than average for the first half of the summer, though.

In Wales, where just 5% of July rainfall has fallen, Natural Resources Wales has moved the worst affected regions in the north and south-east into "prolonged dry weather status", the first step in its drought plan.

Comparisons are being made with last summer, when drought was declared across much of England, Wales and eastern Scotland. It officially ended just four months ago.

This year, drought has not developed as quickly because heavy rainfall recharged our aquifers, rivers and reservoirs during a very wet autumn and winter.

However, the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology says flash droughts, external with a sudden transition between wet and dry conditions are "likely to happen more often, and be more intense".

As the effects of human-induced climate change continue, the Met Office expects our summers to become hotter and drier, external in the future. In fact, by 2070, our summers could be up to 60% drier and 1-6C warmer compared to 1990.

News.title: Thames Water announces hosepipe ban for 10.1 million
News.content:
Thames Water has announced a hosepipe ban affecting 10.1 million customers after an "exceptionally warm and dry spring".

The restrictions mean, from Thursday, hosepipes should not be used for watering gardens or allotments, cleaning cars, filling paddling pools or swimming pools, or cleaning windows.

The water company said its region had seen 40% of average rainfall, and more days at or above 34C this year than ever recorded before.

Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources, said: "We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment."

The ban applies to all customers that Thames Water supplies with drinking water and comes into effect on Thursday.

The company provides water to customers across parts of Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Surrey, the Thames Valley, Greater London, and the surrounding areas, external.

It provides water and wastewater services to 16 million customers overall.

It said water use was currently 10% above normal in the Thames Valley and Home Counties and 7% above normal in London, which amounted to an extra 100 million litres of water every day.

News.title: Watch: 'My flat was turned into a brothel,' landlord tells BBC Panorama
News.content:
A BBC Panorama investigation has uncovered how organised crime gangs are exploiting the UK's private rental market - targeting properties to take over and use for their operations.

Among those featured in a new documentary is landlord and property developer Craig Shepheard, who discovered his flat was being used by a prostitution ring, run by a network in Brazil.

BBC Panorama reporter Hazel Martin also found that criminals are using fake IDs to get rental agreements.

News.title: Fifa opens investigation into Argentina post-final trouble
News.content:
Argentina will face an investigation into the ugly scenes at the end of the World Cup final, Fifa has confirmed.

Fifa's disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess what happened after the final whistle at MetLife stadium.

Any player or coach involved in the fracas could face suspension, while the Argentine Football Association (AFA) may also be fined.

Following their 1-0 defeat on Sunday, members of the Argentina team and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain players as they began to celebrate their World Cup success.

Nahuel Molina, Leandro Paredes, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala all appeared to be involved.

It was incorrectly reported on Fifa's commentator information system that Paredes had been sent off by referee Slavko Vincic for pushing Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat.

Paredes' red card was deleted shortly afterwards and Fifa has confirmed to BBC Sport that no disciplinary action was taken at the time.

Argentina had already had one player dismissed, with Enzo Fernandez receiving a second yellow card in second-half stoppage time.

Fifa had already begun the process of potential disciplinary action against Argentina after their players held a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands following the 2-1 semi-final win against England.

News.title: Boy who inspired organ donation law in NI gets new heart after 8-year wait
News.content:
A nine-year-old boy who inspired changes to Northern Ireland's organ donation laws has received a heart transplant after an eight-year wait.

DÃ¡ithÃ­ Mac Gabhann's father had said he is so grateful that his son "has a new beautiful heart beating inside him" and that he has made "amazing progress over the last few days" since his operation.

DÃ¡ithÃ­ was born in 2016 with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, meaning the left side of his heart did not form correctly.

His family said they said they were "beyond grateful to DÃ¡ithÃ­'s donor and their family for making such a selfless decision at the most difficult time imaginable".

News.title: UK borrows less than expected in June but public finances remain a challenge
News.content:
The government borrowed slightly less than expected in June, according to figures published as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham began setting out measures to cut living costs for households.

Borrowing - the difference between spending and income from taxes - was Â£16bn, about Â£7.9bn lower than a year earlier, although analysts said challenges remained over the UK's public finances.

Other data showed the unemployment rate was unchanged, with the Office for National Statistics (ONS) saying the labour market was "relatively steady".

However, while the borrowing figure was less than forecast, the ONS said total debt was high by historical standards and close to the annual value of the UK economy.

Borrowing for June was slightly below the Â£16.3bn that had been predicted by the government's official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR).

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said June's figure was "a rare piece of good news" for the new prime minister and his new Chancellor, John Healey.

However, she added: "Overall, there's no escaping the fact that the public finances are fragile and that there is limited scope for extra borrowing."

So far in the current financial year, borrowing has reached a total of Â£57.6bn, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). While this is down Â£3.7bn from the same period last year, it is Â£2.7bn above the OBR's forecast.

James Smith, chief UK economist at ING, told the BBC's Today programme the fact that borrowing was still running ahead of the OBR's projections was "a reminder of the challenges that the new chancellor and the new prime minister face".

He added they would face a "difficult picture" at the autumn Budget, with "lots of tough choices to be made".

Burnham and Healey have both pledged to stick to former chancellor Rachel Reeves' fiscal rules on spending and borrowing, although the new prime minister said on Monday he would use "any flexibility within them" to help with policy changes.

Shortly after Burnham's comments were made public, the yield on 10-year government bonds - effectively the interest rate charged to the UK government for a 10-year loan - rose above 5%.

The yield hit 5.03% late on Monday afternoon. However, when trading began on Tuesday the rate slipped back slightly to 5.01%.

In a statement released on Monday, Healey said "fiscal credibility is the bedrock for economic stability and for national security".

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said Labour had "maxed out the nation's credit card and sent borrowing soaring".

"If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control," he said.

The new leadership's first major policy announcement was to cut VAT on household electricity bills from 5% to zero from the beginning of October.

Ministers said it would be funded by savings from the cancellation of the digital ID programme, but Labour's Darren Jones, who was sacked as chief secretary to the prime minister on Monday, accused the government of announcing an unfunded tax cut.

News.title: Does Scotland have the 'game changer' helicopters it needs to fight wildfires?
News.content:
A devastating wildfire burning in the Cairngorms has entered its seventh day, as helicopters battle to stop the spread of the flames.

Two specialist helicopters have been "invaluable" for waterbombing hard-to-reach areas, the Cairngorms National Park Authority says.

But the flames were allowed to torch the landscape for nearly two days before they arrived on the scene around Glenmore Forest Park.

There's been vocal frustration from some local people, who believe the wildfire might have been brought under control if specialist air support had been called in sooner.

Why the delay? Do Scotland's firefighters have the aerial resources they need to tackle the growing threat of wildfires?

News.title: Teenagers jailed for murdering 16-year-old in beach knife attack
News.content:
Three teenagers have been jailed for murdering a 16-year-old boy during a confrontation between rival groups on a beach in North Ayrshire last year.

They were convicted of stabbing apprentice painter and decorator Kayden Moy on Irvine Beach on 17 May 2025.

Cole Turley, 18, who had pleaded guilty to the murder, and Jay Stewart, 19 were given life sentences and told they will serve a minimum of 16 years.

A third teenager - a 15-year-old who cannot be named for legal reasons - will be detained for a minimum of 14 years.

Speaking outside the High Court in Glasgow, Moy's father said his family's grief meant they were themselves enduring a life sentence.

Paul Moy said: "While today's outcome brings a measure of justice, it does not bring peace, it does not bring our son back.

"Kayden was more than a name in the courtroom or a headline in the news, he was our son, he was loved beyond words and had his whole life ahead of him.

"We hope today's sentence sends a clear message that violence has a devastating and irreversible consequences.

"One moment of violence has destroyed so many lives and no family should ever have to endure the pain that we now live with every day."

News.title: Owners of viral TikTok blue lagoon warn people to stay away
News.content:
Owners of a "blue lagoon" that went viral on TikTok during the Covid pandemic have warned people not to enter the site, particularly during the current hot weather.

Brombil Reservoir in Margam in Neath Port Talbot attracted thousands of visitors, which caused traffic problems and littering.

To reach the 30m-deep (100ft) reservoir, visitors must walk up a steep 900m (2,953ft) public footpath.

Leisure Estate Investments Ltd, which bought the secluded site at auction for Â£20,000 in 2024, are now charging Â£2 a visit as "a temporary deterrent" and have installed barriers on its dam face.

It is concerned about people swimming, paddleboarding, littering and damaging structures around the site.

Although the reservoir can be accessed via public footpaths, the barriers were installed to stop people from walking on the dam face - but these have since been removed by trespassers.

The owners said the Â£2 levy was introduced in an effort to manage unauthorised visits and help fund clean-up operations, as part of its efforts to discourage public access because of "inherent safety risks".

A spokesperson for the company said: "We have strictly banned [people] from going there and walking on the face of the dam.

"Our long-term vision has always been to build a sustainable public-private framework so the community can safely enjoy this asset.

"However, managing a critical piece of infrastructure presents immense structural, environmental, and financial challenges that cannot be indefinitely sustained by a private entity alone."

News.title: Monkey abandoned in laundry bag on London bus
News.content:
A marmoset monkey has been rescued by animal welfare officers after being found abandoned inside a laundry bag on a bus in north-west London.

The female primate was discovered by a driver on the route 302 bus when it arrived at Kensal Rise on Friday morning, the RSPCA said.

A passenger with a buggy had been unable to move down the bus because the bag was blocking the luggage bay. When the driver moved it, the monkey began chirping and jumping inside.

A spokesperson for the charity said the marmoset was trapped inside a small, metal bird cage wrapped in a chequered plastic bag. She was left with a piece of apple but was stressed and dehydrated.

News.title: Thames Water lenders offer 'golden share' to head off nationalisation
News.content:
Thames Water's main lenders are offering the government a "golden share" and more control for local authorities in a bid to stop the troubled supplier from being nationalised.

The government recently rejected a previous rescue proposal, and the BBC understands the lenders are preparing a legal challenge in case the new Andy Burnham-led government takes the firm into public hands.

The "golden share" would give the government veto powers over major decisions such as mergers.

The lenders are also proposing giving local authorities greater involvement in the firm, similar to the relationship between United Utilities and Greater Manchester agreed when Burnham was the city's mayor.

In his first speech as prime minister on Monday, Burnham said he wanted to see greater public control of "life's essentials".

Sources close to the creditors have told the BBC that in the event of full nationalisation they would pursue payment in full of the outstanding debts, as has happened in previous cases, which could leave the government with a multi-billion-pound bill.

The London & Valley Water (L&VW ) consortium of lenders had already proposed a Â£10bn deal to prevent Thames Water from entering administration. It would involve writing off nearly half of its debt and injecting new cash in return for leniency on future pollution fines.

The deal was rejected by the government in June, with then-environment secretary Emma Reynolds saying it did not do enough for consumers or the environment.

Sources close to the new deal said the creditors had sweetened it with hundreds of millions in new money on top of the existing offer.

A golden share would give the government veto power over major decisions such as mergers and acquisitions. Golden shares are seen as a way for the government to retain a stake in companies of national significance or importance, such as Royal Mail or Rolls Royce.

Any new proposals would have to be reviewed by Ofwat, the regulator.

A government spokesperson said Thames Water "remains financially stable, but we stand ready for all eventualities, including applying for a Special Administration Regime [SAR] if that were to become necessary".

"The government will always act in the national interest on these issues," they added.

An SAR is a form of temporary nationalisation which would allow the government to recoup some taxpayer cash if Thames was sold again to a private buyer.

L&VW said on Tuesday that the new offer had "material improvements" on the old one, and would benefit customers.

A spokesperson said: "We continue to believe that the L&VW plan is by far the fastest and most reliable route to solving Thames Water's complex problems and improving outcomes for customers and the environment."

They said the new deal "achieves this without any government funding or cost to taxpayers".

Fears first emerged three years ago that Thames Water could collapse and it has recently warned it could run out of cash by November.

If the company does go bust, households will still have drinking water and sewerage services.

Thames Water announced a hosepipe ban for all of its customers on Tuesday morning, citing the UK's "exceptionally warm and dry spring".

The company, which supplies water and wastewater services for 16 million people across London and parts of southern England, was handed a Â£122.7m fine last year, the biggest ever issued by the industry regulator Ofwat, for breaching rules on sewage spills and shareholder payouts.

Sources close to the creditors have previously told the BBC that in the event of full nationalisation, they would pursue payment in full of the outstanding debts as has happened in previous cases, which could leave the government with a multi-billion-pound bill.

News.title: Tributes to Kevin Keegan 'will never be enough'
News.content:
Fans around Newcastle have paid tribute to Kevin Keegan after news broke of the former footballer's death at age 75.

Although not from the city, Geordies claim Keegan as one of their own thanks to the influential stints he had as both player and manager.

Even Sunderland fan, Eddie, whose wife Brenda supports Newcastle, said: "He's a legend isn't he? Red and white, black and white it doesn't matter."

Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe said Keegan had been an "inspiration" and "a friend whose guidance and support meant a great deal in recent years".

"He was always willing to share his wisdom, offer encouragement and provide support, and I will always be grateful for that," he said.

"Every conversation with Kevin left you feeling better. He had remarkable warmth and humour and also a love for football that touched everyone around him."

Flowers have been laid at St James' Park as supporters flock to the ground to pay their respects.

Former Newcastle player and boyhood fan Shola Ameobi was also seen paying his respects at the stadium on Tuesday.

News.title: Northern Ireland's deputy first minster was 'floored' by news of Donaldson arrest
News.content:
Northern Ireland's deputy first minster says she was "completely floored" when she first heard of the arrest and charges of former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Jeffrey Donaldson over historical sex abuse.

In June, he was convicted of 18 counts of sex abuse, including one count of rape, which he committed against two women when they were children.

Emma Little-Pengelly said that people who worked alongside Donaldson over the past 20 years are "floored, shocked and utterly repulsed".

On Friday, it emerged Donaldson is to appeal his conviction.

After the former DUP leader was found guilty, a BBC Spotlight investigation reported on the double life of Donaldson.

The programme heard from former senior police officers and politicians who spoke about behaviour they described as hypocritical and which put Donaldson in danger of being compromised by his political opponents.

Speaking to the BBC's Red Lines podcast, Little-Pengelly said those reports should not take away from the scale of the crimes that he has been found guilty of.

"He's been convicted of being a paedophile and a rapist, and yes, there's all of these other allegations, but they absolutely pale into insignificance of that," she said.

"The focus should always be on the fact that he's been convicted of being a rapist and a paedophile, and that the victims of that have gone through a terrible ordeal to get justice."

Ukraine’s commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi is expected to lose his job as Volodymyr Zelensky looks set to stave off widespread protests.

In the past week, demonstrators have gathered outside the Ukrainian president’s office in Kyiv demanding Syrskyi’s sacking and the reinstatement of popular former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was fired after a clash with senior military leaders.

Fedorov, who is credited with improving Ukraine’s army since he took office in January, was said to have had significant differences with the commander-in-chief.

But Syrskyi on Monday publicly denied the differences were irreconcilable and said their relationship was a professional one, despite the disagreements.

open image in gallery Syrksyi has been in the role since February 2024 ( AP )

He wrote in Ukrainian military news outlet Militarnyi: “It is hard work, not the public drama surrounding it, that wins the war.

"Ukraine is greater than Fedorov, Syrskyi, or any one of us. Reducing this war to a confrontation between two individuals is the greatest favour we could do for the enemy."

He added that he was “sorry” if he had offended Fedorov, adding: “I can be harsh. But I ask you, and everyone who is following this story with enthusiasm: let’s focus not on the personal, but on the global. On victory.”

Zelensky is considering replacing Syrskyi with Joint Forces chief Mykhailo Drapatyi, but he is only one of a list of 11 potential candidates, two unnamed sources told Bloomberg.

open image in gallery People observe a minute of silence during a protest demanding the reinstatement of Mykhailo Fedorov as defence minister and calling for the resignation of Commander in Chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces Oleksandr Syrskyi ( Reuters )

He confirmed last week, during a press conference with Sir Keir Starmer, that there was a rift between the defence ministry and senior military figures. “I would like unity very much. The parties did not find it. And this is not only the problem of the parties, but also mine,” the Ukrainian president added.

Ukraine’s general staff on Monday denied the reports that Syrskyi was about to be sacked, stating that the commander and his deputy, Andriy Hinatov, were carrying out their duties, and that dismissal would take place “on the basis of a decree by the president of Ukraine”.

Syrskyi has served as commander-in-chief since February 2024, after General Valerii Zaluzhnyi was removed by Zelensky during a time of increasing tension between the pair - although his dismissal was officially on ‘health grounds’.

open image in gallery Fedorov was credited with Ukraine’s improved frontline positions ( Reuters )

Fedorov, meanwhile, was the last remaining minister to have held positions in all of Zelensky’s governments.

A tech-savvy reformer who has remained close to the president since his election in 2019, parliament is now set to vote on his replacement by Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko. It is unclear as to whether Fedorov will be given another government job.

His supporters pointed to his role in turning battlefield momentum in Ukraine's favour this year, through ramping up drone purchases and a crucial intervention to cut Russian units off from Starlink internet services.

But his attempts to overhaul the sprawling defence ministry and armed forces reportedly created tensions with Syrskyi - and he has failed to tackle longtime problems around military conscription.

Providing catering at the Fifa World Cup matches in the US has boosted business for Compass Group, the outsourcing giant revealed.

The business, which is the world’s biggest catering group, also said it was cashing in on the AI boom by providing food and services to data centres.

In an update to investors, Compass said it benefited from more work in North America, which co-hosted the men’s football tournament across 16 host cities and stadiums.

Compass provided hospitality and catering at four stadiums in the US: Atlanta, Kansas City, San Francisco Bay Area, and Seattle; which between them hosted 27 matches in the World Cup.

All of the stadiums have capacities of up to about 70,000 people.

The company also catered five of the official fan festivals, including the final watch party in New York’s Central Park.

open image in gallery Compass catered to four stadiums hosting matches at the Fifa World Cup (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Meanwhile, Compass revealed that it was cashing in on supporting “leading AI hyperscalers across the data centre ecosystem”.

This was through services like food, and facilities management and cleaning, for both the building and running of data centres.

The company said it had generated more than 2.0 billion US dollars (£1.5 billion) worth of new work to businesses across different industries.

Compass, which has about 590,000 staff, caters to some of the biggest US tech companies including Microsoft, Google and Amazon.

It has previously said more businesses were opting to outsource food services in the face of complex regulation and the risk of allergies.

This has lead to around half of new contract wins in the past year coming from clients outsourcing catering for the first time.

Compass said its sales grew by 7.1% in the three months to the end of June, compared with the same period a year ago.

Chief executive Dominic Blakemore said: “We are winning market share across multiple sectors, supported by the strongest pipeline of opportunities we have ever seen.”

Madeleine McCann’s younger brother Sean has been selected to represent Scotland at the upcoming Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Sean McCann was just two years old when his sister disappeared shortly before her fourth birthday during a holiday in Praia da Luz, Portugal in 2007.

The promising 21-year-old swimmer is expected to compete in a number of longer-distance freestyle swimming events at the Games, which start on Thursday.

And ambitious McCann hopes the Games, with swimming taking place at Tollcross International Centre, will propel him into contention for a place in the Great Britain team for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

A Loughborough University student, Sean McCann previously represented Scotland at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Tobago in 2023, where he finished fifth in the 400m freestyle event. His twin sister Amelia is also a high-level swimmer and triathlete.

Speaking on the Joe Humphries Memorial Trust website, McCann said: “I started competitive sport when I was eight, joining Charnwood triathlon club.

“It was here that I discovered my passion for swimming and I joined Loughborough Town swimming club to increase the number of swim sessions I did per week.

“At the age of 10, I was selected to swim at City of Leicester and I have since gone on to win multiple county titles as well as becoming regional and national champion in my age group.

“In order to have achieved this, I have had to remain extremely dedicated, getting up at 4am multiple mornings each week to train, since the age of 11.

“I train nine times a week in the pool, as well as three gym sessions, totalling over 20 hours of training per week. I’m aiming to compete at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and also the 2028 Olympics in LA.”

New prime minister Andy Burnham faces several immediate challenges to turn around national fortunes – with the future of Thames Water a particularly key decision after he previously suggested it could be nationalised.

Those behind the firm had proposed to write off half of its debts in exchange for leniency from future pollution fines, among other factors, but the offer has been rejected previously by the government, who informed regulator Ofwat it was not good for consumers or the environment.

Nationalising the company would put control in the hands of the public – or the government, more specifically – but would also likely leave the current lenders to seek the full amount of debt to be repaid, which would cost the nation billions.

Mr Burnham could still argue for greater public control of the debt-laden entity, which owes nearly £20bn and which said last week it only has enough cash to last until the end of 2026, meaning it will need a £2bn cash injection for another year.

Alternatively a sale, temporary administration or any other number of routes could still be on the table.

Will Thames Water be taken into public ownership?

The owners of Thames Water are not likely to allow nationalisation to happen easily.

Already reports suggest they are preparing legal challenges and creditors of Thames Water say they are working with both regulators and the government to ensure a positive outcome.

Existing investors are reported to have floated the idea of part-nationalisation and a so-called golden share for ministers, according to the Telegraph.

That would give them an option to veto key decisions and potentially have an equity stake in the business, to share in profits.

What happens to my bills?

For customers, the immediate message is that the taps will stay on.

Under pressure: Thames Water is being privatised ( Getty Images )

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Capital at risk. Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Capital at risk. Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

If Thames Water enters special administration or is effectively nationalised, households and businesses will continue to receive water and wastewater services as normal. The government has repeatedly stressed that supplies will not be interrupted.

Bills will still need to be paid. Water companies continue to operate while in special administration, with revenue used to fund day-to-day operations and investment in the network.

Whether bills rise in future is a separate question. Ofwat has already approved higher charges over the next five years to help fund improvements to ageing infrastructure and reduce sewage pollution. Those increases would not automatically disappear if the company moved into public ownership.

Longer term, the government would have to decide whether taxpayers should shoulder more of the cost of investment instead of customers through higher bills.

What happens to shareholders, creditors and staff?

Shareholders would almost certainly be the biggest losers.

Thames Water's equity has already been largely wiped out after years of financial turmoil, and any move into special administration could leave shareholders with little or no compensation.

The bigger battle would be over the company's roughly £20bn of debt. Creditors could face significant losses or be forced to accept a restructuring of what they are owed. How much taxpayers ultimately pay would depend on how the government chooses to deal with that debt.

Employees are expected to remain in their jobs.

A special administration regime is designed to keep essential public services running while a long-term solution is found. Staff would continue operating the network, repairing leaks, maintaining treatment works and responding to emergencies.

What's the timeline?

Any move into special administration could happen quickly if ministers conclude Thames Water can no longer remain financially viable.

The High Court would first appoint a special administrator, who would take over running the company. From that point, Thames Water would continue operating while the administrator stabilised the business and worked on a long-term solution.

That process could take many months, or even several years. During that time, the government would decide whether to return the company to private ownership, restructure it with new investors or retain it in public hands for longer.

Customers are therefore unlikely to notice dramatic changes overnight. The biggest decisions – over ownership, debt and future investment – would play out gradually behind the scenes.

A government spokesperson said: “The government will always act in the national interest on these issues. The company remains financially stable, but we stand ready for all eventualities, including applying for a Special Administration Regime if that were to become necessary.”

How much will it cost the taxpayer?

The big issue is that Thames Water has £20bn of debt. The question is, does the government honour that in full, in part or not at all?

Some economists say the real cost of taking on Thames Water is neutral. Since the government would be getting an asset worth at least what it cost to buy.

The bigger issue is years of investment to replace ageing pipes, reduce sewage and improve reservoirs. This will cost billions, but no-one is sure how many.
