England does not have enough water to build the 1.5 million homes pledged by the government this parliament, according to a new report.

Housing was declared one of Labour’s “five missions for government” ahead of the 2024 general election, with 1.5 million homes set to be built over a five-year period under Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership.

However, independent analysis commissioned by Water UK published earlier this week found England only has enough water for 420,000 homes – more than a million short of the Labour target.

The trade body cites two key reasons for this shortage: bureaucratic hurdles where planning rules continue to slow down new water infrastructure, and legislation which prevents companies from building to meet future demand.

open image in gallery Sir Keir Starmer promised to put ‘shovels in the ground and cranes in the sky’ in his pledge to deliver 1.5 million homes ( AFP/Getty )

David Henderson, chief executive of Water UK, highlighted the importance of lowering the “future use” regulatory barrier.

He said: "We desperately want to be able to provide enough water for new housing. But we are being held back by a regulatory system that makes building new reservoirs much slower than it should be, and unrealistic optimism about how much water people will use in the future.”

The current rules he refers to are based on government targets, which assume business demand for water will fall by 9 per cent in real terms by 2037 to 2038.

Water UK insists this prediction is unrealistic. Instead, the report highlights that non-domestic water consumption is only set to increase, particularly in light of the growing number of data centres around the country.

open image in gallery Data centres continue to be criticised for their levels of freshwater consumption ( Getty )

Currently, data centres are explicitly excluded from the Environment Agency's national framework for water resources – an official document that sets out the national strategy for water infrastructure, meaning the additional demand for water isn't currently accounted for in water resource planning.

But, with 563 established data centres, and more than 100 more in varying stages of development across the UK, a report submitted to parliament by Water UK earlier this year estimated data centres currently use 6.6 million litres of water per day, which is equivalent to the water used by 20,000 average homes.

This figure is expected to increase to 19.8 million litres, the equivalent to 60,000 homes, by 2030.

By excluding these centres from national calculations for water usage, Water UK warned both new and existing houses will “increasingly face more frequent restrictions on water use, such as hosepipe bans”.

Under UK law, before developers can build new housing, local planning authorities and water companies must confirm that the regional water network has the capacity to supply the residents living in those homes once they move in.

If there isn't enough water available in the region, water companies cannot grant connections, and local councils can freeze planning permission.

open image in gallery Water UK said in some areas of England, there is only a 2 per cent buffer between the amount of water that is available, and the amount used ( PA Archive )

To try and increase the number of available water sources, the trade body has called for the national framework for water resources to be changed so that it reflects England’s actual use of water and the risk of additional demand from businesses like data centres.

By doing this, the firms responsible for the construction of water sources like reservoirs would be able to bypass the “red tape” that prevents them from building to meet future demand.

The report also calls to attention the impacts that climate change will have on future water consumption, with England facing a potential 5 billion litre daily shortfall by 2055, according to the Environment Agency.

A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said the government is taking action to address water scarcity concerns, with all registered water companies now working with the regulator Ofwat, Natural England and the Environment Agency on 2025 to 2030 water resource management plans.

Small boat crossings to the UK have almost halved, while irregular crossings to Europe are down almost 40 per cent so far this year, The Independent can reveal.

Analysis of Home Office data shows 12,469 people had arrived in the UK on small boats by 10 July this year – down 43 per cent from 2025, when 21,690 people had made the perilous journey across the English Channel in the same period.

There have now been nine consecutive days of no arrivals from 11-19 July, the latest government figures show.

While migration experts are clear that numbers are falling, it is hard to know definitively why this is.

EU border officials have pointed to partnerships in north Africa stemming the number of onward journeys, but experts caution that these pacts come with a deadly cost.

Nearly 1,300 people have lost their lives in the Mediterranean so far this year, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

Here, The Independent examines how many people are travelling on migration routes into Europe, and onwards to the UK, and why this might be.

How many people are arriving on small boats to the UK?

By the end of June this year, 11,884 migrants had arrived on dinghies – down 41 per cent on the same period in 2025 – a particularly high year for crossings, second only to a record-breaking 2022 – and down 12 per cent on 2024.

Labour has tried to bring the numbers down by paying more money for French police enforcement to stop migrants from leaving their shores and sending small boat migrants back to France in exchange for asylum seekers.

But the “one in, one out” scheme, which began in August 2025, has only removed a comparatively small number of migrants, with 1,087 people sent back to France as of the end of June. There have been reports that the French are looking to end the programme in October this year, to focus on a European-wide strategy of tackling irregular migration.

Why are the number of UK small boat migrants falling?

Dr Mihnea Cuibus, senior researcher at the University of Oxford’s Migration Observatory, said it was hard to identify any one policy change, or factor, as being behind the fall in crossings.

He said: “Arrivals are down throughout Europe. They were also significantly down last year, which is significant because you would expect a bit of a lag as people travel through Europe to the UK. The decline we saw last year could finally be feeding through into arrivals in the UK.

“The other thing is change in policies, with the new deal with France, and the one in, one out scheme. The share of those who have been removed to France has remained very low, so we wouldn’t expect that to make a massive difference.

“It is likely that there seems to be a bit of an effect [from the different policy changes], but there are other factors such as arrivals into the EU.”

open image in gallery People thought to be migrants wade in the water as they attempt to board a small boat off the coast of Berck, France, during an attempt to cross the English Channel on 15 June 2026 ( PA Wire )

In 2026 so far, 190 boats have arrived in the UK, compared to 372 boats in the same period last year. The size of dinghies has increased significantly as smugglers adapt to increased police activity on French beaches. Larger boats now “taxi” around the coast of France and wait to pick up people offshore. In an indication of how big the small boats are now getting, a record 128 migrants arrived in one dinghy this week.

The previous record was 125 in September 2025. In total, 41,472 people arrived in 672 boats last year, compared to 36,816 people in 695 boats in 2024.

However, the dip in arrivals in the first half of 2026 compared to 2025 may be due to when the bulk of people arrived last year. In 2025, arrivals were spread out throughout the year, starting with 4,568 people in March and continuing through the summer, with more than 5,000 people arriving in September. In 2024 and 2023 however, more people arrived later in the year, with 5,417 people crossing in October 2024.

This shows that while the arrivals are tracking down this year so far, more could still make the journey in the second half of 2026.

Dr Cuibus cautioned: “We do see these numbers move up and down, at times quite randomly over the past five or six years. We still don’t understand why 2025 was so big, just as we don’t understand quite why there was a surge in people in 2022 – particularly in Albanians.”

He added: “If this trend continues until the end of summer, that will be very interesting. We are in a bit of a waiting pattern until we’ve seen the summer through.”

Where are small boat migrants coming from?

Eritrea was the top country of origin for arrivals last year, with more than twice as many as in 2024. Many leave to escape national service, which is compulsory for all citizens aged 18 to 40, and there is a near-total suppression of civil or religious freedoms in the country.

The number of people coming from Afghanistan, which was the top country of origin in 2023 and 2024, declined to second in 2025 after a peak in 2022, the year after the Taliban takeover – with 8,319 people arriving via small boats.

Figures for the first three months of 2026 show that the Eritrean numbers are being sustained, with 743 citizens making the crossing compared to 735 Sudanese and 598 Afghans.

open image in gallery Migrants leave an area of their camp that was cleared by French authorities on 2 July 2026 in Loon-Plage, France. ( Getty )

The number of Syrian, Iraqi and Vietnamese nationals also fell in 2025, while those from Sudan, Somalia and Ethiopia all increased.

The numbers of Somalians making the Channel crossing surged from 697 in 2024 to 3,783 in 2025. The steep rise comes after the jihadist group Al-Shabaab made major advances in its battle against the Somali government.

In Sudan, where the second-highest number of small boat migrants originate, the country has been experiencing a severe humanitarian crisis after three years of civil war. Over 14 million people have been displaced and two-thirds of the population – 33.7 million people – are in need of humanitarian support, according to the International Rescue Committee.

Judith Sunderland, from Human Rights Watch (HRW), said: “We’ve seen a massive outflow of people from Sudan, many who are stuck in Libya. We’ve already seen an increase in Sudanese on boats to Europe, and there could be a really significant increase if various factors align.”

Explaining migration flows more broadly, she added: “There are a lot of people on the move because they are trying to improve their situation and the lives of their family. So long as there is bad governance and poverty, people will try to get someone where they think they can have a better chance.”

Dr Cuibus explained that Syrians and Afghans are now less likely to be granted asylum in Europe than they were in previous years and said this could be contributing to the reduced numbers arriving.

Irregular border crossings into Europe are also down

Irregular crossings into Europe were down almost 40 per cent in the first five months of 2026 compared to the year before, data from border agency Frontex shows.

Nearly 39,000 crossings were recorded in the months January to June – a decline attributed to co-operation between the EU and Africa to increase police enforcement at departure points. The Western African route saw the steepest decline, with detections down by 71 per cent on the year before.

The number of people arriving in Italy from north Africa across the central Mediterranean route, usually the busiest crossing, is also down 52 per cent year-on-year, with 14,340 people making the journey so far in 2026.

Why are small boat crossings to Europe falling?

Ms Sunderland said the EU drive to stop people making the journey to Europe “carries with it enormous risks and suffering”. She explained that “people are essentially trapped in various locations in their migration journeys”, such as migrants who get sent back to Libyan detention camps when they are picked up trying to cross the Mediterranean.

“Focusing on the numbers hides the suffering that is behind this. It is based on a lot of extremely dubious deals that the EU and individual member states have pursued and support for security forces in places like Libya, Tunisia, Mauritania and elsewhere,” she added.

Giorgia Meloni’s government in Italy, backed by the European Union, is funding, equipping and training both the Libyan and Tunisian coastguards to intercept people on their way to Europe.

Human rights organisations have this week called for the EU to stop funding Tunisia over its security forces’ “reckless and violent conduct” during interceptions at sea.

According to the charity Statewatch, the EU is also looking to team up with Libya’s eastern forces to stem the number of people launching boats from its shores.

Ms Sunderland explained that there are lots of factors that would influence the numbers getting on boats, such as the weather, smuggling dynamics, and the work of border forces.

open image in gallery Migrants trying to flee to Europe, disembark in Sfax from a ship owned by the Tunisian coastguards, after being intercepted by them at sea on 10 August 2023. ( AFP/Getty )

“The numbers have decreased recently compared to the past several years, but they are still higher than they were six or seven years ago,” she explained.

She said that, those who remain stuck in third-party countries such as in detention in Libya, will not give up their determination to move on. “They will keep trying. Very few turn back. And people smuggling networks adapt and change.”

Dr Cuibus added: “The view is that all of these deals, with Libya, Tunisia, more co-operation with Morocco, these things together do seem to have an effect, because at the end of the day it is about physical prevention. Experience kind of reveals that physical enforcement can stop the boats, if you stop people leaving countries from transit, or at least temporarily divert them to other routes. But there are also broader factors at play, like the changes in the home countries’ situation.”

A spokesperson for the IOM told The Independent: “While the number of irregular arrivals to Europe has declined in 2026, the situation continues to demand urgent attention because too many people are still risking – and losing – their lives on dangerous migration routes.

“The central Mediterranean continues to be the world’s deadliest migration route... equally concerning is the growing number of migrants who disappear without trace, with increase evidence of so-called ‘invisible shipwrecks’, where vessels are lost and their fate remains unknown.”

Dubai’s busiest airport is testing biometric technology that allows passengers to walk through immigration without stopping to show their passport or boarding pass.

The “red carpet” lane service at Dubai International airport (DXB) reduces terminal transit time by more than 60 per cent, the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA Dubai) said.

According to GDRFA Dubai, AI biometric cameras can clear up to 10 people simultaneously and see travellers pass through border control in just 3.4 seconds.

Smart Gates featured in the advanced passport control system will “allow guests arriving and departing the airport to pass through passport control swiftly, typically within seconds, thanks to their enhanced features and contactless process”, said DXB.

Those registered need only look at the green light on a biometric camera after removing any face coverings, without scanning a document.

The service initially launched as a trial at Terminal 3 for premium passengers, but is now also available to arrivals after 528,900 people used the Smart Corridor in 2025.

According to GDFRA Dubai, 26.4 million travellers overall used the Smart Gates last year. UAE and GCC nationals, UAE residents and visa-on-arrival guests with biometric passports are automatically eligible to use the Smart Gates.

The airport is the first major transport hub in the world to trial the system, which uses integrated flight data and artificial intelligence to register passengers.

Travellers are registered to use the gates when entering the passport control touchpoint at DXB. Families with children and people under 1.2m tall are ineligible to use the service.

The airport is the first major transport hub in the world to trial the system ( Getty/iStock )

Prospective holidaymakers can check their passport online to see if they can skip queues using the Smart Gates.

The UK’s Foreign Office (FCDO) lifted its “all but essential travel” advisory for the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on 18 June.

DXB expects to welcome around three million passengers through its terminals in the first half of July.

Paul Griffiths, the chief executive of Dubai Airports, told The Times: “We’ve invested in camera technology, whereby you can continue to walk through a space and be verified as OK to enter or leave the country, so no passports in your hand, no gate readers, no difficulty with the whole process.

“We have to make the security process no less rigorous but far less intrusive.

“It will be rolled out to all passengers. At the moment we’ve trialled it in our first and business class, but we’ve now got the camera technology to roll it out properly.”

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

News.title: The 16 best things to do in Lyon
News.content:
Few dedicated foodies make the pilgrimage to Lyon without dining once chez Paul Bocuse, be it at the late chef’s mythical, out-of-town gastronomic temple in Collonges-au-Mont d’Or (which lost one of its three stars in 2020, having held three since 1965) or at the more affordable Comptoir Paul Bocuse inside landmark covered market Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse. Across the street, admire a larger-than-life portrait of the iconic chef, frescoed onto the side of a building. Inside the market, the moules glacées (cold mussel ‘soup’) at oyster and shellfish specialist Maison Merle and a gooey round of Saint Marcellin cheese from Fromagerie La Mère Richard are other local legends. Avoid buying fruit and veg here unless you have to – weekly outdoor food markets elsewhere in the city are cheaper.

To sample future talent in the Lyonnais kitchen, mingle with students over lunch, dinner or drinks and live music at La Commune – an innovative food court that hosts chefs aspiring to open their own restaurant in Lyon. Resident chefs cook up a storm at La Commune for maximum six months, meaning an ever-changing rollcall of epicurean excitement at this unique culinary incubator.

To extend the experience further afield, consider a road trip along a section of the Vallée de la Gastronomie, stretching 620km (385 miles). In Lyon, the gourmet route delves into the secrets behind chef Joseph Viola’s award-winning duck foie gras and sweetbread pâté en croûte (think French-posh pork pie) and the city’s distinctive offal-based bouchon (Lyonnais bistro) cuisine.

Sports.title: Former Premier League star, 22, joins SEVENTH club of his career just 18 months after shock major £64million transfer
Sports.content:
FORMER Aston Villa star Jhon Duran has joined his SEVENTH club at the age of 22, he’s joined Portuguese side Benfica on a season-long loan.

It’s his THIRD loan move since moving to Al Nassr just 18 months ago in a shock transfer.



The Portuguese team will pay a £5.19million loan fee with an option to make it permanent for £25.5m at the end of the season.

Following the move Duran said: “I am happy! I continue to say that it is the biggest club in Portugal. I am very grateful to be here.



“I have very high expectations of being here. I want to play well, give my all and become champion.”

But the £25.5m buy option is pennies compared to the £64m the Saudis, who are now managed by ex-Tottenham and Nottingham Forest manager Ange Postecoglou, paid Villa for his services in January 2025.

It was a transfer which shocked football, as the striker appeared to have the world at his feet at Villa Park.

He was very much competing with Ollie Watkins for the first-choice No9 spot at the age of 21.

He built a reputation for scoring important and memorable goals as he chipped in with late winners and long-range worldies for Unai Emery‘s side.

His potential looked like it had no ceiling.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Prem giants Chelsea held a real interest in the Colombian striker in the summer of 2024, ahead of what would be his last season in the claret and blue of Aston Villa.

However, since his big money move to the Saudi sands, where he earns over £300,000 a week, his career has gone off the rails.

After just five months, Duran joined Turkish side Fenerbahce on loan, where he had some injury troubles and managed three goals in ten appearances.

Despite joining Fenerbahce on a season-long loan, he then switched to Zenit St Petersburg of Russia in February this year.



He managed one goal in six league appearances for the Russians and subsequently returned to Saudi this summer.

And this latest move indicates that Duran has no interest in pursuing a career in Saudi Arabia, it was a move which seemed to be over almost as soon as it began.

Sports.title: ‘It’ll hurt me for a long time’ – Argentina star Rodrigo De Paul blasts ‘conspiracy theories’ over World Cup final loss
Sports.content:
RODRIGO DE PAUL has slammed conspiracy theories surrounding the Argentina team during the World Cup.

The South Americans were outclassed in the tournament’s final by Spain as they failed to retain their title as world champions.



Throughout the World Cup, there were suggestions that Argentina were able to get away with multiple incidents.

Enzo Fernandez stuck an elbow on the back of Elliot Anderson’s head early in the semi-final and went unbooked.



In the quarter-final, Mohamed Salah felt he was fouled 20 seconds before Argentina’s winning goal.

The moment was more controversial as the North African nation had a goal ruled out for a similar offence earlier in the tie.

De Paul, 32, has now hit back at the claims in a post on Instagram in which he suggests they were made by people envious of Argentina’s success.

He wrote: “The greatest pain is that we couldn’t bring the World Cup back to our country, because if anyone deserved to relive that feeling, it was you.

“But as the hours go by, you’re making us realise that your connection with this team goes far beyond the trophy, and that’s something I want to hold onto to get through this moment.

“Today I see how many people were hoping for this defeat.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Spreading unfounded conspiracy theories throughout the World Cup to soothe the pain of others who couldn’t experience what all Argentinians were experiencing.

“Because our smiles bother them, because our mannerisms annoy them.

“But that only reaffirmed that the passion and love for our jersey can overcome anything.

“It will hurt for a long time, but today more than ever I am proud to be ARGENTINE.”



De Paul’s team-mate Cristian Romero echoed the message in his own post on social media.

The Tottenham star proclaimed that finals are not “handed” to teams, suggesting they earned their spot in the showpiece match.

He wrote: “And this time, it didn’t happen for us.

“And believe me, it hurts. It hurts a lot, because no one wanted to keep writing this beautiful story more than we did.



“We dreamed of bringing the cup home again, and it didn’t happen.

“But if there’s one thing we’ll never lack, it’s heart. We left it all out there.

“We had to settle for second place, but we never stopped representing Argentina with the pride and commitment that this jersey deserves.

“What a pride and fortune it is to be part of this family, damn it Argentina.



“Sorry we couldn’t give you that joy we so wanted to deliver.

“We play for you, for every Argentine who was cheering from every corner of the world. We feel that love every day.

“Today it’s time to get back up. Start over. Work harder, believe more, and prepare so that this jersey returns to where we ourselves put it in these last years, at the very top.

“Because finals aren’t handed to you—they’re earned by reaching them.



“And this group, and whoever steps up, will keep fighting, united, with the same dream as always.

“Thank you for being there. Thank you for believing. We’ll rise again. Because that’s Argentina. Always together.”

The posts come after footage emerged of the Argentina team leaving their dressing room before the World Cup final.

National treasure Lionel Messi could be heard telling his team-mates to “forget everything” before they entered the pitch.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The footage has sparked speculation online that something was awry in camp before facing Spain.

Social media theories suggest the message was urging the players to ignore criticism of their aggressive, streetwise style.

The Gunners had been in talks with Aston Villa since the end of the season but would not go close to the £117m asking price, which Chelsea quickly met to secure the deal.

Arsenal are looking to bolster their midfield and wide areas this summer.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr shows off new look after undergoing CHIN surgery and reconciling with ex-girlfriend
Sports.content:
VINICIUS JR has shown off a jaw-dropping new look after the World Cup.

The Real Madrid forward starred in the Brazil side who were eliminated from the World Cup by Norway in the last 16.



But immediately following the tournament – which Spain went on to win after beating Argentina in the final – the 26-year-old reportedly went under the knife for cosmetic surgery on his chin.

In a photo with dermatologist Dr Alessandro Alarcao, Vinicius’ chin was visibly different and more defined compared to before.



Brazilain outlet TMC published a report detailing how Vinicius had undergone a chin harmonisation procedure at a clinic in Goiania, Brazil.

A viral video of the Real star signing a shirt also showed off the side profile of his new-look chin.



While there is no set cost for the cost of such a procedure, in the UK it can range anywhere from £3,000 to more than £14,000 depending on the treatment.

And it appears to have come with Vinicius Jr appearing to reconcile with girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

They now seem to have coupled up again after they were pictured with their arms around one another as she cut the ribbon on opening a new gym.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A comment by Vini under her most recent social media post showing a holiday to Italy where he said “I love you” would also indicate they are now back together.

The pair have been dating on and off since first being linked in 2025. In May 2026 she said they had split before she was seen partying on a superyacht with the footballer.

Vinicius had drawn criticism for relaxing while on a superyacht with bikini-clad Virginia following his trophyless season with Los Blancos and Brazil’s premature World Cup exit.

The cost of hiring the superyacht is understood to be in the region of £1million.

Virginia has previously shared posts about the cosmetic surgery she has had from Dr. Alarcao, who was flown in from Miami, USA, for the operation.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson reveals meeting Kevin Keegan in pub just days after 'love it' rant
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson reveals meeting Kevin Keegan in pub just days after 'love it' rant

The Liverpool legend and former Newcastle United and England manager Kevin Keegan was widely regarded as one of the most admired and beloved figures in world football

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan and Sir Alex Ferguson went head to head for the title in the 95/96 season

Sir Alex Ferguson has recalled a heartwarming encounter with Kevin Keegan, just days after former Newcastle United boss delivered one of the most iconic managerial outbursts in Premier League history.

‌



Keegan, one of the most popular figures in English football died aged 75 following a battle with cancer on Monday.

‌



In a statement, his family said: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

‌



"Kevin, a double Ballon D'or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

‌



Tributes have poured in from across the football world, and former Manchester United manager Ferguson has reflected on a few memorable moments he shared with Keegan.

One of those encounters came in a pub, just days after Keegan famously declared that he would 'love it' if his side beat United in the 1995/96 title race - a passionate response to Ferguson's trademark mind games that helped define their rivalry.

Recalling their encounter, Ferguson said: "That was Kevin, he was all emotion and he brought that to the team as well. They played for Kevin Keegan, there's no question about that.

‌



"The interesting thing about the outburst from Kevin, two weeks after the season had finished, I was playing golf with some friends and went to a great bar up the road, nice food. We went up there, and who walks in? Kevin Keegan and he spent the rest of the night on the piano."

View 3 Images Ferguson and Keegan during Newcastle United's match against Manchester United

That season, Newcastle surrendered a 12‑point lead to United, but by then, Keegan had long put the collapse behind him.

‌



Ferguson added: "The best thing about him is he held no grudges, that was a fantastic quality he had. We had a great night, he would always say - whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten.

"I really respected him for that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 3 Images Tributes to Kevin Keegan outside St James' Park

Keegan died after being diagnosed with cancer, but was still active in the final months of his life. The former England boss is survived by his wife, Jean, and their children, Laura Jane and Sarah Marie.

'King Kev' remains one of the finest players England has ever produced, and his international career - both as a player and later as manager was unforgettable.

‌



A two‑time Ballon d'Or winner, he enjoyed spells with Scunthorpe United, Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton, Newcastle and Blacktown City.

He hung up his boots in 1985 and took charge of Newcastle in 1992. From there, the Liverpool icon went on to manage Fulham, England and Manchester City before returning to St James' Park for a second spell in 2008.

Sports.title: Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final

The Falklands controversy between England and Argentina is back in the headlines following a declaration from a family member of one player

View 2 Images Leandro Parades' sister has reignited the Falklands controversy (Image: La Nacion)

Barbara Parades, the sister of Argentina star Leandro, has brought the Falklands row back into the spotlight after controversially claiming they have the Islands. The dispute over which of Argentina or England owns the South Atlantic Island was a trending topic surrounding their semi-final clash at the World Cup.

‌



In the immediate aftermath of their 2-1 win over the Three Lions, Argentina players celebrated in front of their fans and later revealed a white banner that had the phrase "Las Malvinas Son Argentinas", written on it. In English, that translates to: "The Falklands belong to Argentina".

‌



A FIFA investigation was demanded ahead of their participation in the final, but that went ahead on Sunday without any intervention or punishment. The 2022 world champions took on Spain and were outclassed at MetLife Stadium, with their post-match behaviour drawing much-deserved criticism after punches were thrown.

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Despite that, Barbara's reflection on their campaign was one of pride, largely due to beating England. She told reporters: "Getting this far and beating England along the way meant everything to us. We might not have the fourth star, but we have the Falklands for ourselves."

The Falklands had been a huge topic in the build-up to England's semi-final defeat and rumbled on for days afterwards, following uproar over the banner held up by Argentina players. The UK government even weighed in, saying: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

Argentina's Premier League stars could theoretically have their UK work visas revoked if their conduct is considered "not conducive to the public good", with the Home Office holding the legal authority to do so. Nevertheless, legal expert Asma Bashir has described such an outcome as "highly unlikely".

‌



Such suggestions only emerged following quite an outburst from Nile Gardiner, a former aide to Margaret Thatcher, who had deployed troops to reclaim the Island in 1982. The dispute dates back to the early 19th century, with both nations laying claim to the South Atlantic Island. The conflict lasted 74 days and claimed the lives of over 900 people.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

FIFA have yet to sanction Argentina for that incident, though they could face retrospective punishment over the post-match scenes against Spain, with an investigation now underway.

‌



Paredes was amongst those involved in a brawl with Eric Garcia and Gavi, in which he appeared to throw punches, yet escaped without a red card.

Despite his behaviour, Paredes focused solely on their tournament campaign in his statement following Sunday's final. It read: "Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves.

"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team. To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

‌



View 2 Images Leandro Paredes tried to fight Spain players after Argentina lost the World Cup final

Paredes' mum, Myriam Benitez, also spoke out on the controversy while talking to journalists awaiting Argentina's arrival at the Ezeiza airport in Buenos Aires. She said: "We never disrespect anyone. Respect always, I think that's everything that motivates us and gets us to where we really want to go. I know what the Argentine National Team means to my son."

The 32-year-old is currently turning out for Boca Juniors in his homeland following stints in France and Italy. A number of the Argentina squad actually ply their trade in Spain, with Nahuel Molina amongst those on Atletico Madrid's books.

Arsenal have been heavily linked with signing Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes for the majority of the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is still being linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty )

Arsenal have reportedly stepped up their efforts to sign Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes, but may have seemingly changed their previous plans for the transfer.

‌



Guimaraes has been heavily linked with a move to the Gunners all summer and reportedly expressed a wish to leave Newcastle earlier in the window.

‌



The 28-year-old remains under contract at St James’ Park until 2028, and The Times have reported that Arsenal have now opened talks with Newcastle over a deal for the midfielder.

The report claims that Arsenal had previously made it clear they would be prepared to pay up to £60million to sign Guimaraes this summer.

However, Newcastle are seemingly determined to maintain their £75million valuation, meaning Arsenal would need to change their plans in order to meet the Magpies’ valuation.

A separate report from The Telegraph has claimed that Newcastle have been left "mystified" by the reports claiming they have begun talks with Arsenal over a deal for Guimaraes.

It remains to be seen if an agreement will be reached between Arsenal and Newcastle for Guimaraes, who was recently with the Brazil squad for this summer’s World Cup.

Guimaraes was part of the Brazil squad that reached the last-16 stage in North America, before the Selecao were denied a quarter-final spot thanks to a defeat to Norway.

The Newcastle star will now be on a summer break before returning to pre-season duties in the next few weeks, and it remains to be seen if that will be with Arsenal or Newcastle.

‌



The report does suggest, though, that if Arsenal were to make an offer of around £75million, it would give the Magpies something to think about.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has questioned England boss Thomas Tuchel's approach following the Three Lions' World Cup exit to Argentina

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has been criticised for his tactics in England's semi-final defeat to Argentina (Image: Kevin C. Cox, Getty Images)

Paul Scholes has accused Thomas Tuchel of wanting to be sacked by England. The Three Lions boss endured a disappointing end to his first World Cup as his team exited the tournament at the semi-final stage to Argentina with a toothless end.

The German coach's substitutions came under scrutiny following the match, while Tuchel took aim at the DNA of English football and suggested he never tasked his players with sitting deep to defend their lead. Despite England recording their best finish since winning the tournament in 1996, there has been discussion over whether Tuchel remains the figure to lead the side.

The former Chelsea boss is under contract until after the Euros in two years' time, and Tuchel has indicated he intends to stay in position until that time. But Scholes is not convinced that the 52-year-old wants to stay.

"I think his comments since the game have actually made it worse than the performances. Saying it's not in the English DNA. You're part of that DNA now, Thomas," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad & The Football.

"He's gone on the offensive and blamed players a lot," Scholes continued. "That is something our manager would never do.

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

"He'd blame us behind closed doors on the training ground and meetings but in public never. I think Thomas Tuchel has a bit of a history with this at football clubs; he blames players and falls out with sporting directors. You just wonder with the way he's been speaking, 'do I want to get sacked'."

"It seems to indicate that [Thomas Tuchel] does want to leave [the England role] from the stuff he was saying because it was quite hard to come back from that," he added. "And I didn't realise until yesterday, when I heard someone talking about it, how much he fell out with people at football clubs he's been at.

"You think about it, he's not been at clubs for very long, has he? PSG, Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich. He falls out with people and maybe just engineering his way out."

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel will lead England into the Nations League (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Nicky Butt also questioned Tuchel's approach. "He's obviously an honest coach, and he says what he thinks, but do you think the PR who works with him, obviously they have a big PR at the FA, do you not think they should be coaching him on what to say? 'If you're going to stay on in this job, Thomas, you need to say this.'"

Scholes said: "I don't think he cares. He's had big jobs, he's not bothered."

"I get that but they should lead him in the right direction," Butt replied. "If he wants to stay on he needs to play the game."

Butt was also frustrated with Tuchel's squad selection. "You look at the squad, he brings defenders on, he's not really got that many attacking options to go on anyway," he said.

"Rashford and for me Watkins should have been brought on. Even that 10 role with Palmer and Foden at home, they must be sat at home thinking 'what am i doing here on holiday with my feet up, I should be trying to win us the World Cup'."

Sports.title: Aston Villa are down familiar transfer path but eventually Unai Emery’s magic won’t be enough
Sports.content:
Aston Villa seem to be on a rinse and repeat summer plan that has them grappling whether to sell their top players and then having to think, and think again, before making major signings.

Off the back of a season that saw Unai Emery lead Villa to fourth, owing to a run that saw them win 12 out of 13 games, and end a 30-year trophy drought by winning the Europa League two of their first moves this summer have been to sell Youri Tielemans and, any day now, Morgan Rogers.

Two of their three goalscorers in their European final victory have sought pastures new, recouping £152million in the process, which eases the financial concerns the club may have had whilst they also prepare for Champions League revenue once more.

It seems only Villa can sanction British-record transfer exits and then have to think about whether they go and land some more marquee names. Already Johan Manzambi has been signed from Freiburg for a club-record £58m and Joao Gomes has moved over from Wolves for £38m, but rather than go again, the consideration seems to be whether they may have to sell more of their first-team regulars.

‌



The Midlands outfit have become the poster boys for the flaws in PSR regulations in recent years. But whilst supporters of the club bemoan a system that isn't working for them, it is worth considering that they are not blameless and the reliance on Emery's magic wand is a ticking time bomb.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

Villa find themselves in a position, the like of which they've probably not been in since the early 1990s when they pushed Manchester United for the Premier League title. Their scope for mistakes, and being able to recover from them, is far less than the established teams who can have a poor year and bounce back with relative ease.

So when the Midlands side get hold of a top player, surely it serves them better to retain him - and case studies back that up. Here are a few genuine, maybe slightly hard to accept, facts.

£100m players just don't move to certain clubs. If you're that good and on the market for that amount of money, there's only a cluster of places you end up. So when Villa sell Rogers for £100m the odds on them getting a similar replacement, probably for similar money, are slim to none.

‌



View 4 Images Morgan Rogers has been invaluable to Aston Villa (Image: Dan Mullan, Getty Images)

Villa sold Jack Grealish for £100m and that money was distributed out on new arrivals. They finished 11th with him and 14th without him, sacking a manager in that time. West Ham sold Declan Rice for £105m, distributed those funds and three years later have been relegated. Newcastle sold Alexander Isak for £125m, signed several frontmen to fill the void, and dropped massively. Go back further and Tottenham reinvested Gareth Bale's then world-record fee on the so-called "Magnificent Seven" - which didn't get them far.

So unless you're Liverpool selling Philippe Countinho for over £100m and buying Virgil van Dijk, a defender wanted by every top Premier League team, the offloading of an elite player for huge sums to reinvest has rarely ended well.

The parallels with Tottenham circa 2015 to 2019 are undeniable. A sleeping giant of sorts that finally cracked a once exclusive club, much of it owing to a sensationally gifted manager in the dugout. Mauricio Pochettino made Tottenham more than the sum of their parts and had them mixing it with the elite.

‌



Emery has done likewise, but like Pochettino, there was always talk of him eventually taking the plunge at a club who could consistently offer him the chance to win titles. When Tottenham lost Pochettino, the fear was they'd fall, and so they did. Its hard to deny that the same wouldn't happen to Villa.

And for all the talk of Emery's commitment, the fact he's found the perfect environment, the fact he's allowed the run of the club. Nothing lasts forever and the Spaniard can only pull so many rabbits out of a hat.

View 4 Images Aston Villa have bought in Johan Manzambi as they look to fill the void left behind

Villa, like Tottenham, are investing in their stadium, albeit to a far lesser degree. The hope is that it will bring more financial income, but what about the impact on the pitch? Villa's is yet to be determined but, for all the talk of needing a slight rebuild and getting good money for players, no team in history, has seen sanctioning first-team player exits on an almost annual basis as a route to success.

‌



The frustration with Tottenham, from a Villa stand point, is how they finished 17th and have since spent £185million on two midfielders, breaking their club-record fee twice in a week to land Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali.

That will make them infinitely better, but their financial structure ultimately gave them the scope to do so whilst Villa, who finished fourth, can go nowhere near matching those fees.

In the accounts for 2024/25 Villa had the highest wages to revenue ratio in the league, spending 74 percent of it on their player salaries, just over £270m, according to a Deloitte report. In stark contrast Tottenham's own figure was 45 percent - the lowest in the top flight.

The PSR rules that have governed the Premier League state that clubs cannot post losses of more than £105m over a three-year reporting cycle, which is well documented now, as are the punishments for breaching them. Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system comes in as its replacement from the upcoming season, which means clubs will be allowed to spend a maximum of 85 percent of their revenue on squad costs - which cover player wages, amortised transfers and agents' fees. UEFA's remains at 70 percent.

‌



View 4 Images Unai Emery has continued to mix it with the Premier League's elite, but some will question how long he can keep it up

Villa's willingness to spend so much of their revenue of player wages had actually come down. Go back 12 months to the 2023/24 season and it was more than 90 percent of their revenue. These are decisions ultimately taken by the club, prepared to operate close to the limit, hence why they were fined £19.4m by UEFA this month for a "significant breach" of its squad-cost rule for 2025.

Whether the current financial regulations are fit for purpose is ultimately a debate worth having, but this current set of rules are where we are right now. Plenty of top clubs, and aspiring ones, are managing to operate in an ambitious way within them.

Villa seem to have been hamstrung since the early days of the Emery era, when it did become clear that his managerial prowess was going to cover up for other shortcomings.

‌



Already it looks like a summer where those at Villa Park will, privately at least, bemoan the state of the financial landscape. Emi Martinez is another name being linked with the exit door.

After losing to Everton six months ago Emery himself claimed: "We are not contender to be in the top five. We are still not being contenders. There are other teams with more potential than us."

Whether that was a parting shot at those above him, a genuine reminder of where they are or the harsh reality of managing a club operating at their maximum is anyone's guess.

Sports.title: Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap
Sports.content:
Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap

Chelsea are expected to announce the signing of Argentina international Valentin Barco

View 2 Images Valentin Barco of Argentina is expected to join Chelsea (Image: Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Strasbourg star Valentin Barco is still expected to become a Chelsea player this summer, after the Argentina star had a heated exchange with Jude Bellingham during the World Cup.

‌



Barco was part of the Argentina squad that faced England in the semi-final of the World Cup last week, and is now expected to move to Stamford Bridge in the near future.

‌



Chelsea have already completed the signings of Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra this summer, and there are growing rumours that more could follow in the days and weeks ahead.

‌



It was reported back in May that Barco would sign for Chelsea after the Londoners agreed a €40million (£34m) deal with Strasbourg.

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

The Athletic have now revealed that Chelsea are on the verge of confirming the Barco signing, just days after the midfielder became involved in a fiery confrontation at the World Cup.

Barco was a member of the Argentina squad that battled through to the World Cup final, though he managed just 19 minutes of action across the entire tournament.

‌



It was during the semi-final victory over England that Barco became involved in a tense exchange with Bellingham.

Barco, who remained on the bench throughout the win against the Three Lions, ran past several England players as he celebrated one of Argentina's goals.

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham of England reacts towards Valentín Barco of Argentina (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Following the final whistle, Bellingham was spotted watching on as Argentina's players celebrated, with Barco rushing over to join his jubilant teammates.

The Real Madrid star then noticed Barco and made his way over to the incoming Chelsea star, clipping him around the back of the head before the pair became embroiled in a heated confrontation, with shoving and fierce words exchanged.

‌



Barco will now head off on a summer break having been part of the Argentina squad that reached the World Cup final, with a formal announcement from Chelsea confirming his signing appearing to be just around the corner.

The news surrounding Barco comes as Chelsea seal a deal to bring Morgan Rogers to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa in a £117million transfer, pipping Arsenal to the England international's signature in the process.

Reports have also surfaced suggesting that England defender John Stones is firmly on the Blues' radar, after the 32-year-old departed Manchester City as a free agent earlier this summer.

Sports.title: Chelsea could ruin Arsenal transfer plans AGAIN as Blues target John Stones
Sports.content:
Chelsea could ruin Arsenal transfer plans AGAIN as Blues target John Stones

John Stones is a free agent after starring for England at the World Cup and his availability has alerted both Chelsea and Arsenal in their search for defensive reinforcements

View 2 Images John Stones is on both Chelsea and Arsenal's radar (Image: Pat Isaacs/NurPhoto)

John Stones is one option being considered by Chelsea in their search for central defensive reinforcements, potentially putting the Blues on another collision course with Arsenal.

‌



Stones is available on a free transfer following the expiry of his contract at Manchester City and, despite a season of limited game time, his stock is high after a strong showing at the World Cup with England. At the age of 32, Stones offers extensive Premier League pedigree following his trophy-laden decade in Manchester and is understood to have suitors both in England and abroad.

‌



It emerged over the weekend that Arsenal are courting Stones amid concerns that William Saliba faces up to five months on the sidelines due to the back injury that plagued him during the World Cup.

‌



However, The Athletic have revealed that Chelsea are also keen on Stones, who would aid their mission to add more 'ready-made' players to their squad.

Chelsea could add two central defenders to their squad this summer depending on exits and are currently in talks with Crystal Palace over a deal for the impressive Maxence Lacroix. A deal for the 26-year-old could cost as much as £55million, though, which is a figure higher than Chelsea's valuation of the Frenchman.

If both Arsenal and Chelsea were to move for Stones in the coming weeks, then he would be the second England World Cup star the London clubs have competed for this summer after Morgan Rogers.

‌



Both Arsenal and Chelsea are long-term admirers of the Aston Villa star, who was always expected to move for big money this summer.

View 2 Images Chelsea have already signed another Arsenal target in Stones' World Cup team-mate, Morgan Rogers (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA)

But despite Arsenal emerging as the red-hot favourites to land him in recent weeks, it's Chelsea who have won the race for Rogers' signature after shaking hands with Aston Villa on a deal worth £117m.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have valued Rogers at £80m, though it's understood they may have gone to £100m to land a player who amassed 14 goals and 12 assists across 55 games in all competitions last season.

But with Villa's valuation of Rogers increasing in the wake of Elliot Anderson's £116m transfer to Manchester City, Chelsea have put up the money to seal what could well end up being the biggest deal of the summer.

Sports.title: 'Biggest moment of my career' - Emotional Menzies reflects on Humphries win
Sports.content:
An emotional Cameron Menzies dubbed his win against Luke Humphries "the biggest moment of my darts career" after his dramatic upset secured his place in the next round of the World Matchplay Darts.

Menzies pulled out an incredible Big Fish checkout to beat world No 2 Humphries 10-7 in his first-ever triumph at Winter Gardens.

The monumental victory was a full-circle moment for the Scot, and represents a remarkable turnaround in fortune just eight months after he required surgery for punching a table during his first-round defeat to Josh Manby at the World Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies lands the Big Fish finish to stun Luke Humphries at the World Matchplay.

"I don't know how to explain that [victory]. I did believe in my heart that I could maybe cause an upset but I would have to play it out of my skin," Menzies said.

"I wouldn't say I played it out of my skin, but I played really well. I did say before the game started, to beat Luke, I need to take every chance that he gives me.

"It's not like Luke to give a lot of chances away but obviously I'm going to take it. A lot went in. I was happy. I stole a few legs to win but it's made the best moment of my darts career."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies hits a HUGE double-double finish against Luke Humphries!

The Scot revealed in February that he considered giving up darts altogether, but reflected on his greatest ever win after a "terrible" start to 2026, which also included the death of his uncle:

"It's up there because I didn't think I was going to qualify for this.

"The start of the year, I was terrible. I was just really bad. I had a really poor start to the year but I went through a lot.

"I'm in a better place mentally and physically. I'm enjoying darts again."

Mardle: Menzies knows he can handle anything now

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hear from Cameron Menzies and Wayne Mardle after the Scotsman claimed a famous win over Luke Humphries at the World Matchplay.

Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle:

"It's his best ever win, and he mentioned that.

"With Cameron Menzies, everyone mentions his emotions, but it's the way he had to win that game.

"Nothing went according to plan. He was broken back early twice, that's up and down emotions. The high of breaking to being broken back.

Image: Menzies' win against Humphries was his first at Winter Gardens

"Then he went on a run, and got pegged back.

"There was a lot happening in that game, but he held it all together beautifully.

"Humphries had an amazing spell of four legs, but then Menzies found a level again, and that's something we don't see enough.

"What he should take away from tonight was the way he handled this situation. It was like he was there a million times before.

"He knows he can handle anything now."

Image: Luke Littler, World Matchplay Darts 2026

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens from July 18-26, as a 32-player field compete for the prestigious Phil Taylor Trophy.

Two-time world champion Luke Littler takes on Nathan Aspinall in a blockbuster clash after opening his defence of the Phil Taylor Trophy with a sensational 10-6 win over Niko Springer on Day One in Blackpool.

Three-time World Matchplay winner Michael van Gerwen faces fellow Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode, while Gary Anderson - the 2018 champion - goes up against 2023 runner-up Jonny Clayton having recorded the eighth-highest average in World Matchplay history, averaging 109.96 in his 10-2 demolition of Ryan Joyce.

Sports.title: 'We know a lot of what's going on' - Rahm tight-lipped on LIV future
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm has remained tight-lipped about his LIV Golf future for 2027, saying "we know a lot of what's going on" but he is not in a position to share details.

The future of the breakaway golf league beyond the end of this season remains in doubt after backers the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund confirmed in April it is ending its funding for the series.

As one of the league's highest-profile players, Rahm's future beyond this season has been the subject of speculation amid LIV's bid to seek alternative investment.

LIV is in the UK this week for its event at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Staffordshire, its first tournament since the start of June.

Asked in Tuesday's pre-event press conference whether he had any clarity about LIV's future heading into 2027, Rahm said: "Yes. Well, we're in contact with them.

"We know a lot of what's going on, yeah.

"Not that I can share with you guys right now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment New Zealand's Ryan Fox won The Open with a 12ft birdie putt on the 18th hole at Royal Birkdale

Put to him that he seemed optimistic, the Spaniard said: "I'm always optimistic.

"I play a game for a living. I can't really be too upset about how things are going in life. Even though I'm very frustrated on the course very often, off the course I'm very different to what a lot of people think."

Rahm, who joined the league from the start of 2024, was then asked directly whether he expected to be playing on LIV next year.

"I'm not going to share anything that I can't share with you guys right now," he replied.

Rahm wants clarity over code of conduct warnings

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Rahm received a code of conduct warning at The Open after throwing his club following his tee shot on the par-three 15th at Royal Birkdale

Rahm returns to LIV action after finishing tied 46th at The Open last week after shooting four-over for his final round.

The Spaniard received a code of conduct warning from Friday's second round at Royal Birkdale last week after throwing his club following his tee shot on the par-three 15th.

Asked whether he had sufficient clarity on what actions constitute a warning or a two-shot penalty under the new-for-2026 major code of conduct rules, Rahm said: "I personally have no idea what the line is. No clue."

He added: "I think you can all kind of understand what it may or may not be. I completely forgot about it until it happened. I know they issued multiple warnings over the course of the week.

"Yeah, it would be nice to have some clarity."

Sports.title: Charges and challenges - the scale of the task facing Maresca at Man City
Sports.content:
Plenty of the Premier League's top clubs have rolled the managerial dice ahead of next season. Manchester City are one of those starting a new era, turning to Enzo Maresca in the wake of Pep Guardiola's decision to depart.

Maresca is returning for his third stint at the club, having been an academy coach in 2020-21 and then Guardiola's assistant in 2022-23 - the famous Premier League-Champions League-FA Cup treble-winning campaign.

He is familiar with the pursuit of silverware, but is yet to be the one to deliver it at such scale. So, how well positioned is he to lead Man City to glory in 2026-27?

Sky Sports' Ben Ransom and Laura Hunter explore Maresca's chances of success in year one - and whether trophies are the only barometer by which he will be judged in the wake of Guardiola's seismic exit.

Sympathetic start gives Maresca breathing room

Maresca has been given a kind start to his term, meeting Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Coventry City in his first three outings - a generous run to be able to establish some early rhythm. It also gives Man City's World Cup warriors, those in battle until the very last, a chance to ease back in.

Image: Rodri played nearly every minute of Spain's World Cup campaign

Rodri played nearly every minute of Spain's triumphant campaign and is the most susceptible to breaking down with fatigue. Given those first three fixtures will still heavily favour Man City without him, he should benefit from a phased return.

Maresca will, however, be under pressure to deliver given how winnable those fixtures are on paper. He cannot afford to cede ground early, especially as City face Man Utd and Liverpool in two of the next three in September. Clearly both of those rival bouts hold significance beyond the result.
