Sports.title: Gabby Agbonlahor speaks to Morgan Rogers about £117m transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor speaks to Morgan Rogers about £117m transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea

Gabby Agbonlahor has urged Aston Villa fans not to turn on Morgan Rogers as he nears a record-breaking move to Chelsea.

The 23-year-old is set to join the Blues in a £117million transfer to become the most expensive British player in history.

3 Rogers has agreed a six-year deal at Chelsea until 2032, with the option of a further 12 months Credit: Getty

Despite the Villans being set to play Champions League football in the 2026/27 season, with Chelsea not in Europe altogether, the England international has jumped at the chance to play under Xabi Alonso.

Versatile attacking midfielder Rogers departs Villa Park after two-and-a-half-years, where he scored 31 times in 125 games across all competitions.

One of those strikes came in last campaign's Europa League final against Freiburg - helping the club end their 30-year trophy drought.

He is one of three high-profile players that will depart the Midlands giants this window, with Youri Tielemans already joining Manchester United in a £35m switch.

Left-back Lucas Digne meanwhile is closing in on a return to Paris Saint-Germain after the Champions League holders activated his release clause - worth around £8.5million.

Roger that

After Arsenal refused to stump up more than £80m for Rogers, the player is now poised to be unveiled as a new Chelsea star.

For Villa cult hero Agbonlahor, he has revealed that he sent a text message to Rogers on Monday night after he passed his Blues medical.

Speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show, Agbonlahor said: "I watched him [at the World Cup], obviously, Aston Villa fan.

"And I had to message him last night, I said to him, 'Listen, thank you for everything you've done for my football club, wish you all the best in the future.'

He replied, 'Thank you, mate, I really appreciate it.'

3 Rogers proved influential in Villa finishing in fourth spot in the 2025/26 season

"And I want every Villa fan to be like that with Digne, with Tielemans, with Rogers.

"These players won our first [European] trophy since 1982 and have been a fantastic group of players for this football club.

"They've moved on now, no problem, I'm sure Morgan Rogers will get a good standing ovation when he comes back to Villa Park."

And Agbonlahor believes he will be a roaring success at Stamford Bridge - tipping him to reach another level under the tutelage of Alonso.

Commenting on where he could fit in at Chelsea, he remarked: "If Alonso does play that 3-4-2-1 that he liked at Leverkusen and play two 10s.

"He could play [Cole] Palmer and Rogers as two 10s, but he can play off the left - not off the right - it doesn't suit him over there.

3 Rogers scored three goals from 15 Europa League appearances in the previous campaign Credit: Getty

"But what you've got from this player is somebody who will receive the ball under pressure.

"And I've never seen a player who can drive with the ball- he's quicker when he's running with the ball.

"He's got such strength, skill and he can finish as well.

"Honestly you've got an all-round top player here in Morgan Rogers.

"I think he's going to get better and better.

"Let's not forget he's only 23, he's going to learn a lot from Alonso and I think he's going to be a huge success at Chelsea Football Club."

Sports.title: Deluded World Cup final villain Enzo Fernandez insists Argentina represented nation in 'best possible way' despite disgraceful behaviour in New York and riling England fans with Falklands flag
Sports.content:
Argentina's World Cup pantomime villain Enzo Fernandez has claimed he and his team-mates represented the country 'in the best possible way' in a bizarre statement on social media on Tuesday.

The Chelsea star, who goaded England with a mocking celebration after netting Argentina's equaliser in last Wednesday's dismal semi-final defeat, was left with egg on his face in the World Cup final on Sunday as his red card proved crucial to Spain's crowning 1-0 victory.

Fernandez, already booked for dissent, sent Pau Cubarsi flying with a dangerous tackle in stoppage time and left Argentina to defend with 10 men for the entirety of extra time.

Argentina's behaviour throughout the World Cup was heavily criticised after Lionel Scaloni's men used aggressive tackling, timewasting and dirty tactics to aid them en route to the final, before several players attacked Spanish stars after the full-time whistle at MetLife Stadium in deplorable scenes of violence and thuggery.

Despite being under investigation by FIFA over the post-match melees, Fernandez urged that Argentina represented themselves 'in the best possible way' during the tournament.

Enzo Fernandez believes Argentina showcased themselves and the country 'in the best possible way', despite several players attacking Spain's stars after the World Cup final

Fernandez goaded England with a mocking celebration after scoring in Argentina's 2-1 victory

'As time passes, you realise there is something much bigger than a result,' he wrote in a statement on social media platform Instagram. 'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn't just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I'll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country's shirt is the greatest honor of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I'm called upon to defend it.'

Several Argentina players were involved in ugly post-match clashes with Spain's players immediately after the final whistle, which confirmed the European nation as world champions with a 1-0 victory after extra time.

Spain's captain Rodri was struck by Nahuel Molina as he went to celebrate with his team-mates, before Dani Olmo was punched by Argentina coach Roberto Ayala.

Elsewhere, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes attacked Eric Garcia by grabbing him by the neck and then, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes.

The Chelsea star was sent off in the final after sending Pau Cubarsi flying with a late tackle

The deplorable post-match incidents came after Spain had dominated the match in terms of possession and chances, while Argentina attempted to stop them in their tracks with tough tackling, timewasting and dirty tactics.

After the final, world football's governing body FIFA swiftly opened an investigation into Argentina's violent post-match conduct, appointing a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to review footage, referee reports and documentation submitted by match delegates.

According to FIFA's Disciplinary Code, players found guilty of violent conduct should be issued with at least a three-match ban.

The same penalty applies to acts of aggression including punches, kicks, elbows, headbutts or other blows against an opponent.

Fernandez and his team-mates were also at the centre of controversy after celebrating with a banner claiming that the Falkland Islands were Argentine following their late 2-1 win over England last week.

FIFA are also investigating whether to issue a sanction in relation to the political statement, which is against their rules and regulations.

Fernandez played a key role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar before moving to Chelsea for a then-British record fee of £106.8million.

Following his behaviour and antics at the 2026 World Cup, Fernandez could receive a hostile reception in the first few weeks of the Premier League season when he returns to Stamford Bridge under new manager Xabi Alonso.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal mocks Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with hilarious sign at Madrid's celebration parade after star's shameful violence at the World Cup final - as red carded villain claims they represented nation 'in best possible way'
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal mocks Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with hilarious sign at Madrid's celebration parade after star's shameful violence at the World Cup final - as red carded villain claims they represented nation 'in best possible way'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain superstar Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with a punchy sign at his country's World Cup celebrations in Madrid.

Two million Spain supporters crowded the streets of the capital to welcome their heroes after they defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final.

But the immediate aftermath of the match was marred by the barbarous antics of Paredes, who attacked two Spain players.

He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before shoving over substitute Gavi, causing a large-scale melee in the middle of the pitch - and it's that second act to which Yamal's sign referred.

Yamal held up a sign which read: 'Velada del ano VII: Paredes vs Gavi'. The Velada del Ano is a celebrity boxing event in Spain, not unlike Misfits.

Argentina were widely condemned for their behaviour after losing the final - but they have maintained a siege mentality about it. Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off in normal time, claimed that they had represented their nation in the 'best way possible'.

Lamine Yamal mocked Leandro Paredes referring to his altercation with Gavi after the World Cup final

Argentina midfielder Paredes was lambasted after the whistle for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground

He said: 'As time passes, you realize there is something much bigger than a result.

'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I’ll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country’s shirt is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I’m called upon to defend it.'

Defending the shirt with violence is another matter, though, and the BBC's piundits weren't impressed. Micah Richards said of Argentina's behaviour: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid on Monday afternoon

Yamal carried his bags - including an oversized Hermes Birkin sack - off the plane

Wayne Rooney said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, the first of which came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of Monday morning

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigious Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Sports.title: World Cup star's secret 20-month-old daughter: Michael Olise labelled 'heartless' by mother of his child - whom he has NEVER met - after she ended two-year romance because he spent 'too much time playing on his PlayStation'
Sports.content:
World Cup star's secret 20-month-old daughter: Michael Olise labelled 'heartless' by mother of his child - whom he has NEVER met - after she ended two-year romance because he spent 'too much time playing on his PlayStation'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Olise has been described as 'heartless' by the mother of his secret 20-month-old daughter after she alleged that he has never met his child, nor contributed to her upbringing financially.

The France international, 24, was revealed to have fathered a child with 34-year-old Fatima Zaunbrecher on the heels of their two-year relationship, with Zaunbrecher taking her story public for the first time this week.

Speaking to German outlet BILD, Zaunbrecher claimed that Olise has not spoken to her since his daughter Aaliyah Noor's birth, choosing instead to communicate through lawyers.

Olise is also not believed to have met his daughter, with his lawyers reportedly advising him that it 'wouldn't be productive' for him to do so.

'How heartless can you be towards your child?' Zaunbrecher questioned in her interview, adding that his 'callousness' had 'devastated her'.

'He doesn't even talk to me, and just sends his lawyers instead. And then they send me letters saying that "it wouldn't be productive for their client to see the child". Another of his lawyers wrote to me suggesting I buy the little girl secondhand clothes to make ends meet with the money I have right now.'

Michael Olise has been accused of not supporting or meeting his 20-month-old daughter

Zaunbrecher is based in Dusseldorf and had been when the former couple started to communicate on Instagram in 2022.

The relationship began when Olise was playing at Crystal Palace, ahead of his £47.4million move to Bayern Munich.

The woman alleges that messages were exchanged between them for two months before she joined him in south London for their first date, saying that the pair had 'liked each other immediately'.

'He's half Algerian, I'm half Moroccan,' she explained. 'They're neighbouring countries after all. He also dislikes large crowds and parties, just like me.

'When he tried to kiss me on our first date, I stopped him and told him we should get to know each other better. He accepted that. From then on, I flew to London regularly.'

Their relationship eventually became tempestuous, Zaunbrecher added, due to disputes over Olise's frequent habit of playing PlayStation rather than spending time with her, and claims of infidelity on his part.

Zaunbrecher then claimed that two weeks after she had finally broken up with him over a suspected other woman, she discovered she was pregnant.

A paternity test - completed in Munich at Olise's insistence - has since confirmed that he is Aaliyah's father, but despite this, he is never thought to have met her.

BILD confirmed that sources close to the footballer suggested that he had not refused contact with Zaunbrecher.

Zaunbrecher also claimed that she has been fighting with Olise's lawyers for over two years in a bid to receive alimony, after the player initially offered a sum she has described as 'ridiculous'.

Olise has an intensely private social media presence and has often seemed to shy away from the spotlight in public too.

But since the revelation in the German press, Olise is believed to have seen his social media comments section overwhelmed with replies, and since switched off the function on Instagram.

Alongside the article, BILD also released what they alleged to be a copy of the document confirming Olise's paternity.

Olise has not yet issued a comment publicly.

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson is keen on reuniting with Unai Emery at Aston Villa as Man United, Arsenal and Chelsea target Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.

Sports.title: The teenage sweetheart who was Kevin Keegan's rock right until his last moments: Football legend met his wife of 51 years Jean on the waltzers at a Doncaster fair - but modest star told her a white lie
Sports.content:
It was a summer's day in 1970 when Kevin Keegan plucked up the courage to speak with a certain Jean Woodhouse at Doncaster fair.

He was 19, she 16, and the pair had been on the waltzers. The soundtrack of that summer was Mungo Jerry's 'In the Summertime', and were he to take her out for fish and chips, it would've cost 20 to 30 pence.

By this stage Keegan was already making strides in football, an employment which entitled him to around £30 per week. He had spent two years playing for Fourth Division side Scunthorpe United and in eight months he would be off to Liverpool.

But feeling slightly bashful, a young Keegan did not try to woo his new belle with tales from the football pitch. Instead, he pitched himself as a humble steelworker, the job he took in summertime to earn a bit of extra cash. During the off-season, Scunthorpe cut his weekly wages, you see, so he had to supplement that with jobs on the steel and in a psychiatric hospital.

'Telling them I was a footballer would have sounded too flash, even though I was an unknown playing for a small club,' Keegan later recalled. Humility was often his way.

The ruse worked. Woodhouse was charmed - despite the fact she had a crush on Manchester United superstar George Best - and four years later they married at St Peter in Chains Catholic Church in Doncaster. The eager lovers brought the ceremony forward while he was serving a ban.

Kevin Keegan and his wife Jean Woodhouse were married for 51 years from 1974 until he died

The duo, who met on the waltzers at Doncaster fair, kept their private life out of the public eye

Their marriage lasted 51 years until his death on Monday and, despite him being one of the poster boys for English football in that time, little is known of the life they kept away from the pitch. Privacy and the protection of their daughters Laura and Sarah were paramount.

Jean didn't take too much of an interest in the football herself, but with a self-sacrificial spirit, she followed him everywhere.

In May 1971 he moved to Liverpool for £33,000 and was inducted into Bill Shankly's legendary team. Suddenly his basic wage was £50 per week. There, Keegan won three First Division titles and a European Cup, though their Liverpudlian stint started inauspiciously.

Keegan arrived for his debut against Nottingham Forest late because he had misjudged the severity of the traffic on the way to Anfield. That earned him the nickname Andy McDaft, but he silenced any doubters after 12 minutes with a stunning debut goal.

After six remarkable years with the Reds, Jean followed him to Hamburg, Germany, where he would twice win the Ballon d'Or prize for being the world's best player.

Life later took them to Southampton, County Durham, the United States, Spain, and Inverkip in Scotland, and Jean was always by his side - even if she didn't pay much attention to his sporting antics.

'My wife Jean has always taken football with a pinch of salt,' Keegan once told The Guardian.

'She doesn't ever get over-involved in it, not when I'm out of it and not when I'm in it. That is the key. After matches, if you've lost she knows not to say too much for about 24 hours while you get over it and if you've won she knows I might take her out at night.

Jean wasn't overly interested in his footballing antics - and he even hid his career at first!

She and one of their daughters, Laura, joined Keegan as he received his OBE at Buckingham Palace in 1982

'We decided early on that football and family should mix as seldom as possible. In our minds there was football and then there was life.'

Football was talked about so little in the home that his daughters actually thought he was a professional golfer, given how much time he dedicated to it in their seven years in Spain.

The love he and Jean shared was horse riding. She was more adept than himself but, on those rides out, they could share a peace which wasn't afforded to him when out in public.

'To relax, I do horse riding. My wife is keen on horses,' he said in a television interview.

'I can't ride a horse to save my life. If you see me running funny on a Saturday, it's because we've been for a horse ride on the Friday night!

'Once you get on the back of a horse and get up a mountain, it's funny, nobody wants your autograph when you're galloping along. They want to get out of the way!'

He added: 'I just live normal. The terrible thing about the public in a way, and I don't mean terrible in a nasty way... you can go and talk to someone and they'll say: "oh, he talked to me, he's natural."

'Of course I'm natural! I was born the same as they were. I was brought up the same as they were. I'm just the same as they are. I think people tend to think you should be different and if you see it long enough, it could make you different.

Jean pictured outside a romany caravan near their house they shared in north Wales while Keegan was at Liverpool

Liverpool, Newcastle and England legend Keegan has died at the age of 75 after a short battle with illness

Keegan (pictured in 1977 after winning the European Cup with Liverpool) is one of the greatest players English football has ever produced

The sprawling Georgian property that was once home to footballer Kevin Keegan while he was the boss of Newcastle United in the 1990s

The property features a large white kitchen decorated with chandeliers and characterful touches

'I enjoy meeting people very much. I enjoy meeting the fans. I just came down on the train and had half a dozen around me all the way. I'd sooner have them round me than be sat on my own twiddling my thumbs.'

The sense you get is that Kevin and Jean retained their humility even when their circumstances improved.

Keegan's mother Doris was a domestic worker and his father, Joe, was a miner and Newcastle fan. The future England manager grew up in a home with no electricity, bathroom or inside toilet. If he wanted to watch the beautiful game which he so dearly loved, he had to go to a friend's house to sit down in front of the TV.

When he was manager of Newcastle in the 1990s, he and Jean moved into a sprawling country pad.

The grand Georgian property in County Durham is situated on 5.4 acres of gardens in a gated community with 24-hour security and boasts a games room, pool and bar.

This expansive property was extended in Keegan's day and has been extended again since making it now a five-bedroom home of nearly 10,000 sq ft.

It boasts a reception hall, kitchen/breakfast room, lounge, dining room, orangery, study, wine cellar and indoor swimming pool on the ground floor.

Last year it was listed for sale for £2.25million.

That's an example of the type of property they could afford, but they never lost sight of the simple pleasures of life. In the mid-2000s they purchased a house in Inverkip, a village in Scotland's west central Lowlands, and would take driving trips out into nature together. Local business workers knew them as regulars.

As one local recalled: 'I met him a few times with his wife and daughter – he was a very nice man with a nice family, and you could have a laugh with him.'

Keegan died on Monday surrounded by Jean and their two girls, having been diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January. In sickness and in health Jean stood by his side - whether at Buckingham Palace to receive his OBE or on a candyfloss-filled summer's day at Doncaster fair.

Sports.title: Shameless moment Argentina star fakes an injury in desperate attempt to save Enzo Fernandez from red card in World Cup final
Sports.content:
Shameless moment Argentina star fakes an injury in desperate attempt to save Enzo Fernandez from red card in World Cup final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Footage has emerged displaying Argentina's pathetic attempt to con the referee into reversing his decision to show Enzo Fernandez a red card in the World Cup final.

The Chelsea midfielder was given his marching orders in the 93rd minute on Sunday, after picking up a second yellow card for a recklessly late challenge on Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

Fernandez protested his innocence vehemently, but it was hard to argue against the decision of referee Slavko Vincic. Cubarsi had gone flying through the air after the foul.

And now a new angle of the foul has come to light, showing that Nicolas Tagliafico faked an injury within seconds of Fernandez flying in on Cubarsi, in an attempt to try and save the 25-year-old from being dismissed.

The full-back was walking normally until he spotted his team-mate's moment of madness, before dropping to the deck in an instant, holding his leg.

Lionel Messi then shamelessly rushed over to the referee after he had already gotten the red card out of his pocket, and pointed over to Tagliafico in a last-ditch attempt to prevent Argentina going down to 10 men ahead of extra-time.

Argentina's Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card in the 93rd minute of the World Cup final

Nicolas Tagliafico (top left of the shot) could be seen faking an injury to try and distract the referee after Fernandez committed the foul

The desperate ploy failed to change Vincic's mind, and no amount of fakery could prevent Fernandez from being sent for an early bath.

Fernandez's dismissal rounded off an abysmal 90 minutes for the 2022 champions, who had no shots compared to Spain's 15.

Argentina went on to lose in extra time after Ferran Torres smashed home a 106th-minute winner to secure a second star on Spain's crest.

The ugly antics from the South American side worsened after the full-time whistle, with Leandro Paredes, who was incredibly lucky to avoid being sent off during the final, sparking a mass brawl during Spain's celebrations.

The midfielder was consumed by rage after the defeat and could be seen throttling Eric Garcia in the throat. Moments later, he pushed Gavi to the ground while thrashing his arms around.

Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved in the scuffle, too.

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

Fernandez sent Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air with his recklessly late foul

There were also ugly scenes after the full-time whistle as Leandro Paredes (centre) sparked a brawl

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart believed the post-match behaviour from Argentina was 'disgusting' while pointing out that Messi was the only player to show some 'class'. Meanwhile, Wayne Rooney wasn't surprised.

Rooney said: 'We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them. If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Sports.title: Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA
Sports.content:
Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Madeleine McCann's younger brother will represent Scotland in swimming at the upcoming Commonwealth Games.

Sean McCann, 21, has been selected to compete for the Scots in the pool at the home Games, with swimming beginning Friday in Glasgow.

Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three, back in 2007, and has been missing ever since. Sean was just two years old at the time.

19 years on, Sean is now making his senior international bow as a swimmer, and will compete alongside Olympic champion Duncan Scott for his national team.

McCann is a distance freestyler and is expected to compete in the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the slimmed-down Games.

It is yet to be known whether parents Kate and Gerry McCann will attend the event to watch their children compete.

Madeline McCann's younger brother Sean will swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games

Sean will be swimming the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the home Games in Glasgow

Sean has been competing in the pool since the age of eight, and his career took him to the international stage at youth level in 2023 as he competed at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago.

The distance swimmer, who originally hails from Leicester but qualifies to represent Scotland through his father Gerry, is a student at Loughborough University, studying Chemical Engineering.

Loughborough is known for nurturing Great Britain's hottest prospects in the pool, with multiple Olympic champion Adam Peaty coming through the ranks at the performance centre.

Sean is looking to follow in the footsteps of the likes of Peaty by qualifying for the next Olympic Games in 2028.

There is confidence that his upcoming appearance has him on teh right path to competing for Team GB in LA in two years.

'I started competitive sport when I was 8, joining Charnwood Triathlon Club,' He once wrote on the Joe Humphries Memorial Trust website.

'It was here that I discovered my passion for swimming, and I joined Loughborough Town Swimming Club to increase the number of swim sessions I did per week.

'At the age of 10 I was selected to swim at City of Leicester (Leicestershire's performance swimming club), and I have since go on to win multiple county titles as well as becoming regional and National champion in my age group.

Madeline McCann went missing in 2007 when Sean was just two years old

'In order to have achieved this, I have had to remain extremely dedicated, getting up at 4am multiple mornings each week to train, since the age of 11.

'I am currently studying chemical engineering at Loughborough university, and train nine times a week in the pool, as well as three gym sessions, totalling over 20 hours of training week.

'I am aiming to compete at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and also the 2028 Olympics in LA.'

Sports.title: 'We still have the Falklands': Sister of Argentina thug who punched Spanish footballer at the World Cup final makes bizarre claim after nation's shameful behaviour
Sports.content:
'We still have the Falklands': Sister of Argentina thug who punched Spanish footballer at the World Cup final makes bizarre claim after nation's shameful behaviour

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The sister of Leandro Paredes shared a bizarre statement about Argentina's claim to the Falklands just hours after the national team lost their World Cup final to Spain on Sunday evening.

Disputes over the British Overseas Territory have been at the centre of Argentina's World Cup campaign, with the players singing anti-English songs throughout the tournament and displaying a banner parroting their claim to the archipelago after beating England in the semi-final.

But Barbara Paredes went one step further after landing in Buenos Aires following the team's defeat, claiming that she was consoled by the islands belonging to Argentina.

'We’re all delighted, but to be honest we didn’t expect to get this far, and having made it this far and come out on top against England – for us, that meant the world,' Barbara told reporters.

'We may not have the third or fourth star, but we’ve got the Falklands all to ourselves.'

Argentina have repeatedly attempted to assert a claim over the islands, which have been a British territory since 1833, and in 1982, launched an abortive invasion which led to the 10-week Falklands War.

" No ganamos la cuarta estrella pero tenemos las Malvinas para nosotros."



Hermana de Leandro Paredes, en Ezeiza. pic.twitter.com/ca8dgoCSth — Gabriel Alfie (@GabrielAlfie15) July 20, 2026

Leandro Paredes' sister Barbara had more incendiary comments on the Falklands after Argentina's World Cup final defeat

Paredes was heavily involved in the fighting which broke out after the loss in New York

Falkland Islanders most recently overwhelmingly pledged to remain British in 2013, with 99.8 per cent voting to stay British in an island-wide referendum.

But Argentina fans, players, and Argentine politicians whipped up what they believe is their own claim to the islands they refer to as Las Malvinas, with foreign minister Pablo Quirno suggesting that the referendum was illegitimate days before meeting England in last week's semi-final.

Quirno used an essay in La Nacion newspaper to claim the population had been 'artificially implanted by the occupying power', which was flatly rejected by Downing Street.

Meanwhile, Argentina lodged a diplomatic protest with the UK over what it called the 'unlawful' movement of a Royal Navy patrol ship near the South Atlantic archipelago.

In an official statement shared on X after the semi-final, the country's foreign affairs ministry expressed its 'strongest rejection' of the movements of HMS Medway and accused Britain of a 'military incursion' into its waters.

No 10 said the UK had notified Argentina in advance of undertaking a routine logistics visit and the British Navy 'always operates in full compliance with international law'.

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni had said before the game he did not want the fixture to become about the conflict over the territory.

But the country's vice-president Victoria Villarruel tweeted a victory message at full-time saying 'it wasn't just another match', alongside a video of what appeared to be Argentinian soldiers.

In the build-up to the fixture, she had described England as 'invaders' and 'usurping pirates'.

Premier League players Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez were among those who waved the banner after the final whistle on Wednesday, with more players in the team such as Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez set to return to England to resume their club careers after the summer break.

Despite urgent calls to FIFA to sanction players who breached the tournament's rules around the displaying of political banners, FIFA has not yet issued a sanction.

Argentina players were previously fined a paltry £20,000 in 2014 after displaying a similar banner, but European institution UEFA has since taken a harsher line, issuing one-match bans for Spain players Rodri and Alvaro Morata for leading chants of 'Gibraltar is Spanish' after winning Euro 2024.

The Boca Juniors star dragged Gavi to the floor after throttling Eric Garcia at full-time

Argentina are already under investigation after displaying a banner which supports their claim to the Falklands

Donald Trump's White House opted to back Argentina ahead of the final for using the banner, with the head of the FIFA task force Andrew Giuliani saying that it was allowed due to the country's First Amendment rights.

Argentinian president Javier Milei later waded into the row, declaring that his government was getting 'closer every day' to recovering sovereignty over the islands.

He wrote on X: 'While some are busy throwing tantrums befitting a terminally mononeuronal teenager, we, through the diplomatic route, are getting closer every day to the recovery of the Malvinas Islands, Georgias del Sur and the South Sandwich Islands, and the surrounding maritime space.'

But while Argentina may have felt free to display the banner again - after taking it to their team hotel last Wednesday - if they had won the final, the team did not get the opportunity to do so after losing to Spain 1-0 in extra time.

With the final whistle, and the loss of their World Cup title, Paredes was one of Argentina's players to mentally collapse, with the Boca Juniors midfielder disgracing himself with violent conduct.

Paredes throttled Eric Garcia in upsetting scenes before wrestling Barcelona star Gavi to the ground.

Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also involved in scraps, while Nicolas Otamendi tried to draw Player of the Tournament Rodri into an argument by accusing him of 'complaining to referees' in the build-up to Sunday's game.

With Paredes failing to be sent off after the final whistle, FIFA has since opened a second investigation into Argentina's conduct, appointing a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess the incident.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson fury fight 'on another level' with huge prize fund
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson fury fight 'on another level' with huge prize fund

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are due to go head-to-head in a huge heavyweight fight in November - but both must win their respective warm-up bouts first

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua is set to face Tyson Fury in November (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Anthony Joshua will earn "hundreds of millions" from his long-awaited all-British blockbuster fight against Tyson Fury later this year, according to Matchroom's Barry Hearn.

‌



Joshua, 36, is expected to go up against Fury, 37, in a seismic heavyweight clash in November, providing both win their respective warm-up bouts this weekend. Joshua is due to face Albania's Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday, 24 hours after Fury goes in the ring with Poland's Mariusz Wach.

‌



Although Joshua has signed the contract to face Fury in November, the fight is yet to be announced and the wait is thought to be because both boxers need to come through their warm-ups unscathed. Joshua is as short as 1/20 to beat Prenga, while Fury is priced up at as low as 1/50 to get past Wach.

‌



Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua undercard finally revealed ahead of comeback fight READ MORE :

Should both win, as expected, a gigantic 'Battle of Britain' is awaiting Joshua and Fury later this year, with the total prize fund set to be off the scale. Reports have suggested that Joshua and Fury are poised to bank £100million each as part of the agreement, which could be formally announced as early as next week.

Although boxing promoter Hearn refused to reveal the total figures when asked how much Joshua and Fury are poised to earn, he did say it will be a "load of noughts and then quadruple it".

Speaking to The Mirror, Hearn said: "Nothing I want to publicise but take a load of noughts and then quadruple it, and you've got somewhere near what he's gained. I mean, the money in boxing, especially with the Saudi involvement, Turki Al-Sheikh has made things happen that probably wouldn't have happened simply by the size of Percy's.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Joshua is set to face Tyson Fury in November (Image: Getty Images)

"I mean, it's hundreds of millions in total, so I can't say that he's replaceable if he wasn't there. I don't know where the money would come from. I'm used to doing big paper news shows where you generate millions and millions, but this is on another level.

"This is a global advert for Saudi and the facilities and the tourism and whatever. It's an international global field of play, and with that comes enormous money, which is great for the fighters."

‌



Fears had grown about the fight potentially collapsing due to the fact no announcement has yet been made and the prospect of Joshua or Fury losing their warm-up fights. But Hearn doesn't expect any issues and is still confident the clash will go ahead as planned later in 2026.

When asked if the fight might not go ahead, Hearn added: "No. I don't know if you've ever been hit on the chin by someone who weighs 17st... I haven't, and I don't want to. There's always the potential of a banana skin in boxing. History tells us that. I think it's unlikely in both cases, of course.

"But Anthony Joshua, to his credit, he's not thinking beyond Saturday. He knows what's at stake here, a fight that he's wanted for 10 years has been signed for. All they have to do is deliver their respective victories, I believe that is a huge odds-on favourite."

Article continues below

Watford-born Joshua, who last fought against YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in December 2025, has an imperious record of 29 wins and four losses across his professional. Meanwhile, Fury's most recent fight was against Arslanbek Makhmudov in April 2026 and has lost just ONCE across his 38 professional bouts.

Both Joshua and Fury as seen as two of Britain's greatest-ever heavyweight fighters, with both former world champions, making November's proposed fight a must-not-miss should it go ahead as scheduled.

Sports.title: Madeleine McCann’s brother Sean, 21, competing for Scotland in Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Madeleine McCann’s brother Sean, 21, competing for Scotland in Commonwealth Games

The Games, which take place in Glasgow from this Thursday until 2 August 2026, will mark Sean McCann's Commonwealth debut for Scotland

View 3 Images (Image: Getty Images for Commonwealth Sport)

Madeleine McCann’s brother will take part in the Commonwealth Games after being selected to swim for Scotland. Sean McCann is getting ready to step out onto the global stage this week when the Games begin in Glasgow.

‌



Madeleine was three when she went missing from her family’s holiday apartment in Praia da Luz in southern Portugal on May 3 2007, shortly before her birthday. Sean and his twin sister Amelie were just two when their older sister disappeared.

‌



According to Scottish Swimming, Sean will compete in the freestyle disciplines as he looks to qualify for Team GB and swim at the LA Olympics in 2028. The 21-year-old began competing aged eight and previously raced for Scotland at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago in 2023 in the 400m and 1500m freestyle.

‌



Speaking about his competitive journey a few years ago on the Joe Humphries Memorial Trust website, he revealed: “I started competitive sport when I was eight, joining Charnwood triathlon club. It was here that I discovered my passion for swimming and I joined Loughborough Town swimming club to increase the number of swim sessions I did per week.

"At the age of 10, I was selected to swim at City of Leicester and I have since gone on to win multiple county titles as well as becoming regional and National champion in my age group. In order to have achieved this, I have had to remain extremely dedicated, getting up at 4am multiple mornings each week to train, since the age of 11.

Josh Kerr slams 'appalling' prize money he receives for running the fastest mile ever READ MORE :

"I train nine times a week in the pool, as well as three gym sessions, totalling over 20 hours of training per week. I’m aiming to compete at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and also the 2028 Olympics in LA.”

‌



It is not known if his parents Kate and Gerry McCann will be in attendance at the Tollcross International Swimming Centre during the 11-day event, which begins on Thursday, July 23.

Mr and Mrs McCann criticised a true-crime drama about their daughter’s disappearance back in May, saying the programme was made without their consultation or consent.

Kate and Gerry said they 'had no involvement whatsoever' in the making of Channel 5’s 'Under Suspicion: Kate McCann', which depicts Madeleine’s mother being treated as a suspect during the investigation into her disappearance in May 2007.

‌



In a statement released on the day the show aired, Kate and Gerry raised concerns over the 'negative impact' such programmes have on their family as they continue to grieve Madeleine’s disappearance 19 years on.

View 3 Images Kate McCann, the mother of the missing British girl Madeleine, carries her son Sean after piking him up from the local nursery at the Ocean Club holiday resort on May 22, 2007 in Praia da Luz, Portugal. (Image: Getty Images)

“Thank you to everyone who has offered support & kindness this month,” they wrote on the Find Madeleine Campaign website. “May is never the easiest. We usually start to feel a bit ‘lighter’ at this stage of the month.

‌



“We are disappointed however, knowing that a Channel 5 ‘docu-drama’ will air tonight. We have not given, or been asked for, our consent and have had no involvement whatsoever in its making.

“We fail to see how it will help. Programmes like this, always have a negative impact on our family.”

The Metropolitan Police’s probe into the 2007 disappearance of three-year-old Madeleine has been active since 2011. German authorities identified Christian Brueckner as the prime suspect in Madeleine’s case back in 2022.

‌



View 3 Images Gerry (L) and Kate McCann (R) leave their home in Rothley, Leicestershire in central England with daughter Amelie and son Sean, 12 September 2007. (Image: Getty Images)

However, Brueckner has never been charged over Madeleine’s disappearance and has previously denied any involvement. Speaking in December, dad Gerry, from Glasgow, said the hope of finding her after all this time is 'slim', but not 'extinguished'.

“Madeleine’s been missing for 18 years, and the bottom line is, we still don’t know what’s happened to her,” he told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. Gerry added: “I don’t even mean ‘convincing’ evidence – there is no evidence to say she’s dead.

Article continues below

“Now we fully understand she may be dead, it may even be probable, but we don’t know that. I’d love to find her alive, but we need to find out what happened and bring whoever’s responsible to justice, and other children and people are at risk while that perpetrator is free.”

Sports.title: Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer
Sports.content:
Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer

Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth contract as Manchester United and Arsenal circle, even if the Cherries maintain their midfielder will not be sold

View 2 Images Alex Scott has rejected the offer of a new contract at Bournemouth

Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth deal as the likes of Manchester United circle - but the Cherries stance is set to remain the same.

‌



Scott has received a number of offers since discussions began towards the end of the season, but the Bournemouth midfielder has indicated he is not currently willing to agree new terms, reports Sky Sports.

‌



The 22-year-old has entered the final two years of his deal but the Cherries don't want to sell the Englishman and have rejected enquiries for his signature. As well as the Red Devils; Chelsea and Arsenal have also been linked.

‌



Bournemouth expect Scott to remain their player next season regardless of whether he signs a new deal or continues to run down his contract.

The club, who have just secured European qualification for the first time, have adopted a firm stance as they bid to keep their best players, which also includes Junior Kroupi and winger Rayan, who have attracted plenty of interest.

Man Utd ahead of Arsenal in Manu Kone race after opening transfer talks for £51m star READ MORE :

Scott's stock continued to rise throughout last season and he was selected in his first England squad last November and was then called up into Thomas Tuchel's extended pre-World Cup training camp in Florida.

‌



United are the club most heavily linked with the Bournemouth star given their desire to add to their midfield ranks. They've also prioritised adding Premier League-proven talent, but reports claim their attention has shifted to Manu Kone, the Roma midfielder who was hugely impressive for France at the World Cup.

View 2 Images Alex Scott's displays earned him England recognition

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023 for £25m and they would be able to demand a fee that far exceeds that if they did want to cash in. In recent years the Cherries have been prepared to sell their top assets for huge profits, but are determined to retain them this summer.

Article continues below

Midway through last season they sold Antoine Semenyo to Manchester City for £65m. That came after a summer where they cashed in on Milos Kerkez, who headed for Liverpool, and Dean Huijsen to Real Madrid.
