Sports.title: Mike Tyson Crushes Carl Williams In 93 Seconds
Sports.content:
Williams had earned the opportunity the hard way. The 6-foot-4 challenger was the IBF’s #1 contender after victories over Trevor Berbick and other leading heavyweights. He had also gone the distance with former champion Larry Holmes, and his height, long reach and jab were considered his best weapons against Tyson’s relentless pressure.

Promoted by Don King and televised by HBO, the championship attracted approximately 11,000 fans to Convention Hall. Tyson reportedly earned about $5 million, while Williams received roughly $1.2 million. Ringside tickets sold for $500, although the event generated a much smaller gate than Tyson’s previous blockbuster title defenses.

Williams tried to establish his jab immediately while tying Tyson up whenever the champion closed the distance. Tyson continued stalking forward, slipping punches and waiting for an opening.

That opening arrived barely more than a minute into the fight. Williams fired another left jab, Tyson slipped outside it and answered with a crushing left hook that landed flush on the jaw. Williams crashed backward to the canvas. He beat referee Randy Neumann’s count but remained unsteady as he leaned against the ropes. After asking Williams if he was able to continue and receiving no convincing response, Neumann stopped the fight at 1:33 of the opening round.

The decision immediately drew boos from the Atlantic City crowd. Williams protested the stoppage, insisting he was able to continue, and his camp unsuccessfully sought a rematch. No second meeting ever took place.

The victory improved Tyson’s championship reign with one of the quickest heavyweight title fights in history. It also became the final successful defense of his undisputed championship before Buster Douglas ended his reign in Tokyo on February 11, 1990. Although the ending remains controversial, Tyson’s explosive left hook and the disputed stoppage have kept the fight among the most discussed moments of his championship career.

Sports.title: Roy Jones Jr. Says Errol Spence Takes Over Late Against Tim Tszyu
Sports.content:
Jones Jr. said Tszyu’s best opportunity comes in the opening rounds before Spence settles into his rhythm.

“Man, it’s a hard call, but I’m going with Errol. Hope Errol can withstand the early start that Tszyu is going to probably put up early because if you get past four or five rounds, Errol definitely is going to beat him because Errol, to me, is stronger later than anybody fighting. You get him past round six, and you got a problem in your hand. I don’t care who it is, especially if he ain’t beat up or nothing in the face. You get to round six, you got a problem because that’s when he starts to come alive. Ask Ugas. Ask Brook,” Jones Jr. said to Fight Hub TV.

Roy Jr. compared Spence’s relentless style to Marvin Hagler’s, arguing that constant pressure eventually wears opponents down. He also pointed out that Spence has more technical ability than many people remember from his amateur days, even though he has relied primarily on pressure as a professional.

The matchup remains a difficult one because Tszyu is naturally aggressive and has never been afraid to trade punches. That style may create entertaining early rounds, but it also plays into the kind of fight Spence has often thrived in if he can avoid taking too much punishment at the start.

Jones Jr. believes surviving the opening rounds is the key. If Errol reaches the middle rounds without absorbing significant damage, he expects the former unified welterweight champion to begin taking control with steady pressure and superior stamina.

A victory over Tszyu would put Spence back in the title picture at 154 pounds after a three-year absence from the ring. A loss would leave him facing another setback at a point in his career when every fight carries added significance.

Sports.title: Salvador Sanchez’s Final Triumph: The Classic Battle With Azumah Nelson
Sports.content:
The bout carried significant championship stakes. Sanchez defended both the WBC featherweight championship and The Ring featherweight championship for the 10th time. Already established as one of boxing’s premier pound-for-pound fighters, the Mexican star had built his reputation with victories over Hall of Famers Danny Lopez, Wilfredo Gomez, Juan LaPorte and Roberto Castanon.

Nelson came in as the WBC’s #10-ranked featherweight contender after accepting the fight as a late replacement. Largely unknown to American fans, the 24-year-old Ghanaian had never faced anyone close to Sanchez’s level, and most observers expected another successful title defense for the champion.

The unfamiliar challenger hurt attendance. Only 5,575 fans paid to attend the event, producing a modest gate of $129,244 despite Don King serving as promoter. Sanchez, as the champion and established attraction, earned the larger purse. Nelson also received the biggest payday of his young career, although the official purse figures were never publicly disclosed. Veteran referee Tony Perez worked the bout.

What unfolded surprised nearly everyone. Instead of being overwhelmed, Nelson attacked Sanchez from the opening bell with relentless pressure. He fired hooks, overhand rights and body punches, forcing the champion into one of the toughest fights of his title reign. Nelson captured several early rounds with his aggression and briefly had Sanchez backing toward the ropes, something rarely seen during the champion’s prime.

Sanchez began making the necessary adjustments. Beginning in the middle rounds, his timing became sharper. He started landing crisp counter left hooks, straight rights and punishing body shots that slowed Nelson’s relentless attack.

In the seventh round, Sanchez scored the fight’s lone knockdown with a sharp left hook, but Nelson beat the count and survived the remainder of the round.

Sanchez closed the fight by landing the sharper combinations and investing to the body, gradually breaking down Nelson’s offense before the 15th-round stoppage.

The conclusion arrived in the 15th and final round. Sanchez trapped Nelson along the ropes and unloaded a sustained barrage of hooks and body shots. Nelson remained upright but was no longer defending himself effectively. At 1:49 of Round 15, Perez stepped in and stopped the contest, awarding Sanchez a technical knockout after one of the finest performances of both men’s careers.

Following the fight, Sanchez praised Nelson’s toughness, later describing him as one of the strongest and most durable opponents he had faced. The fight proved career-defining for both men.

It became the final chapter of an extraordinary career for Salvador after his death on August 12, 1982, in a Porsche crash that deprived boxing of one of its brightest young champions. Many historians still rank him among the greatest featherweights in history despite his short career.

The defeat for Nelson became a launching point rather than a setback. The defeat raised Nelson’s profile, and he went on to win world titles in three weight classes before being inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

Over four decades later, Sanchez-Nelson has grown in stature. What appeared to be a routine title defense during the summer of 1982 is now remembered as one of the finest featherweight championship fights ever contested and the unforgettable final masterpiece of Salvador Sanchez’s career.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Taunts Keyshawn Davis After WBO Purse Bid Order
Sports.content:
“Anybody seen Keyshawn Davis?” Bill Haney posted on X.

The WBO’s order gives Devin Haney a commanding 75/25 purse split as champion if negotiations fail and the fight goes to a purse bid. Instead of celebrating a mandatory title shot, Team Davis suddenly finds itself staring at a brutal financial reality.

As champion, Haney is entitled to 75% of the winning purse bid and has little incentive to give ground while the mandatory process favors him.

The order also changes the conversation surrounding Haney’s options. Before the WBO stepped in, most of the attention was on a fight with Shakur Stevenson. Now the mandatory defense against Davis takes priority, and the July 27 purse bid deadline gives both sides limited time to reach an agreement.

If no deal is reached, the winning bidder will secure promotional rights for the fight under the WBO’s 75/25 split. That reality leaves Team Davis with an important decision. They can either reach terms before the deadline or allow the purse bid process to determine where and under what promoter the fight takes place.

Team Haney has little reason to blink before July 27. The WBO’s order already gives Devin Haney the financial advantage, leaving the pressure on Team Davis to decide its next move.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco Looks Much Improved Against Immanuwel Aleem
Sports.content:
Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn told the media at the post-fight presser that Pacheco made a sensible decision choosing to wait for a title match, being that he had a new training team and Pacheco preferred to take the fight until he was ready at 100 percent.

Saturday night, a much-improved Pacheco boxed a much more technically sound fight by controlling the distance, utilizing his jab, and being defensively disciplined. Against Sadjo, Pacheco took a lot of punishment and also suffered the first knockdown of his professional career, but against Immanuwel Aleem (22-5-3, 14 KOs), he showed another level.

He landed 44.2 percent of his total punches, keeping Aleem at range with his jab. Immanuwel struggled to get on the inside and was offensively ineffective, finding minimal success connecting on only 24.1 percent of his total punches (Compubox).

WBC interim world super middleweight champion Lester Martinez (20-0-1, 16 KOs) fought Aleem to a close and hard-fought 12-round unanimous decision. Many believed he would be a much more challenging opponent for Diego, but he proved otherwise.

After the fight, Pacheco expressed to the media at the post-fight presser his desire to continue his progression and fight the best super middleweights in the world. He’d like fights against Jaime Munguia, Christian Mbilli, Hamzah Sheeraz, and Canelo Alvarez.

It’s only his first fight under Buddy, and his potential is limitless. He demonstrated Saturday night at the War Grounds he has the potential to challenge for a world title. Hearn said he hopes to have Pacheco fight at this venue again this year, around October or November, but will keep their options open if a big fight comes along.

Sports.title: Olympic Gold And Professional Glory: Champions Who Conquered Both
Sports.content:
Among the earliest examples was Frankie Genaro, who won Olympic flyweight gold in 1920 before claiming the NBA flyweight championship as a professional. The 1924 Games produced three future professional champions in Jackie Fields, Willie Smith, and Fidel LaBarba.

The post-war era continued the trend with Pascual Perez, Floyd Patterson, Nino Benvenuti, Joe Frazier, and George Foreman. Patterson became the youngest heavyweight champion in history at the time, while Foreman and Frazier carried their Olympic success into Hall of Fame careers.

The 1970s and 1980s produced another remarkable generation. Michael Spinks, Sugar Ray Leonard, Pernell Whitaker, Lennox Lewis, Ray Mercer, Henry Maske, Mark Breland, Meldrick Taylor, Frank Tate, Patrizio Oliva, Maurizio Stecca, Mate Parlov, Leo Randolph, Giovanni Parisi, and Kennedy McKinney all captured professional world titles after winning Olympic gold.

Oscar De La Hoya extended that tradition after the 1992 Barcelona Games, becoming one of boxing’s biggest attractions while winning titles in six weight classes.

The modern era has added Guillermo Rigondeaux, Andre Ward, Yuriorkis Gamboa, Vasiliy Lomachenko, Robeisy Ramirez, and Robson Conceição to the list. Ward retired undefeated after becoming the unified light heavyweight champion, while Lomachenko captured world titles in three weight classes after winning Olympic gold in both 2008 and 2012.

Not every Olympic champion reaches the top of the professional game, making this list a reminder of how difficult it is to dominate both amateur and professional boxing. While Olympic gold opens doors, history shows that only a relatively small percentage of champions have gone on to win recognized world titles in the paid ranks.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Admits Discipline Failed Him Before Steven Butler Fight
Sports.content:
“I feel like I was just getting by just because of my talent,” Berlanga said on Brian Custer’s channel. “What separated me from those guys was my dedication and my discipline. I always gave myself 50%. This camp has been different. The light switch turned on.”

What Berlanga isn’t saying is that what played a part in him being able to get by at only 50% is how he was managed. The early narrative was built on a shiny marketing gimmick: 16 straight first-round knockouts. Top Rank arguably spoon-fed him opponents selected specifically to keep the streak alive.

Once he stepped up into actual eight- and ten-rounders against basic step-up opponents like Demond Nicholson, Marcelo Coceres, Steve Rolls, and Roamer Alexis Angulo, the knockout power suddenly vanished. He was getting dropped, biting opponents out of frustration, and looking completely ordinary against basic journeymen.

Matchroom essentially bought into the hype to leverage his Puerto Rican fanbase in New York, giving him soft touches like Jason Quigley and Padraig McCrory to line him up for a massive payday against Canelo Alvarez.

When Berlanga finally stepped up to elite level, the reality caught up with him. Canelo Alvarez outclassed him across 12 rounds, dropping him along the way. Hamzah Sheeraz exposed the gap in level by stopping him inside five rounds.

Attributing his struggles entirely to “lack of discipline” or “giving 50%” is a classic promotional spin to protect a fighter’s brand. Lack of dedication may play a role, but the primary reason he looked invincible early on was careful matchmaking hiding serious technical limitations, limitations that got punished the second he stepped in with elite competition.

“I want to change the perspective of people,” Berlanga said. “I want to be talked about like Bam Rodriguez, Shakur Stevenson… that I got skill, IQ. I owe it to myself.”

Comparing himself to operators like Crawford, Shakur, or Bam is completely disconnected from who he is in the ring.

Those guys are elite, generational defensive technicians and sweet scientists with master-level footwork, ring vision, and distance control. Berlanga is an aggressive brawler who relies on raw athleticism, wild power, and intimidating his opponents. You do not wake up at 29 years old after a decade of fighting as a crude slugger and suddenly develop elite IQ, nuanced defense, or counter-punching instincts just because you worked hard in one training camp.

It is one thing when a fighter is just spouting promotional buzzwords to hype a fight, but it is another thing entirely when they genuinely convince themselves of it. In boxing, that kind of delusion is dangerous.

Berlanga spent years being told he was an unstoppable monster while blasting out overmatched opponents in one round. That level of early praise distorts a fighter’s self-image.

Now, facing the reality of his technical limits, his brain is reaching for the easiest explanation: “I just wasn’t trying hard enough.” Accepting that you just lacked effort is a lot easier on the ego than accepting that you simply do not have the natural ring IQ, reflexes, or skill ceiling of a Crawford or a Shakur. If it was just a lack of discipline, it means the talent is still there waiting to be unlocked.

Sports.title: Lamont Roach Jr. Still Eyes Tank Davis Before Zepeda Fight
Sports.content:
“I’ve been moved on from a rematch with Davis, but if it presents itself, then obviously we’ll take it. You know, I really want to get what I deserve on paper. Even though I did it before, on paper I’d like that,” said Lamont Roach to DAZN.

Roach’s position is understandable. Many boxing fans felt he deserved the decision in his first fight with Tank, and a rematch would give him the chance to settle the issue officially.

Lamont followed that performance with another draw, leaving him without the type of win that would strengthen his position in negotiations for another marquee fight. Instead of rebuilding his leverage, he’s remained stuck while continuing to mention Tank and Shakur as preferred opponents.

Zepeda is one of the busiest pressure fighters in the lightweight division, and Roach will need one of the best performances of his career to beat him on August 1. A loss would leave him even farther from either Tank or Shakur.

Neither fight is close to becoming reality. Tank has other high-profile options available whenever he returns, and Shakur has repeatedly talked about Devin Haney and other major names since signing with Zuffa Boxing.

Roach may believe he already earned another opportunity against Tank, but boxing rarely works that way. Beating Zepeda is the only result that moves him closer to either fight. Another draw or a loss leaves him with even less leverage than he has now.

Ghana News.title: OSP disputes interpretation of US immigration court proceedings involving Ofori-Atta
Ghana News.content:
Logo of OSP

The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has rejected reports suggesting that a United States immigration court has dismissed its criminal allegations against former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta, insisting that the widely circulated account misrepresents both the facts and the legal processes involved.

In response to media reports based on a purported transcript of proceedings before a US immigration court, a source at the OSP said the office was not prosecuting Mr Ofori-Atta before any American court and had no role in his reported detention by US immigration authorities.

"The portrayal is inaccurate and risks misleading the public," the source said.

The clarification follows widespread reports that a US Immigration Judge ruled the OSP had failed to provide credible evidence linking Mr Ofori-Atta to criminal wrongdoing in Ghana while considering his application for permanent residency.

According to the OSP source, Mr Ofori-Atta's reported detention in the United States was linked solely to his immigration status and not to any action taken by the anti-corruption agency.

"Mr Ofori-Atta was not arrested or detained at the request of the Office of the Special Prosecutor. He was taken into custody by the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) pursuant to U.S. immigration laws relating to his immigration status," the statement said.

It stressed that it has "neither the legal authority nor the operational capacity to direct or procure immigration detention by U.S. authorities."

The source further emphasised that US immigration proceedings are entirely separate from extradition proceedings and criminal prosecutions.

"The existence of criminal proceedings in Ghana does not, in itself, constitute the legal basis for immigration detention in the United States," he noted.

He also disclosed that Ghana's request for Mr Ofori-Atta's extradition has not yet reached the judicial stage in the United States.

He said the extradition request submitted by the Office of the Attorney-General and the OSP is still undergoing executive review by the US Department of Justice, including requests for supplementary documentation and authentication where required.

"It has not yet been placed before a U.S. extradition court for judicial determination," he said.

He further pointed out that Mr Ofori-Atta's own legal team has publicly acknowledged that they are yet to receive a formal extradition complaint or supporting court processes from US authorities.

He cautioned against interpreting the purported immigration court transcript as a determination of the criminal allegations pending against the former minister in Ghana.

He stressed that three distinct legal processes must not be conflated: US immigration proceedings, extradition proceedings and the substantive criminal prosecution before Ghanaian courts.

"Any narrative suggesting that a U.S. court has already commenced hearing the merits of Ghana's criminal allegations, or that an immigration judge is adjudicating the OSP's criminal case, is inconsistent with the established legal process governing extradition between sovereign states," he noted.

He also urged the public and the media to exercise caution in relying on documents whose authenticity has not been independently verified.

"The transcript currently circulating has not, to public knowledge, been authenticated by the Executive Office for Immigration Review, the U.S. Department of Justice, or any official court source," he claimed.

He concluded by urging that ongoing legal processes be allowed to proceed without "distortion, sensationalism or misinformation," stressing that public confidence in the administration of justice depends on verified facts rather than speculation.

Ghana News.title: MMDAs urged to prosecute illegal land sellers
Ghana News.content:
Gifty Nyarko — National President, LoGSAPP

Metropolitan, Municipal, and District Assemblies (MMDAs) have been urged to prosecute persons who sell land without the legally required Land Use Certificate to curb the illegal sale of wetlands, watercourses, and floodplains.

The National President of the Local Government Service Association of Physical Planners (LoGSAPP), Gifty Nyarko, said although climate change contributed to flooding, weak enforcement of the Land Use and Spatial Planning Act, 2016 (Act 925) remained a major driver of indiscriminate development in environmentally sensitive areas.

She told the Daily Graphic that strict enforcement of Sections 96 and 97 of Act 925 would reduce flooding, environmental degradation, land disputes, and the destruction of lives and property.

Ms Nyarko urged MMDAs to move beyond public education and consistently prosecute offenders, adding that firm enforcement of Sections 96 and 97 of Act 925 would deter illegal land transactions, protect wetlands and watercourses, and promote safer, more resilient, and sustainable communities.

Legal obligations

Ms Nyarko, who is also the Head of the Physical Planning Department of the Nkoranza South Municipal Assembly, explained that Section 96 of Act 925 prohibits the sale, lease, or transfer of land unless the seller can demonstrate that it had been properly zoned or rezoned for its intended use.

She said the law also required sellers to ensure the land conforms to approved land use and to attach evidence of the approved zoning to every transfer or conveyance.

Ms Nyarko said the provisions place clear legal obligations on chiefs, family heads, private landowners, estate developers, land agents, and all persons involved in land transactions.

She expressed concern that although the law had been in force since 2016, many assemblies had failed to enforce it, allowing wetlands, watercourses, floodplains, road reservations, and other protected lands to be sold for development.

Ms Nyarko urged MMDAs to educate chiefs on the provisions of Act 925, explaining that while traditional authorities played an important role in land administration, many were unfamiliar with the law.

She stressed that chiefs and customary landowners should allocate land only in conformity with approved structure plans or local plans, explaining that ownership of land did not automatically confer the right to allocate or develop it for any purpose.

Ghana News.title: Vehicle smoke contains cancer-causing agents – Health Experts warn
Ghana News.content:
Smoke from vehicle exhaust contains cancer-causing substances, health experts have warned, as a new study reveals that air pollution has become one of Ghana’s leading causes of death, claiming more than 30,000 lives annually.

The warning comes amid growing concerns over deteriorating air quality across Ghana, where pollution levels in several communities exceed national and international safety standards.

Researchers and public health experts are calling for stricter enforcement of vehicle emission regulations, improved urban planning, and increased public awareness to reduce pollution and prevent thousands of avoidable deaths linked to respiratory diseases, cardiovascular conditions, and cancer.

Air pollution has emerged as a major public health challenge in Ghana, driven by rapid urbanisation, an increasing number of vehicles, open waste burning, industrial activities, and the widespread use of biomass fuels.

According to a recent study conducted by PSS Urbania Consult, with support from the Clean Air Fund, pollution-related illnesses now account for more annual deaths than malaria, HIV/AIDS, and road traffic accidents combined. The findings highlight the urgent need for coordinated action by government, local authorities, and citizens to tackle the growing threat.

Speaking on the issue, Dr Kwadwo Ansong, Deputy Director at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research–Savanna Agricultural Research Institute (CSIR-SARI), warned that vehicle exhaust fumes contain polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), which are classified as carcinogenic by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

“The smoke from cars contains polycyclic hydrocarbons, PAHs, that can cause cancer. In Germany, there is a company called TÜV that checks vehicles with smoky exhausts. I urge the DVLA to put stringent measures in place to reduce smoke emissions into the atmosphere,” he said.

Dr Ansong also urged vehicle owners to take responsibility for properly maintaining their engines to prevent excessive emissions.

The study identified major sources of air pollution in Ghana as vehicular emissions, open waste burning, the use of firewood, pesticide use in farming, and dust generated from road construction activities. The findings also highlighted the deteriorating air quality situation in the Greater Accra Region.

Senior Urban Planner and Managing Partner of PSS Urbania Consult Ltd, Joseph Ayitio, advised Metropolitan, Municipal, and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to implement measures aimed at reducing air pollution in their respective areas.

The Public Health Director of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA), Mrs Florence Kuukyi, said the Assembly had introduced measures to monitor and address the pollution challenge.

“We have received support to install low-cost sensors across Accra to monitor air pollution levels and intervene where necessary. We are also implementing measures to decongest traders operating close to roadsides, as this contributes to traffic congestion and increases emissions. We are working to reduce this,” she said.

Experts warn that without urgent and sustained interventions, the health and economic burden associated with air pollution will continue to worsen.

This report was produced in collaboration with New Narratives, with funding from the Clean Air Fund.

Ghana News.title: No Ebola outbreak in Ghana — Health Ministry dismisses false SABC report
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Health has dismissed as false and misleading reports claiming that Ghana has recorded 2,300 Ebola cases and 930 deaths, assuring the public that the country has not registered a single case of the disease.

The Ministry's response follows the circulation of a publication attributed to the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), which claimed on its news ticker that Ebola infections in Ghana had surged, allegedly forcing consumers to reduce purchases of fresh produce.

In a statement on Tuesday, July 21, the Ministry said the publication was inaccurate and urged the public to disregard the figures, stressing that Ghana remains free of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD).

"The Ministry wishes to state unequivocally that Ghana has not recorded any case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD). The figures being circulated are false, misleading, and should be disregarded," the statement said.

The Ministry explained that recent visits by the Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, to the country's points of entry, laboratories and treatment facilities formed part of Ghana's routine public health preparedness and should not be misconstrued as evidence of an Ebola outbreak.

It said the inspections were intended to strengthen the country's capacity to prevent and respond promptly to any potential public health emergency, consistent with established disease surveillance and emergency preparedness measures.

According to the Ministry, such precautionary exercises are standard public health interventions and do not indicate the presence of Ebola in the country.

The Ministry therefore urged Ghanaians to remain calm and avoid circulating unverified reports capable of causing unnecessary fear and panic.

It advised the public to rely exclusively on information issued by the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service on matters relating to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies.

The Ministry further reiterated its commitment to protecting public health through continuous surveillance, preparedness and timely dissemination of accurate information, while cautioning against the spread of misinformation that could undermine public confidence and create unwarranted anxiety.

Ghana News.title: 20 acres of illegal mining-degraded land reclaimed at Nweneso following National Security clampdown
Ghana News.content:
About 20 acres of land degraded by illegal mining have been reclaimed at Nweneso No. 1 and No. 2 in the Atwima Kwanwoma District of the Ashanti Region, following a two-week suspension of all mining activities ordered by national security in the Ashanti Region.

The directive, issued two weeks ago after an inspection of the enclave, required all miners to halt operations and begin reclaiming degraded lands as part of efforts to restore the environment and prevent further destruction.

Some illegal miners operating at Nweneso No. 1 and No. 2 have complied with the directive by filling abandoned pits and restoring portions of the degraded land for plantation and vegetation purposes.

To assess compliance, the Atwima Kwanwoma District Security Council, together with officials from the Environmental Department and members of the media, toured several illegal mining sites in the area. The inspection revealed that significant progress has been made in reclaiming portions of the affected land.

Chairman of the District Committee Kingston Opoku Bediako, overseeing the reclamation of abandoned galamsey pits, said the committee would continue to conduct regular inspections to ensure all degraded lands are restored.

“It is the vision of the district chief executive to ensure that all abandoned galamsey pits are reclaimed to prevent future tragedies. We will not abandon this exercise after today. We will continue to monitor the sites regularly to ensure the reclamation works are sustained,” he said.

Mr. Opoku Bediako warned that anyone found engaging in illegal mining activities on restored sites would face the full rigours of the law.

The Atwima Kwanwoma District Environmental Officer, Ernest Boakye, expressed satisfaction with the progress made so far, describing the reclamation exercise as a major step toward restoring the district’s degraded environment.

According to him, the reclaimed lands will be used for tree planting and other vegetation restoration programmes to improve biodiversity and protect the ecosystem.

“This is the kind of progress we expect to see at all illegal mining sites. Reclaiming degraded lands is essential to restoring our environment. I therefore urge all illegal miners in the district to cooperate with the authorities and support the reclamation efforts,” he stated.

The reclamation exercise at Nweneso No. 1 and No. 2 is being undertaken with the support of Danmark Prime Company Limited, the firm contracted to carry out the restoration works.

The company’s Operations Manager, Robert Dambo, said about 20 acres had already been reclaimed, with plans to restore additional degraded lands before the end of the year.

“We appeal to everyone to support the government's efforts to restore our degraded lands. Land reclamation is highly capital-intensive, so continuous monitoring and adequate security are needed to prevent illegal miners from returning to destroy the reclaimed sites,” he said.

The inspection team was joined by officials from the national security apparatus in the Atwima Kwanwoma District.

The District Liaison Officer for National Security, Bernard Kofi Ampofo, commended the level of compliance by some miners, noting that the directive had yielded positive results.

“We are impressed with the level of compliance so far. But those who fail to comply with the directive should be prepared because we will come after them,” he cautioned.

Ghana News.title: Konongo-Odumase residents give gov’t one-month ultimatum to complete bypass project
Ghana News.content:
Frustration is mounting among residents of Konongo, Odumase and surrounding communities over the prolonged abandonment of the Konongo bypass road project.

The residents have served the government a one-month ultimatum to return to site and complete the project or face a massive demonstration that could disrupt traffic on the strategic Kumasi-Accra Highway.

According to them, the bypass project, announced under the Akufo-Addo administration, was expected to divert through traffic from the town and significantly reduce congestion on the busy highway.

However, years after work began, construction has stalled. They claim the contractor, Kofi Jobs Construction Company, is no longer on site, leaving the project incomplete.

Residents say the abandoned project has turned the highway into a daily nightmare, with motorists spending several hours in traffic while businesses suffer significant losses.

They also blame the delays for the increasing number of fatal crashes on the stretch.

Their concerns have intensified following last Wednesday's tragic accident at Odumase, where 13 people, including a five-year-old child, died instantly after three vehicles collided.

One resident claimed that ''more than 32 people have lost their lives in crashes on the Konongo-Odumase stretch in recent years'.''

He recounted the death of his apprentice, Akwesi Yamoah, who was knocked down by a vehicle, describing the incident as one of several tragedies that could have been prevented if the bypass had been completed.

The residents further lamented the poor condition of the link roads, while describing sections of the ECOWAS highway as a death trap because of deep potholes and deteriorating road surfaces.

They are, therefore, calling on the government to immediately resume construction of the bypass and rehabilitate the affected roads to improve safety and ease traffic congestion.

One of the organisers of the planned demonstration, Pascal Kwaku Oppong, says the agitation is driven by public frustration and not political affiliation.

Mr Oppong, who says he once composed a campaign song for the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), insists the youth have moved beyond partisan politics in their demand for a safer road.

"We are tired of the politics and the endless promises. People are dying while leaders continue to debate. If nothing is done within the one-month ultimatum, we will block the Kumasi-Accra Highway until government acts," he warned.

The residents say they remain united in their demand for the immediate completion of the Konongo bypass, warning that any further delay could result in a major protest that would disrupt movement along one of the country's busiest highways.

Ghana News.title: US launches fresh strikes on Iran, as Trump warns of retaliation for deaths of soldiers
Ghana News.content:
The US military says it launched another round of strikes against Iran to "further degrade" its capabilities to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The strikes - the 10th consecutive night of attacks - come after US President Donald Trump vowed to punish Iran for the deaths of US soldiers.

In response, Iran saidit struck two oil tankers in the waterway, as well as US military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, state news agency IRNA reported.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now fighting a "full-scale war" with the US. Trump earlier said Iran had been hit "very hard" the previous night "in honour" of three US soldiers killed recently - two in Jordan and one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest strikes had hit Iranian "military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems".

Explosions were reported near the north-western city of Tabriz, where state media said one person was killed and several wounded, as well at the Gulf ports of Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini and the south-eastern ports of Chabahar and Konarak.

Centcom also insisted that commercial vessels were continuing to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran meanwhile said its forces struck two oil tankers as they attempted to transit through what it called the strait's "unsafe and hazardous southern route" and rescue teams were picking up their crews, according to state media.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz had reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

It was not clear whether the tanker reported by UKMTO was among those cited by Iran.

Six fuel tankers and cargo ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to preliminary data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler. Two of these vessels had previously been sanctioned by the US for links with Iran.

This is down from eight vessels crossing on July 19, the data shows. All but one of the crossings made on July 20 were via the northern route near Iran.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also claimed to have targeted a data centre belonging to the US company Amazon in Bahrain, according to state media on Tuesday.

The IRGC "attacked and destroyed the central data infrastructure of the American company Amazon in Bahrain with several cruise missiles," state news agency IRNA reported.

Jordan said on Tuesday that it had intercepted five drones after saying it had shot down three missiles late on Monday. Bahrain said drones launched by Iran had targeted its air navigation systems - but traffic remained unaffected. Kuwait's armed forces also said they had intercepted Iranian drones.

At the same time, Tehran said diplomatic messages were still being exchanged by both sides through intermediaries, despite a collapse of a ceasefire.

On Monday night the Department of Defense confirmed the identities of two of the US soldiers – Pte Isabella Gonzales, 19, from Texas, and Lt Tyler James Feehan, 25, from Hawaii - who were killed in an Iranian strike on the Muwaffaq Salti base in Jordan over the weekend.

Centcom said earlier a third service member also went missing in action after the attack, and unidentified remains were later found in the area.

Ghana News.title: IFRIG seals landmark partnerships with Malaysia, Indonesia Universities to boost non-interest banking
Ghana News.content:
The Islamic Finance Research Institute of Ghana (IFRIG) has taken a bold step toward transforming the country’s financial landscape, signing two strategic Memorandums of Understanding with top-tier Asian universities during a historic training tour of Malaysia.

The agreements, inked in Kuala Lumpur, pair IFRIG with Malaysia’s International Islamic University of Malaysia (IIUM) and Indonesia’s University of Darussalam Gontor.

The move is designed to accelerate non-interest banking and finance education, promote joint research, and strengthen professional capacity-building among Ghana’s financial regulators.

Speaking to the press, IFRIG’s Executive Director, Dr. Ali Shuaib, described the partnerships as a game-changer for Ghana’s regulatory ecosystem.

“This MOU is not just a formality. It is about building the capacity of our financial regulators and deepening the relationship between IFRIG and these universities in terms of research, scholarships, and knowledge exchange,” Dr. Shuaib said.

The training tour, which marked IFRIG’s maiden overseas capacity-building programme, brought together key financial regulators from Ghana to engage with global best practices in non-interest banking and finance.

Representing IIUM, Vice Rector of the School, Prof. Dr. Aslam Mohammed Hanif, welcomed the collaboration and expressed optimism about future joint initiatives.

“We look forward to deeper collaboration and meaningful outcomes that will benefit both institutions and the wider financial community,” he noted.

From Indonesia, Prof. Dr. Hamid Fahmy Zarkasyi of the University of Darussalam Gontor also reaffirmed his institution’s commitment, promising that the university would provide the necessary training and resources for all beneficiaries in the coming years.

Why this matters for Ghana

As Ghana continues to expand its financial inclusion agenda, non-interest banking offers a viable alternative for individuals and businesses seeking ethical, Sharia-compliant financial products. These international partnerships are expected to equip local regulators with the expertise needed to oversee and grow the sector responsibly.

For Ghanaian students and professionals, the agreements also open doors to scholarship opportunities and joint research collaborations with two of the world’s most respected Islamic finance institutions.

What’s next?

IFRIG has indicated that the next phase will involve structured training modules, faculty exchanges, and possible curriculum development for Ghana’s financial institutions. With these new alliances, Ghana is positioning itself as a rising hub for non-interest finance in West Africa.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: India’s ‘cockroach’ protest movement halts marches after police violence
World.content:
Leaders of the movement say they will continue campaigning but will not stage another march through New Delhi.

Leaders of India’s “cockroach movement” say they will continue to protest against the government but will refrain from further rallies through the streets of New Delhi because of concerns about the safety of their supporters after a violent police response when more than 10,000 people tried to march to parliament.

“We will not march again because the police will hurt the youth again,” Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said at a news conference on Tuesday.

He said 150 protesters were wounded by police who fired tear gas and beat activists with canes and batons during Monday’s march.

The movement will continue to demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who it said must be held accountable for flaws in the education system.

The movement emerged after a leak of exam papers that forced 2.2 million aspiring doctors to retake their exams, reportedly contributing to at least 12 students dying by suicide. The CJP is calling for compensation of 10 million rupees ($104,000) for each family of the students who took their own lives after the leak.

“We won’t stop. Pradhan has to be sacked,” the CJP’s Ashutosh Ranka said.

⁠Opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and his ⁠sister Priyanka along with members ⁠of their Indian National Congress party, staged a protest outside Prime Minister Narendra ‌Modi’s house, videos shared by the party showed on Tuesday.

“We have marched to PM ⁠Modi’s house to ⁠demand answers from him for the brutalities against ⁠young students yesterday,” ⁠Rahul Gandhi posted ⁠on X.



The rights group Amnesty International said in a statement late on Monday that the police action showed “how peaceful dissent is being suppressed in India.”

“They beat us black and blue, and they damaged our protest site,” Sahil Singh, a protester from the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, told the Reuters news agency. “We want accountability to be set with Pradhan’s resignation.”

The number of protesters who marched on Monday was larger than expected, partly due to widespread anger after veteran 59-year-old activist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on hunger strike for three weeks in solidarity with the CJP, was seized by police and hospitalised against his will.

The Delhi ⁠High ⁠Court ruled on Tuesday that Wangchuk could be moved ⁠from a government hospital to a private healthcare facility after his ⁠wife petitioned the court, alleging he was being held in “illegal detention”, the legal news website Bar and Bench ‌said.

About 200 protesters gathered at the CJP protest site at Jantar Mantar in central New Delhi on Tuesday morning, chanting slogans under a monsoon drizzle.

Paramilitary personnel continued to patrol central parts of India’s capital, and barricades were restricting traffic.

Delhi police said nearly 180 people – 60 protesters and 118 security and police personnel – were injured in Monday’s clashes. Police also said 70 protesters were detained and legal action would be initiated against them.

Multiple videos of Monday’s clashes show police attacking protesters, but no footage has emerged of any violence by the marchers.

The CJP and its supporters remain hopeful that they may change the status quo. A representative said on Monday that a federal minister had promised the government would consider their demands.

On Tuesday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said: “I think when the talks are going on in a right direction, the atmosphere should not be vitiated.”

The CJP’s campaign initially began online with viral satirical memes mocking the government, and it quickly amassed millions of followers on social media. It has since morphed into a movement able to mobilise thousands on the streets, as Monday’s march demonstrated.

After the chief justice of India’s Supreme Court likened some unemployed young people to “cockroaches”, the protesters adopted the insult as the name of their movement.

World.title: Hunger is falling but is still higher than pre-COVID levels: UN report
World.content:
Global hunger has declined, yet millions of people are still going hungry.

The number of hungry people around the world is falling.

According to the latest United Nations State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World report, an estimated 645 million people faced hunger in 2025, 14 million fewer than in 2024 and 43 million fewer than 2022.

Yet hundreds of millions continue to face acute food shortages driven by conflict, economic shocks and climate extremes.

Gradual improvement

According to the report published on Tuesday, an estimated 7.8 percent of the world’s population experienced hunger in 2025, down from 8.1 percent in 2024 and 8.6 percent in 2022.

The decline marks a third consecutive year of improvement after hunger surged during the COVID-19 pandemic. But hunger levels still remain higher than they were in 2019 before the pandemic struck.

Where do the most hungry people live?

Africa remains the world’s hunger hotspot.

In 2025, an estimated 309 million people in Africa were undernourished – equivalent to one in five people on the continent and representing almost half of the world’s hungry people.

By comparison, 292 million people in Asia (6 percent of the population) and 32 million in Latin America and the Caribbean (4.8 percent) experienced undernourishment.

According to the report, Asia and Latin America and the Caribbean have made steady progress in reducing both the share and the number of people facing hunger in recent years.

In Africa, the long-running rise in hunger appears to have stalled. The prevalence of hunger fell slightly from 20.3 percent in 2024 to 20 percent in 2025 although population growth meant the total number of hungry people continued to increase.



Looking ahead, the UN projects that the global number of undernourished people will fall by about 20 percent by 2030 compared with current estimates.

Even so, 510 million to 520 million people are still expected to face hunger by the end of the decade with 56 percent of them living in Africa.

The report also warned that recent crises, including the 2026 US-Israel war on Iran, could undermine progress, particularly in Africa and Asia.

Who is unable to afford a healthy diet?

According to the report, the number of people unable to afford a healthy diet fell from 2.97 billion in 2021 (37.4 percent of the global population) to 2.69 billion in 2025 (32.7 percent).

The decline suggested that, on average, people’s available income for food increased faster than the cost of a healthy diet.

However, the cost of eating healthily continues to rise. The global cost of a healthy diet reached $4.28 per day, using purchasing power parity, in 2025, up from $3.44 in 2021 and $2.94 in 2017.

Despite global improvements, affordability remains a major challenge in Africa and Asia. While Asia has the largest number of people unable to afford a healthy diet at 1.4 billion, or 29 percent of its population, Africa faces the highest rate with 1.03 billion people, or nearly two-thirds of the population, unable to afford nutritious food.

In Latin America and the Caribbean, about 172 million people are affected (26 percent of the population), compared with 77.5 million in Europe and North America (7 percent of the population) and 2.3 million in Oceania (5 percent of the population). The figures underscored persistent inequalities in access to nutritious food across regions.

Compared with 2021, the share of people unable to afford a healthy diet increased in Africa while it declined in Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Northern America and Europe.

What is a healthy diet basket?

According to the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Bank, a healthy diet basket is the lowest-cost combination of locally available foods that meets a person’s daily energy needs and provides most essential nutrients required for a healthy diet.

It is made up of 11 food items from six food groups, providing about 2,330 kilocalories per person per day while maintaining the recommended balance of foods needed for adequate nutrition.



How many people are facing catastrophic levels of hunger?

While global hunger levels have declined in recent years, millions of people in the Global South continue to face acute food shortages, driven by conflict, economic shocks and climate-related extremes.

A separate report published by the FAO and World Food Programme, the Global Report on Food Crises 2026, estimated about 1.4 million people worldwide are facing catastrophic hunger, the most severe phase of the five-phase IPC/CH food security classification scale.

IPC/CH is the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification/Cadre Harmonise, a global system that classifies the severity of food insecurity from Phase 1 (minimal) to Phase 5 (catastrophe/famine).

Catastrophic hunger occurs when households have exhausted all means to survive and face an extreme lack of food and basic needs. At this stage, starvation, acute malnutrition, destitution and death become widespread, requiring immediate action to prevent further loss of life.

Gaza has the largest number of people facing catastrophic hunger with about 640,700 people, representing 32 percent of its population. The crisis has been intensified by the impact of Israel’s genocidal war on the enclave and restrictions on the entry and distribution of humanitarian aid by the Israeli military.

“While markets are more stocked compared with this time last year, many families cannot afford to buy enough food due to the loss of income and the extremely difficult economic situation,’ says Maram Humaid, an Al Jazeera reporter who reports from Gaza.

“The closure of many community kitchens has further exacerbated the situation, removing an important source of support for thousands of people who relied on free cooked meals.”

Sudan follows closely behind Gaza with 637,200 people experiencing catastrophic hunger although they account for about 1 percent of the country’s population. Other countries reporting people in this extreme category include South Sudan (83,500 people), Yemen (41,200), Haiti (8,400) and Mali (2,600).

World.title: Hamas’s new leader must bridge a movement divided over Iran
World.content:
Khalil al-Hayya’s election as the new head of Hamas is far more than the filling of a position left vacant by war. Decided by a single vote after nearly two years of collective leadership, it reveals the divisions within a movement transformed by exile, regional upheaval and its increasingly consequential relationship with Iran.

Al-Hayya, Yahya Sinwar’s former deputy in Gaza and a member of the five-person council that has led Hamas since Sinwar’s killing in October 2024, defeated former political bureau chief Khaled Meshaal in a 35-34 vote. That razor-thin result encapsulates the central question now facing Hamas: whether it can reunite its competing currents or whether al-Hayya’s victory will consolidate the influence of the camp most closely aligned with Tehran.

From Gaza to the diaspora

When Hamas was established in December 1987, who stood at the head of the movement mattered far less than it does today. Its leadership structure was considerably simpler before growing more complex over the following two decades.

Although formally born in Gaza, the Islamic Resistance Movement, known by its Arabic acronym Hamas, was the joint project of several organisations operating under the umbrella of the Bilad al-Sham, or Levant, branch of the Muslim Brotherhood. These included Muslim Brotherhood organisations in Gaza, the occupied West Bank and Jordan as well as affiliates across the diaspora, particularly in Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

Initially, the leadership of the Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza exercised overall control. Like Muslim Brotherhood organisations elsewhere, it was governed by an elected Shura Council representing different parts of the Gaza Strip. The council, in turn, elected an executive office from among its members.



It was this executive office that met on December 9, 1987, and decided to transform the Muslim Brotherhood’s organisation in Gaza into the Islamic Resistance Movement. Its members were Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, Abdulaziz al-Rantissi, Salah Shihada, Abdulfattah Dukhan, Muhammad Sham’ah, Ibrahim al-Yazuri and Issa al-Nashar.

That leadership model was soon disrupted by Israeli repression. After Hamas declared responsibility for several resistance operations, the Israeli occupation forces launched a series of severe crackdowns against it. A mass detention campaign deprived the movement of virtually all its first- and second-tier leaders.

The crackdown alarmed Hamas’s support networks outside Palestine. Mousa Abu Marzouk, who had been studying for a doctorate in the United States, was sent to Gaza to salvage what remained of the badly battered organisation.

The growing role of Hamas’s external support apparatus in rebuilding the movement marked the beginning of a transfer of leadership from Gaza to the diaspora. Abu Marzouk later moved to Jordan and became the head of the movement’s political bureau, remaining in the position until he was arrested at John F Kennedy International Airport upon returning to the US in 1995. Khaled Meshaal succeeded him and was subsequently re-elected several times, remaining head of the political bureau until 2017.

A structure that deepened internal divisions

Under Meshaal, Hamas reorganised its leadership into three principal constituencies. Gaza, the West Bank and the diaspora. Each had an elected local Shura Council and its own executive leadership.

The intention was to decentralise decision-making and establish a clearer division of labour. Inevitably, however, the new structure also produced a growing bureaucracy, duplicated mandates, conflicting interests and recurring disputes between the movement’s different branches.

Hamas’s removal from Jordan in the late 1990s initially appeared to be a blessing in disguise. During the 11 years that followed when its leadership was based in Damascus, the movement considerably expanded its international relations.

It was during this period that the so-called axis of resistance, comprising Iran, Syria, Hezbollah and Palestinian groups, including Hamas and Islamic Jihad, began to take shape. With most Arab governments identifying with the opposing camp, commonly described at the time as the “axis of moderation”, Hamas’s alliance with and growing reliance on Iran appeared increasingly inevitable.

Since the early 1990s, Iran has sought, with limited success, to turn Hamas into a proxy similar to Hezbollah and, to some extent, Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Throughout the Meshaal era, however, Hamas maintained a significant degree of independence despite accepting Iranian financial and military assistance.



The Arab Spring rupture

That relationship was severely tested by the Arab Spring. Hamas welcomed and supported the popular uprisings and rejected Iranian demands that it side with the Syrian government as it moved to suppress the revolution. The movement instead left Damascus for Doha, abandoning what some of its members in Syria considered the considerable privileges and political gains it had accumulated during the previous decade.

The departure from Damascus coincided with the end of Meshaal’s second and supposedly final term as head of the political bureau. The movement’s rules did not permit him to stand for another term, and his Gaza-based deputy, Ismail Haniyeh, expected to succeed him.

Meshaal was nevertheless persuaded by allies inside and outside Hamas that the regional circumstances made a leadership change inadvisable. A campaign was mounted to amend the rules and allow him to stand for a third term.

The rules were changed, and Meshaal was re-elected. But the decision produced a serious internal crisis and opened a rift between competing leadership currents that continued to deepen in the years that followed.

After the coup in Egypt and the success of the counterrevolution in crushing much of the Arab Spring, Hamas found itself under pressure from both sides. Arab governments opposed to the uprisings punished the movement for having supported them so unequivocally. Iran, meanwhile, punished Hamas for refusing to stand by the Syrian government.

By the time Haniyeh eventually succeeded Meshaal as head of the political bureau, the movement’s financial difficulties had become more severe. The diaspora branch, which was then headed by Meshaal, was deprived of much of the funding it needed to sustain its extensive organisational structure.

Iran increasingly dictated which parts of Hamas should benefit from its financial support, insisting that funds should not be made available to Meshaal’s team. In practice, this allowed Tehran to strengthen a pro-Iran current within Hamas while weakening the opposing current led by Meshaal.

Neither Sinwar’s subsequent rise to the overall leadership nor the collective leadership established after his killing resolved this underlying struggle.

Against this background, al-Hayya’s narrow victory will inevitably be interpreted in some quarters as a victory for the pro-Iran camp. Until a few years ago, that current represented only a small minority within the movement. It has since been strengthened by the perception that Iran is the only state in the region willing to support Hamas as well as by the belief among its advocates that Iran is emerging from the current US war stronger and more determined.

Yet the closeness of the result also demonstrates that Hamas remains deeply divided. Al-Hayya may have won the leadership, but a one-vote margin does not amount to a decisive mandate for one current to marginalise the other.

For those who judge leadership principally by charisma, Meshaal remains the more commanding figure. Hamas, however, has historically depended less on individual charisma than on clarity of vision and unity within its ranks.



Al-Hayya’s defining challenge

Al-Hayya’s greatest challenge will, therefore, not simply be to lead Hamas through an exceptionally difficult regional moment. It will be to work with his comrades to repair an internal rift that has developed over more than a decade, reunite the movement’s competing currents and preserve the clarity and independence of its political vision.

Whether he succeeds will determine whether this election becomes the beginning of renewed cohesion or another stage in the consolidation of one camp at the expense of the movement as a whole.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: ‘Won’t back down’: Indian student protesters return after police crackdown
World.content:
More than 100 students injured in police action against thousands of demonstrators during march on parliament. But students say they aren’t done – just like the cockroaches India’s chief justice compared them to.

New Delhi, India – Blood spots on the walls, overturned barricades, shattered mirrors and sandals strewn across the road. A scarf here, broken glasses and a torn shirt there lie as remnants of the chaos that took over the Indian capital.
