World.title: Gachagua accuses IEBC of bias ahead of Ol Kalou by-election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Gachagua wants IEBC to commit to conducting the Ol Kalou by-election in a free, fair, and credible manner.

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) of bias and demanded assurances that Thursday's Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election will be conducted in a free, fair and credible manner.

In a letter addressed to IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, Gachagua claimed the commission had lost public confidence and alleged it had selectively enforced electoral laws in favour of the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA).

He cited previous by-elections, including those in Malava, Mbeere North and Narok Town Ward, claiming the commission failed to act against alleged voter bribery, intimidation and violence involving politicians allied to the government.

Gachagua also questioned the commission's handling of disciplinary action against Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia, arguing she had been unfairly treated and denied due process.

The former Deputy President further alleged that senior government officials, including Cabinet Secretaries, Principal Secretaries and other state officers, had actively campaigned for the UDA candidate in Ol Kalou without attracting sanctions from the electoral commission.

He raised concerns about the integrity of the July 16 poll, claiming he had received information from a meeting allegedly held on July 13 that involved UDA officials, government officers and political leaders.

According to Gachagua, discussions at the meeting allegedly centred on plans to interfere with the electoral process.

Among the allegations, he claimed there were plans to delay accreditation of DCP agents, postpone the opening of polling stations in opposition strongholds, issue double ballot papers to UDA supporters, permit voter bribery, deploy plain-clothes police officers to intimidate voters and agents, and interfere with vote counting through planned power outages.

He also alleged that police officers in civilian clothing would be deployed inside polling stations and that additional security personnel would be used to suppress opposition supporters and disrupt vote tallying.

At the same time, Gachagua questioned the commission's decision to rely solely on the electronic voter register, arguing that a manual register should remain available as a backup in line with a 2022 High Court ruling.

The DCP leader urged the IEBC to publicly confirm that all party agents would receive accreditation on time, polling stations would open as scheduled, ballot papers would be properly scrutinised, security agencies would remain impartial and all legal safeguards governing voting and vote counting would be observed.

He also accused police of failing to investigate several alleged incidents targeting DCP supporters and campaign teams in Ol Kalou, including assaults, destruction of campaign equipment and an alleged attempted assassination of former East African Legislative Assembly member Kanini Kega.

He warned that any irregularities in the by-election could undermine public confidence in the IEBC's ability to conduct the 2027 General Election.

"The Ol Kalou by-election is an acid test for the IEBC," Gachagua said, urging the commission to use the poll to restore public trust in Kenya's electoral process.

World.title: Wetang'ula risks jail over alleged breach of court orders on political campaigns
World.content:
National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula addresses residents in Bungoma County. [Bernard Lusigi, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a contempt application seeking to have National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula jailed for at least one month or fined Sh725,017 for each political engagement for allegedly violating conservatory orders issued on July 8, 2026.

Justice David Mburu ordered that a contempt of court application filed by Vocal Africa against Wetang'ula be fast-tracked over allegations that he continued to disobey court orders restraining him from participating in partisan political campaigns, including allegedly campaigning for President William Ruto's re-election.

World.title: Egypt tops 10 destinations for Uzbek tourists-Ambassador
World.content:
Uzbekistan’s Ambassador in Cairo Mansurbek Kilichev, said that Egypt has officially ranked among the top 10 favourite travel destinations for Uzbek tourists, with about 26,000 Uzbeks visiting the country during the first half of 2026, according to Uzbek statistics.

The ambassador, in statements on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, described the figure as “a remarkable achievement” that highlights the growing closeness between Egypt and Uzbekistan.

Uzbek visitors are drawn not only by Egypt’s world-class beach resorts and renowned hospitality, but also by the deep cultural, historical and spiritual ties linking the Egyptian and Uzbek peoples, making Uzbeks feel genuinely welcome in Egypt, Kilichev said.

He added that Uzbek tourists appreciate Egyptian hospitality and enjoy visiting the country’s historic landmarks, including the Pyramids and the ancient city of Luxor.

Kilichev said the noticeable increase in the number of Uzbek tourists visiting Egypt reflects the strong friendship and constructive dialogue between the leaderships of the two countries, which has helped facilitate smoother travel.

He said tourism growth has been strongly supported by an extensive air network, with direct and charter flights connecting Tashkent to Cairo, Sharm El-Sheikh and Hurghada.

Expressing his satisfaction with the latest figures, Kilichev said they represent only the beginning, noting that there is significant potential for further growth in the sector.

He said he expects the number of Uzbek tourists visiting Egypt to rise further by the end of 2026, adding that tourism serves as an ideal bridge for cultural exchange while naturally opening new opportunities for trade and economic partnerships as relations between the Egyptian and Uzbek peoples continue to deepen.

The ambassador said the embassy remains fully committed to supporting Egyptian and Uzbek travel partners to maintain this positive momentum.

According to the ambassador, the top 10 preferred destinations for Uzbek tourists are Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, China, Egypt and Vietnam.

World.title: Egypt chairs Arab group preparing for UN desertification talks
World.content:
Egypt’s Desert Research Center (DRC) took part in the 24th meeting of the Arab team responsible for following up on the UN conventions to combat desertification and conserve biodiversity, held at the Arab League headquarters in Cairo with the participation of representatives of Arab countries and regional and international organizations.

Ahmed Abdel Aty, Egypt’s Executive Coordinator for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), and Mohamed Youssef, coordinator of Egypt’s Fourth National Report, represented the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, the Desert Research Center and Egypt at the meeting.

The meeting aims to formulate a unified Arab position on key issues to be negotiated during the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17), scheduled to be held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in August.

At the opening session, Arab member states unanimously elected Abdel Aty as chairman of the Arab follow-up team for the UN conventions on desertification and biodiversity, reflecting confidence in Egyptian expertise and underscoring the leading role of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Desert Research Center in supporting joint Arab environmental action.

Under Egypt’s chairmanship, the Arab team is expected to discuss a number of strategic issues, including drought, land restoration, land degradation neutrality, financing, technology transfer, capacity building and stronger Arab coordination, with the aim of unifying Arab positions and advancing the region’s priorities during the international negotiations.

World.title: First lady meets Montenegro counterpart
World.content:
Egypt’s First Lady, Entissar al-Sisi, met with First Lady Milena Milatović of Montenegro during the latter’s official state visit to Egypt.

In a post on her official social media accounts, Egypt’s First Lady shared that they both toured the Diarna exhibition in El Alamein, describing it as a vibrant celebration of Egypt’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship.

She noted that the exhibition truly reflects the spirit of Egypt, showcasing the nation’s authentic heritage and its deep pride in its national identity.

World.title: FM: Egypt offers development expertise to deepen cooperation with Mozambique
World.content:
Egypt is ready to share its development expertise and provide technical support to Mozambique as the two countries seek to deepen bilateral cooperation, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty said on Monday.

Speaking at a joint press conference with his Mozambican counterpart, Maria Lucas, Abdelatty said Egyptian companies, which have played a key role in Egypt’s infrastructure and development drive, stand ready to contribute to Mozambique’s sustainable development efforts.

Abdelatty said the visit carries special significance as it coincides with the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Egypt and Mozambique, describing bilateral ties as being rooted in mutual trust and Egypt’s longstanding support for African liberation movements.

He said the talks focused on strengthening cooperation, particularly in the economic and investment sectors, and on advancing the outcomes of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s visit to Maputo in 2023.

The minister added that he had conveyed President al-Sisi’s invitation to the Mozambican president to visit Cairo later this year, with both sides agreeing to coordinate the timing of the visit as part of efforts to launch a new phase of their development partnership.

The two countries also agreed to accelerate preparations for the third session of the Egypt-Mozambique Joint Higher Committee, due to be held in Cairo.

Abdelatty said the relevant technical committees had been instructed to finalize pending agreements and memoranda of understanding ahead of the committee’s meeting.

World.title: White House rushes to further secure Trump’s new Air Force One — but he plans to keep flying it domestically
World.content:
The White House is working to quickly upgrade the Qatari-donated jet that has newly started serving as Air Force One, a development that comes after administration officials internally discussed the need for President Donald Trump to avoid flying it in high-threat areas, according to two sources familiar with the matter.

The extent of the required upgrades, which will be made later this fall, remains unclear. But the two sources said that before Trump traveled on the jet to Turkey earlier this month, officials had discussed the president not traveling on the newly refurbished jet to areas that could pose a higher risk to him, specifically Israel, amid the monthslong war with Iran.

Trump, who has lavished praise on the retrofitted plane, nevertheless flew it to Turkey earlier this month after an initial assessment by top officials deemed it safe, the sources said.

Officials later realized that clearing it for use on that trip was a mistake, one of the sources said. The other source noted that security assessments frequently change.

Trump has appeared to publicly acknowledge that the plane needs additional security enhancements, telling reporters Sunday that it would soon be “maxed out.” He added that it would “take about a month” to make the planned changes — a timeline experts say isn’t enough to make significant improvements.

When he left Turkey, Trump opted to take the older presidential plane rather than the newer jet, spurring scrutiny of its security deficiencies. Trump insisted at the time that the swap was so US service members at a UK air base could see the plane, not due to a lack of security measures. But two sources familiar with the matter previously told CNN the newer plane did not possess the same capabilities to ensure the president’s safety in international settings.

The subsequent reporting on safety concerns regarding the plane infuriated the president, spurring an extraordinary leak investigation that included subpoenaing the New York Times reporters who first reported on the issue. Officials at the White House has were also asked to turn over their phones as part of the probe.

On Monday, press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that the new jet was slated to undergo more work, even as she maintained that it was “perfectly safe.”

“The new Air Force One is perfectly safe for the President’s travels, but will receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete,” she said in a statement.

Trump is still expected to use the jet for domestic trips — and potentially even some international travel — before the upgrades, one of the sources familiar with the matter said, citing assessments that deemed it safe to take to low-risk destinations. That could include flying it to Ireland, where he’s considering a visit in September.

Trump has also suggested he could take the new jet to China later this year, amid discussions about a meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. But those plans are likely to hinge on completing all the upgrades in one month — an accelerated timeline that prompted immediate skepticism from aviation experts.

Richard Aboulafia, a managing director at AeroDynamic Advisory, told CNN that no significant improvement could reasonably be made to a plane in such a short period of time.

“But for 30 days there are a number of different pilot drink holder options they might want to pursue,” he joked.

The military took possession of the jet from Qatar last year, and the work that was done on it took a little over a year to complete.

“The amount of time they originally had was useful for scanning for security weaknesses and installing some basic equipment for communications and some limited level of self-protection,” said Aboulafia, who has served as an aviation analyst and consultant since 1988. “Getting up to the standards of the old Air Force One — that’s a couple years.”

The donated jet is meant to serve as a “bridge” plane to fill the role of Air Force One until Boeing finishes outfitting two new planes, which are slated for delivery in 2028. Boeing has spent nearly a decade designing and upgrading the two 747s.

“This is the most complex twin aisle aircraft we have ever done,” Boeing’s CEO Kelly Ortberg told CNBC Monday. “We are through the design phase and building the airplanes back up. So we are confident we know what we’ve got in front of us.”

Since Qatar gifted Trump the $400 million jet, its design and retrofitting has taken on outsized personal importance for the president, whose term would be mostly over by the time the new other planes are delivered, assuming the project remains on track. In the meantime, the White House roundly dismissed legal, ethical and national security questions surrounding its decision to accept the plane.

Trump hand-picked much of the interior details of the plane, sources told CNN, down to the flooring in each individual area. When he publicly unveiled the jet, he deemed it “the world’s most luxurious plane.”

“Frankly, we couldn’t build a plane like this because we wouldn’t be willing to spend the kind of money necessary,” Trump said ahead of its inaugural flight earlier this month, as he took reporters on a tour of its gold-accented cabin. “They spent top dollars.”

World.title: Bodies recovered after passenger ferry carrying over 100 people sinks off Guyana
World.content:
Reuters — Guyana’s government said Monday that 27 bodies have been recovered from a ferry that capsized off the coast over the weekend with 179 people on board.

Dozens of people were feared dead after the ferry capsized late Saturday. Authorities suggested that an inaccurate passenger list and drug use by the crew might have contributed to the situation.

At least 69 people have been rescued but 83 are yet to be found, Guyanese Prime Minister Mark Phillips said Monday.

The captain and other crew members are now in police custody, Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said at a press conference late Sunday.

“Search and rescue is still in progress,” Edghill said. “So to the families that are out there wondering about their loved ones, we are doing everything that is humanly possible to find them.”

The MV Barima capsized off the North Atlantic coast, approximately seven miles from shore, while traveling from the capital, Georgetown, to the village of Port Kaituma, authorities said.

Officials initially said the boat had 133 people, but after reviewing footage of the boarding process, they determined it was carrying 179.

Air traffic control received a distress call from the ferry around 11 p.m. Saturday, triggering a search and rescue operation.

Edghill said early responses were hampered by the darkness and lack of vessels with scanners that could search for survivors, leaving rescuers reliant on eyesight and sound.

Companies in the oil and gas sector have since deployed vessels with scanners, and the government has activated divers to enter the ferry to search for bodies, Edghill said. Authorities have also expanded the search area to 1,040 square kilometers (401 square miles) from 400 square kilometers.

Edghill initially insisted Sunday afternoon that there was no sign of “neglect” on the part of the ferry operator. But on Sunday evening, he said the captain and at least one other crew members had tested positive for marijuana.

In addition, a number of people who were rescued were not listed on the ferry’s manifest, indicating inaccuracies in the ferry’s passenger list and hampering rescue operations because authorities do not know how many people they are searching for.

Lifeboats are seen during a search and rescue mission after a ferry carrying more than 100 people sank off the coast of Guyana late Saturday. Hon. Prime Minister Brigadier Mark Phillips/Reuters

The boat had maintenance in 2024 and was due for dry docking — the process of temporarily taking a ship out of water to inspect it and make repairs — later this year, the minister said.

The disaster has torn apart families.

Leon Murray, a passenger on the ferry, told local news outlet Ignite News that about four hours after leaving Georgetown, someone shouted that the boat was sinking.

After the boat capsized, Murray managed to swim to the surface where he used a life jacket to keep himself afloat. He drifted and shouted for help and found his son and three others holding on to a floating box.

Murray said he and his son survived, but his wife, daughter and four grandchildren haven’t been found. “Six of them gone.”

Guyanese Prime Minister Mark Phillips said in a statement that the vessel reported a cargo weight of 268 tons out of a capacity of 284 tons. He said the ferry was licensed to carry more than 300 passengers and was outfitted with 250 life jackets, six inflatable life rafts and two rigid life rafts.

But by Sunday evening, at a press conference, Phillips said an investigation had been launched into wrongdoing involving members of the police force, defense force and maritime administration department.

“Let me be absolutely clear: where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law.”

World.title: Why Trump and Mamdani might both welcome a fight over Netanyahu
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s approval ratings may be sliding, but one political super sense is as sharp as ever: picking a fight with an adversary he casts as the entire Democratic Party.

Step forward, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

It took just days for Trump to jump on Mamdani’s refusal to roll back a campaign pledge to arrest Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for whom the International Criminal Court has issued a warrant, if he showed up in the city.

“Benjamin Netanyahu will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America,” Trump announced on Monday on Truth Social, his preferred venue for igniting new culture war tussles.

The president’s response raised the possibility of a clash between federal power and the city he once called home.

But its real significance goes further.

This was also a classic example of Trump’s habit of seizing on an issue or a personality to ignite a wider political controversy. He wasn’t just defending an ally in Netanyahu — and perhaps creating a new sense of obligation with a leader with whom he’s recently had tense relations. Trump was also preparing the ground for his emerging midterm election narrative of a Democratic Pary that’s become too extreme.

Still, both Trump and Mamdani might embrace a fight over Netanyahu — which has deeper domestic ramifications than a foreign policy dispute over civilian deaths in the Israeli onslaught in Gaza after Hamas’ October 7, 2023 attacks.

It’s therefore not really important whether Mamdani can arrest Netanyahu. (This is a murky question because the US has not ratified the Rome Statute, which requires member states to arrest those under warrant from the International Criminal Court. And Washington has long allowed even enemy leaders — from places like Iran and Cuba – to visit New York for the United Nations General Assembly.)

Instead, this is one of those occasions when having the fight is more important than winning it.

It’s also a snapshot of how American politics is moving away from historical and near-universal support for Israel and it’s a moment that exemplifies the Democratic Party’s own broader evolution.

How Democrats now view Israel differently

Mamdani is among a new generation of Democrats who’ve adopted sharply anti-Israel rhetoric that delights grassroots liberals. Declining to drop his campaign vow to arrest Netanyahu shows Mamdani curating the political capital he won during his campaign, which is critical to enacting his progressive program as he transitions from insurgent outsider to government insider.

Mamdani’s views on Israel have become an article of faith among many progressive and younger Democrats who believe that Netanyahu perpetrated genocide against tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The prime minister “belongs in The Hague. He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court,” an opinion “held by many,” Mamdani said in the same New York Times podcast interview in which he said he was consulting his legal advisers over Netanyahu.

Palestinians walk along a road surrounded by buildings destroyed in Israeli military strikes during the Israel-Hamas war, in Jabaliya, Gaza Strip, on July 2, 2026. Jehad Alshrafi/AP

Israel strongly rejects claims that it perpetrated genocide and says it is acting in legitimate self-defense following the terror attack on Israeli civilians by Hamas, a radical Palestinian organization based in Gaza. It blames Palestinian casualties on Hamas for embedding military targets in civilian areas. Both the Biden and Trump administrations argued Israel’s actions did not equate to genocide.

But some key Democrats are now building an anti-Israel argument that goes beyond Gaza into the top midterm election question — the affordability of middle-class life. “I want my tax dollars spent here in Michigan to provide schools in Michigan, to build health care in Michigan, to invest in Michigan rather than to be sent abroad to kill Palestinian people due to genocides and apartheid,” Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed told CNN’s Kasie Hunt on July 2.

How a bromance could sour

A full-on feud over Netanyahu would be the latest twist in Trump’s relationship with Mamdani. They had something of a bromance during an Oval Office meeting last year. “I get along very well with him. We had some good meetings, some good talks and he’s the way he is,” Trump told conservative radio host Sid Rosenberg in January.

The New York mayor showed up in the Oval Office again in February — bringing visual props to make his pitch to the former real estate developer for a massive federal housing investment in the city.

Starkly different in age, ideology and temperament, Trump and Mamdani share key traits. Both try to keep their base happy with populist policies and have highly developed political communications skills.

It suits Mamdani to engage with Trump because it underscores his influence as a national figure. The president, meanwhile, is always searching for an angle.

Trump’s exploration of a showdown with Mamdani over Netanyahu was fairly mild among the overall tenor of his Truth Social posts. But it opens the possibility that New York’s starring role in the Democratic Party’s shift against Israel may soon become a data point in the wider White House case that the party is too extreme for many Americans.

President Donald Trump meets with Zohran Mamdani, then the Mayor-elect for New York, in the Oval Office of the White House on November 21, 2025. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

Mamdani could become, for Trump, a metaphor for the wider Democratic Party in the run-up to the midterms.

Trump has done this before. He portrayed New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who’s also a democratic socialist, as the epitome of her party. He’s called Vermont independent Sen. Bernie Sanders, a former Democratic presidential primary candidate, “crazy.”

Democrats have a significant opening against the president’s party in November, since polls show that the country’s lost faith in his economic management and faults his failure to largely live up to promises to bring prices down.

But if Trump can create ideological or cultural clashes, he may stop Democrats from peeling away more conservative, White working-class voters away from his 2024 coalition. Two years ago, Trump successfully leveraged issues like immigration, transgender athletes in sports, and crime to portray Democrats as out of touch. Israel may be next. And bringing Israel into this campaign helps Trump build enthusiasm among evangelical conservatives who back Israel, establishment Republicans who might have soured on his message and swing voters who may feel more comfortable with traditional US foreign policies.

The Democrats are already heading for a huge split over Israel, as more moderate members warn that some anti-Netanyahu rhetoric veers into antisemitism. Trump may even feel he could woo some Jewish voters who’ve traditionally voted Democrat.

Centrist Democrats worry that their party is endangering a critical ally. “Look at the kinds of people that we’ve elected in the primaries, not just pro-Palestinian, just intensely, intensely anti-Israel,” Pennsylvania Democratic Sen. John Fetterman told CNN’s Manu Raju last week.

Exemplifying the split, El-Sayed’s Democratic primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, is acknowledging the fury of many Democratic voters towards Netanyahu while adopting a position that might be more mainstream in a general election clash with a Republican rival.

“I can say that Israel has a right to peacefully exist alongside the people of Palestine and in Gaza. It is very clear that Mr. Netanyahu has not made us safer, has not brought us closer to peace, and he’s endangered Jews here in America and around the world,” Stevens said in a debate earlier this month.

The divisions laid bare in her confrontation with El-Sayed are unfolding far beyond Michigan. Support for Israel is also weakening among the most nationalist fringes of the Republican Party. The issue is likely to prefigure a critical dynamic in both parties’ looming 2028 presidential primaries.

For now, however, the clearest splits over the war in Gaza are within the Democratic Party. And Trump has every reason to try to use a figure like Mamdani to try to tear them wide open.

World.title: Israel’s far-right openly boasts of resettling Gaza as election looms
World.content:
With elections looming in October, Israel’s right wing is turning the push to rebuild Jewish settlements in Gaza into a central issue of their campaign.

It is part of a broader effort to push Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reverse the 2005 disengagement from the coastal enclave that saw Israel unilaterally uproot its settlements.

On Sunday, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich – two key far-right members of Netanyahu’s government – led thousands of Israeli settlers and activists to the Gaza perimeter demanding the reestablishment of three settlements in northern Gaza: Nisanit, Dugit and Elei Sinai. Organized by the hardline Nachala settler movement, the demonstration included senior government ministers and lawmakers. The demonstration is more than just a political stunt meant to secure right-wing votes. Expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank and rebuilding settlements in Gaza are an open dream of Israel’s far-right, and they see the current moment in time with Israel occupying more than half of Gaza as a prime opportunity to pressure Netanyahu to advance their agenda.

In an attempt to prevent the demonstration from entering Gaza,the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) declared the area a closed military zone, forcing organizers to alter the route. But the marchers would not be deterred, pushing toward the Gaza perimeter while dodging barriers set up by the Israeli miliitary and police.

Buses transported families, including children and teenagers, from Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank, while young activists from Ben Gvir’s and Smotrich’s parties handed out campaign materials and pamphlets.

“If someone had said three years ago that we would control 70% of the Gaza Strip, no one would have believed it,” Ben Gvir said at the rally.

“So today I say: there will be Jewish settlement throughout Gaza,” he said, adding that Israel should “encourage voluntary migration” of Palestinians – an idea briefly floated by the Trump administration before it was ultimately rejected in the Gaza ceasefire agreement.

“We are returning home. Gaza is ours,” Ben Gvir said.

Smotrich cast the moment in clear political terms, warning that a change of government could “roll back all the Zionist and national settlement revolution” of the previous four years under the most right-wing government in Israel’s history.

“All of this could go down the drain – and we will march here again to prevent evacuations,” he said. Smotrich has expanded settlements dramatically in the West Bank during this government’s tenure, and he has made clear his desire to keep going.

Both Smotrich and Ben Gvir have both championed rebuilding the settlements in Gaza since October 7, 2023, and have framed the Gaza war as a chance to reverse the 2005 disengagement.

Smotrich, who also is the minister in charge of settlement affairs within the defense ministry, said in June that completed plans for three northern Gaza settlements are awaiting Netanyahu’s approval. He has described Gaza as “an inseparable part of the land of Israel” and argued that renewed settlement would serve as a security buffer. “Where there is no settlement, there is no security,” Smotrich said in late June.

Thousands of Israelis, led by far-right ministers, walked to the Gaza border on Sunday in support of the reestablishment of Jewish settlements in the territory. Amir Cohen/Reuters

Defense Minister Israel Katz has declared separately he intends to establish three military outposts in the area. The Israeli government also uses military outposts as a first step to establish a physical, civilian presence on the ground, which is then gradually expanded into civilian communities and settlements.

Netanyahu, however, has neither endorsed or denounced these settlement plans, and they have not been brought before the Israeli cabinet. Netanyahu currently leads a caretaker government until the next election on October 27.

Israeli forces currently hold approximately 60% of Gaza’s territory, and Netanyahu has publicly said that he ordered the military to take 70% and maybe more. Under the October 2025 US-brokered ceasefire, Israel was required to pull back to roughly 53% of the territory, though the IDF has since expanded its control well beyond that line. Trump’s Gaza peace plan and ceasefire framework explicitly ruled out Israeli occupation or annexation of Gaza.

Before the 2005 disengagement, Israel maintained 21 settlements across Gaza, home to about 8,000 settlers. The unilateral withdrawal under former Prime Minister Ariel Sharon dismantled those communities and evacuated four additional settlements in the northern West Bank. In recent years, Netanyahu’s government has reversed elements of that policy, including legislation allowing Israelis to return to previously evacuated areas in the West Bank and approval of new settlements in these areas.

Last week, the Israeli government approved plans to allocate more than 2.3 billion shekels (approximately $766 million) to establish new Jewish settlements and build access roads in the occupied West Bank, part of an accelerated effort to entrench the settlement enterprise and destroy the possibility of a future Palestinian state.

All Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are considered illegal under International law, but settlers have successfully established dozens of unauthorized outposts in recent years and eventually secured Israeli government approvals.

Israel’s renewed settlement push, combined with the prolonged Gaza war and a rise in settler violence, has dramatically increased international criticism of Israel. Several countries, including the UK, France, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Norway, have recently imposed new sanctions on groups and individual linked with the settler movement, along with travel bans on Ben Gvir and Smotrich in some European countries.

World.title: UPND Petauke Youth Leader Dies After Collapsing
World.content:
A United Party for National Development (UPND) youth leader in Petauke District has died after collapsing while walking home from a party campaign centre.

The deceased, Lackson Banda, 52, served as UPND Youth Secretary for Petauke Central Constituency.

According to Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba, Banda was walking along Petauke Boma Road with Petauke Central Constituency Youth Chairperson Rhodwell Meleki, 45, and UPND member Ruth Mbewe, 26, after leaving the party’s campaign centre in Mayard Compound.

Police said Banda suddenly complained of weakness and numbness in both legs before sitting down by the roadside.

Meleki and Mbewe reportedly borrowed a bicycle and rushed him to Petauke District Hospital for medical attention.

However, shortly after being attended to by medical personnel, Banda was pronounced dead.

The matter was reported to Petauke Police Station at around 19:55 hours by Meleki, after which officers conducted a physical inspection of the body.

Police said the body has since been deposited in the Petauke District Hospital mortuary, where it is awaiting a postmortem examination to establish the cause of death.

World.title: Agricrop team wins Anglican Golf tourney
World.content:
Agricrop-sponsored team has emerged winners of the Anglican Church fundraising golf tournament held at the Ndola Golf Club.

‎

‎The team composed of Model Kanyimbo, Rex Mwansa, Mapalo Tanasho and Patrick Kaoma combined for 106 points to win the crown on Sunday.

‎

‎The Church is fundraising to host the upcoming October 2026 Peniel Zambia Conference, a meeting of bishops and worshipers with special speakers expected from countries such as Nigeria and the United States of America.

‎

‎Kanyimbo, Mwansa and Tanasho carded 32, 38 and 36 points respectively as results were picked from the best three players.

‎

‎Team captain Kaoma said his squad was pleased to compete for a noble cause.

‎

‎Kaoma said: _“We want to thank the organisers and the sponsors for coming up with this tournament. This time it is us who won, next time it will be others but they have to come prepared for a tough battle to take this title away from us.”_

‎

‎In second place was the team sponsored by the Zambia Air Force [ZAF] with a score of 104 points thanks to Major Mutambo, Nkrumah Musonda and Mtonga Mtonga who brought home 35, 35 and 34 points respectively.

‎

‎In third place was a team sponsored by the Public Service Pension Fund [PSPF] who finished with 103 points. In individual awards, Samuel Mwaba had the best score of 41 points while Mutambo got the nearest to the pin award.

‎

‎The event was graced by Copperbelt Province Permanent Secretary Lawrence Mwanza who donated K10,000 towards the fundraising venture.

‎

‎Mwanza said: “When we come together to support a good cause, our collective efforts create opportunities that can benefit a lot of people.”

‎

‎Meanwhile, Anglican Diocese of Central Zambia Bishop Emmanuel Chikoya said part of the raised money will go towards helping vulnerable children in school and health.

‎

‎Tournament Organising Committee Chairperson Ernest Sumani said they had targeted to raise about K600,000 but did not reach the target.

‎

‎Sumani said: “I must honestly acknowledge that we did not reach our original target. However, I want to emphasise that this does not diminish the success of this tournament.”

World.title: Binwell to know his fate on 20th August
World.content:
Former MP Binwell Mpundu to know on August 20 if he has case to answer in sedition trial

Former Nkana independent Member of Parliament Binwell Mpundu will learn on August 20 whether he has a case to answer over a Facebook post allegedly urging politicians to arm themselves, after narrowly avoiding detention under a bench warrant at the Lusaka Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Magistrate Webster Milumbe discharged a warrant that had been issued against Mpundu on July 9 after he failed to appear for a scheduled hearing in his ongoing sedition trial. The former lawmaker told the court he was not offering excuses but expressing genuine regret, explaining that a vehicle breakdown in remote parts of Luapula Province had prevented him from returning to Lusaka in time.

“Your Honour, my apologies. I failed to come because my vehicle broke down in Luapula where I had gone for campaigns. Your Honour, this made it difficult for me to return in time,” Mpundu told the court.

He explained that he currently holds a key position in a presidential candidate’s campaign team ahead of the August 13 general election, a role that requires extensive travel before campaign rallies. Mpundu said the journey that led to his absence had taken his team from Luapula Province through several districts in Eastern Province, including Nyimba, Petauke, Sinda, Katete and Lundazi.

He further told the court that deteriorating road conditions and a tyre burst along the Muchinga escarpment compounded the delays, making it impossible to reach Lusaka in time for the hearing.

The former MP said he had consistently attended all previous court sessions and produced photographs of the damaged vehicle as evidence of the breakdown.

“Your Honour, I am a law-abiding citizen, and I respect our courts of law,” he said.

In his ruling, Magistrate Milumbe said Mpundu deserved the benefit of the doubt in light of his previous attendance record. The court discharged the warrant and allowed him to continue on police bond before proceeding with the hearing.

The prosecution then called Detective Inspector Steven Simweenda, who testified that police investigations had linked a Facebook post to an account belonging to Mpundu.

According to Simweenda, the post, titled Defend Yourselves With Equal Measures and published on December 20, 2024, urged fellow politicians to acquire firearms following a reported assault on opposition leader Sean Tembo.

The officer told the court that such a call would have encouraged politicians to act contrary to the Public Order Act, which prohibits the possession of firearms at public gatherings.

He testified that police obtained an authenticated copy of the Facebook post from the Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority (ZICTA), which established that the account belonged to the former Nkana legislator.

Simweenda further told the court that the Facebook page had more than three million followers, giving its owner considerable public influence and responsibility for the content published on the platform.

During cross-examination, the investigating officer maintained that the Facebook account belonged to Mpundu and that he was responsible for the publication. He added that during earlier investigations, the accused had acknowledged ownership of the page but denied committing the offence after being formally warned and cautioned by police.

Mpundu is charged with one count of seditious practices contrary to Section 57(1)(b), read together with Section 60(1)(i), of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia.

With the prosecution having closed its case, Magistrate Milumbe adjourned the matter to August 20, when the court will determine whether Mpundu has a case to answer and should be placed on his defence.

World.title: Six UNZA Students Escape Hostel Fire, Lose Property
World.content:
Six University of Zambia (UNZA) students escaped unharmed after a fire gutted two hostel rooms at the institution’s Great East Road Campus on Sunday evening.

The fire broke out around 19:00 hours in Room 18 of October 2 Hostel before spreading to the neighbouring Room 28.

According to preliminary police investigations, the fire is believed to have originated from an electrical socket while the students were using an electric cooker.

The blaze destroyed laptops, refrigerators, clothing, documents and other personal belongings, leaving the affected students with significant losses.

The six occupants managed to escape after raising an alarm as smoke engulfed the hostel.

The Fire Brigade later responded to the scene and successfully extinguished the fire before it spread to other parts of the hostel.

Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi confirmed that no injuries were recorded during the incident.

“The fire destroyed clothing, laptops, refrigerators, documents, and other personal belongings in Room 18 before spreading to the neighbouring Room 28, where additional property was also destroyed,” Chilabi said.

Police have since processed the scene and opened an inquiry to establish the exact cause of the fire, while the value of the damaged property has not yet been determined.

World.title: President Hichilema Says Law Was Changed to Provide Retirement Benefits for Former Vice Presidents
World.content:
Speaking during the funeral service of former Vice-President Dr. Guy Scott at the Anglican Cathedral of the Holy Cross in Lusaka, President Hichilema said it was unfair that individuals who had served as the country’s second-highest office holders were not provided for after leaving office.

The President said that upon assuming office in 2021, he found that while former judges and former Speakers of the National Assembly were entitled to retirement benefits, former vice presidents had no similar legal provisions.

“One of the things that when we won the election in 2021, I realised that vice presidents in this country were never looked after post their service in office. Just totally ignored,” President Hichilema said.

He explained that after raising the matter, he was informed that the law did not provide for retirement benefits for former vice presidents, prompting him to seek legal guidance from the Attorney General.

President Hichilema said he initially appointed former vice presidents as Presidential Special Envoys under existing constitutional provisions to enable the country to continue benefiting from their experience and expertise.

He said those appointed included Dr. Guy Scott, Malimba Masheke, General Godfrey Miyanda, Nevers Mumba, Enoch Kavindele and Inonge Wina.

According to the President, the appointments were intended to ensure that the knowledge and experience of former national leaders continued to contribute to the country’s development.

President Hichilema said his administration later worked with Parliament and the Attorney General to enact legislation providing retirement benefits for former vice presidents.

“I want to thank Parliament for passing that law. That law is now in place. Former vice presidents, all of them, irrespective of political party, because they served this country, are now on retirement benefits,” he said.

World.title: Government Says Public Service Recruitment Will Be Merit-Based
World.content:
Government has assured citizens that the ongoing public service recruitment exercise will be conducted through a transparent and merit-based process.

Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana said all successful applicants will be recruited based on merit, adding that the exercise will not rely on previous application databases.

Speaking on the News Diggers Podcast, Kawana said some applicants have been advised to submit fresh applications as part of the recruitment process.

He said President Hakainde Hichilema remains committed to transparency and has ensured that government contracts and appointments are awarded on merit rather than political affiliation.

Kawana added that the President has retained several public officers who served under the previous administration because Government values competence and effective service delivery.

Meanwhile, Kawana dismissed allegations that Government vehicles are being used for UPND campaign activities, stating that the ruling party is using its own resources while Government vehicles remain assigned to official duties.

He also rejected claims by the Tonse Alliance that Government is targeting opposition leaders, saying there are no plans to assassinate Alliance leader Brian Mundubile or any other opposition figure.

Kawana said police officers were deployed to Mtendere to maintain public order after Mundubile allegedly failed to notify law enforcement authorities about a planned roadshow following a scheduled rally at Heroes Stadium.

On agriculture, Kawana said the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) has not yet announced the maize floor price because the moisture content of the grain remains above the legally required 12.5 percent for safe storage.

He further criticised Brian Mundubile’s campaign pledges, saying the opposition leader lacks a manifesto and is promising programmes that have already been implemented by the current Government.

World.title: 18-year-old gang raped by four unknown men in Mazabuka
World.content:
An 18 -year- old woman of Airstrip Compound in Mazabuka District of Southern Province has been gang raped by four unknown men in a cane field.

According to a statement issued by Southern Province Police Commanding Officer, Moono Namalongo to the media, the victim secured the door and windows of the house where she was sleeping with her 30 -year- old sister before going to bed at around 22:00 hours.

However, two of the perpetrators who were wearing face masks broke into the victim’s house on July 18, 2026 around 01:00 hours and forcibly dragged her to a nearby cane field where they had unlawful carnal knowledge of her.

He added that other individuals joined at the scene in performing the unlawful act.

Mr Namalongo said the victim reported the matter to the police where a medical report form was issued.

He has confirmed that a docket has been opened and investigations in the matter have been instituted, though no arrest has been made at this stage.

“The Zambia Police Service strongly condemns acts of sexual violence. I can assure the public that every effort will be made to ensure that the perpetrators are brought to justice,” Mr Namalongo stated.

World.title: Zesco refutes loadshedding claims
World.content:
Zesco Limited has dismissed claims by some political players that the power utility company will resume excessive loadshedding after the August 13 general elections.

Zesco Managing Director, Justin Loongo, says the power utility company will continue with its normal power supply across the country even after the elections, following the continued investment in solar, coal and hydro power generation plants.

Speaking when he paid a courtesy call on Central Province Permanent Secretary, Milner Mwanakampwe in Kabwe, Mr Loongo assured the nation that the company has put in place adequate measures to ensure there are no power disruptions.

And Mr Loongo disclosed that over 300 megawatts of solar power has been added to the national electricity grid against the 1,000 megawatts target, with many more other power generation projects being undertaken across the country.

Meanwhile, Central Province Permanent Secretary, Milner Mwanakampwe, has cautioned Zambians against believing in deceptive assertions that the end of load shedding is political.

Dr Mwanakampwe emphasised that the government is on course to achieving its target of adding 1,000 megawatts of power on the national electricity grid.

He said Central Province alone has so far contributed over 300 megawatts of solar power to the grid to ensure sustainable economic development and activities.
