World.title: Croatian Clubs Discover Potential European Draws
World.content:
Croatia’s European hopefuls found out their possible third qualifying round opponents on Monday, with draws confirmed across the Europa League, Champions League, and Conference League paths.

Hajduk could face Salzburg

Should Hajduk get past Cypriot side Pafos in the second qualifying round of the Europa League, their reward will be a third-round clash with Austria’s Salzburg. Hajduk host Pafos in the first leg on Thursday in Split, with the return fixture in Cyprus the following Thursday. Should they progress, Hajduk would again have home advantage in the first leg of the third round, with the second leg to follow in Salzburg. Third qualifying round ties are scheduled for August 6 and 13.

Should Hajduk instead lose against Pafos, they would drop into the Conference League third qualifying round, where they’d face the winner of the tie between Georgia’s Dinamo Tbilisi and Lithuania’s Žalgiris, with the first leg played away from home.

Dinamo await Vikingur or Hapoel

Champions Dinamo Zagreb have also learned their potential path forward. Should they be eliminated by Switzerland’s Thun in the Champions League second qualifying round, Dinamo would drop into the Europa League third qualifying round to face either Iceland’s Vikingur or Israel’s Hapoel Beer Sheva.

Should Dinamo instead get past Thun and reach the Champions League third qualifying round itself, Mario Kovačević’s side would face the winner of the tie between Faroese side Klaksvik and Lithuania’s Kauno Žalgiris, coached by Željko Sopić. First legs in that round are set for August 4/5, with second legs on August 11.

UEFA has scrapped the previous system of forming subgroups ahead of the “champions’ path” draw this season, meaning Dinamo faced a considerably wider pool of possible opponents than in previous years.

Before turning their attention to the third qualifying round, Dinamo first face Thun in the first leg of the second qualifying round on Tuesday in Switzerland, kicking off at 8 pm, with the return leg set for Tuesday, July 28.

Rijeka and Varaždin could head to Iceland

Rijeka and Varaždin also discovered their potential third qualifying round opponents in the Conference League on Monday. Rijeka, if they eliminate Ireland’s Derry City in the second round, would face the winner of the tie between Iceland’s Stjarnan and Finland’s Ilves. Varaždin, if they see off Czech side Jablonec, would take on the winner between Latvia’s RFS and Iceland’s Vestri.

Third qualifying round fixtures in the Conference League are scheduled for August 6 and 13.

World.title: Croatia vs Spain, Greece & Italy: Which Destination Comes Out on Top?
World.content:
July the 21st, 2026 – Croatia has become one of Europe’s most sought-after summer destinations, but how does it compare to the longtime tourism giants Spain, Greece and Italy?

As Vedran Salvia reports for Index, each country offers something unique, from world-famous beaches to ancient cities and exceptional cuisine. Despite the constantly evolving competition, Croatia appears to very successfully continue carving out its own niche, attracting travellers looking for crystal-clear waters, historic towns and a more relaxed coastal experience.

the croatian coast needs very little help in attracting attention

Croatia’s greatest strength remains its spectacular Adriatic coast. Stretching for more than 1,700 kilometres and dotted with over 1,200 islands, islets and reefs, it offers endless opportunities for sailing, island hopping and discovering secluded beaches. Unlike many Mediterranean destinations where development unfortunately totally dominates the coastline, much of Croatia’s shore remains remarkably well preserved, with national parks, hidden coves and picturesque, ancient fishing villages sitting alongside popular tourist hotspots like Dubrovnik, Split and Makarska.

how does that compare with spain?

Tourism heavyweight Spain continues to attract visitors with its vast array of long, sandy beaches, lively nightlife and major cities such as Barcelona, Valencia and Málaga. It also offers year-round sunshine in many regions. Croatia, however, appeals to travellers seeking a more intimate experience. While destinations like Dubrovnik can become crowded during peak season, much of the coastline remains quieter than Spain’s busiest resorts, particularly away from the best-known locations.

greece – the home of influencer islands

Nearby Greece is globally renowned for iconic, entirely different islands such as Santorini, Mykonos and Crete, along with its ancient history and rich Mediterranean cuisine. Croatia, located just up north, offers a different style of island holiday. Rather than focusing on a handful of internationally famous islands which have become totally swamped by influencers over more recent years (see Mykonos, for example), visitors can choose from hundreds of inhabited and uninhabited islands. Each of them has its very own character, from the lavender fields of Hvar’s interior and the vineyards of Korčula to the untouched nature of Mljet and Lastovo.

the home of the romans is hard to contend with, yet croatia manages to do so

Neighbouring Italy remains one of the world’s most visited countries thanks to remarkable cities such as Rome, Venice and Florence, alongside the Amalfi Coast and Sicily. The country that gave the world the Romans would be difficult to compete with for anyone, and yet Croatia, in its own way, still manages. Naturally, Croatia cannot match Italy’s sheer number of globally recognised cultural landmarks or its geographical size, but it often provides a similar Adriatic atmosphere at a more accessible price point. This is particularly true for sailing holidays, waterfront accommodation and seafood dining outside the very height of the summer season.

croatian prices – a gap that is narrowing (and quickly)

One of Croatia’s traditional advantages has always been affordability, although that gap has greatly narrowed in recent years. Since the country’s accession to the Eurozone, prices for accommodation, restaurants and tourism services have spiked noticeably, especially in popular coastal destinations. During the peak summer months, visitors may find Croatia approaching the prices of parts of Italy or Greece, particularly down in Dubrovnik, as well as in central Dalmatian destinations such as Hvar and Split. Despite that being the case, many lesser-known destinations continue to offer excellent value, particularly along the Kvarner coast, northern Dalmatia and of course away from the sea entirely in inland Croatia.

croatia is so much more than “just beaches”

Croatia’s appeal extends well beyond the coastline and 1,000+ islands. Visitors can explore the marvellous Plitvice Lakes National Park, hike through the imposing mountains of Velebit, discover a great many Roman monuments in Zadar, Pula and Split, sample world-class wines up in Istria and down Pelješac, or experience vibrant festivals and cultural events throughout the entire summer. Combined with its strong reputation as one of Europe’s safest destinations by far, these experiences continue to attract travellers looking for far more than a traditional beach holiday.

the verdict – croatia is the small country that could (and very much has)

Spain offers energy and variety, Italy delivers world-famous culture, and Greece remains synonymous with idyllic island escapes. Croatia, meanwhile, combines elements of all three: spectacular islands, historic towns, exceptional natural beauty and a coastline that remains one of the cleanest and most diverse in Europe. For travellers seeking a Mediterranean holiday that balances relaxation, adventure and history, Croatia continues to prove that it deserves its place alongside the region’s biggest tourism giants.

World.title: Europe’s Smallest Bible Is Hidden in Croatia, And It Fits in the Palm of Your Hand
World.content:
July the 21st, 2026 – You don’t have to be religious to appreciate the wonder of religious architecture and items, and one of the most fascinating (and tiny) items can be found in Croatia. Europe’s smallest Bible is actually hidden in a relatively overlooked part of Croatia.

Croatia is home to countless historical treasures, but few are as surprising as the smallest Bible in all of Europe, a tiny masterpiece that can fit comfortably in the palm of your hand. Putni kofer writes that this truly remarkable miniature Bible is kept in the town of Ludbreg, widely known as “the centre of the world” in northern Croatia, where it has become one of the area’s most unusual cultural attractions.

ludbreg – full of surprises

Despite its incredibly small dimensions, the Bible contains both the Old and New Testaments, printed in microscopic text and bound with exceptional craftsmanship. Its pages are so small that visitors are often astonished that an entire Bible could be produced in such a compact format, making it as much a feat of printing as it is an object of religious significance.

The miniature Bible forms part of Ludbreg’s exceptionally rich cultural and religious heritage. The town is already well known as one of Croatia’s most important pilgrimage destinations thanks to the Sanctuary of the Precious Blood of Christ, which attracts thousands of visitors each year, but this tiny book offers another fascinating reason to visit.

Visitors to Ludbreg are often surprised to discover that such a unique artefact is housed in a small Croatian town rather than in one of Europe’s larger museums.

more than a mere religious object

While the Bible’s size makes it an instant conversation piece, it also reflects the extraordinary skill of the printers and bookbinders who created it. Miniature books have long fascinated collectors around the world, but examples containing the complete biblical text are exceptionally rare, making Ludbreg’s specimen one of the continent’s most unusual literary treasures.

As touched on above, Ludbred is known as the “Centre of the World” thanks to a local legend. This small, humble northern Croatian continues to surprise visitors with attractions that extend far beyond its famous pilgrimage traditions. From its historic streets and castle to one of Europe’s tiniest Bibles, the town proves that some of Croatia’s most remarkable stories are found in places many international visitors have yet to discover.

World.title: Croatia Tightens Online Alcohol Sales With e-Citizens Age Verification
World.content:
July the 21st, 2026 – Croatia is continuing to fight its apparent war on alcohol sales from all angles, with mandatory e-Citizens age verification looming.

Purchasing alcohol online in Croatia is set to become significantly more secure after new rules introduced by the government require customers to verify their age through the e-Citizens (e-Građani) digital identity system before buying it. Poslovni reports that this latest measure is designed to prevent minors from buying alcoholic beverages online by introducing a reliable electronic age verification process, replacing the self-declaration methods commonly used by many online retailers today.

the age of digital id

Under the new rules, customers purchasing alcoholic drinks online will have to confirm they are of legal drinking age using Croatia’s e-Citizens platform. The digital verification system will allow retailers to confirm whether a customer is an adult without relying solely on manually entered dates of birth or simple tick-box declarations, which have long been criticised as ineffective.

In traditional shops, retailers are obviously already required to refuse alcohol sales to minors and can ask customers to present identification if they doubt their age. The new system aims to bring online alcohol sales closer to those same standards by ensuring age verification takes place before the transaction is completed. Officials say the change reflects the growing importance of digital commerce and the need to apply the same consumer protection rules regardless of whether alcohol is purchased in person or online.

online retailers should have the exact same level of responsibility

Businesses selling alcoholic beverages over the internet will now need to integrate the e-Citizens verification process into their online stores. The move is expected to improve legal certainty for retailers while making it considerably more difficult for underage users to bypass age restrictions through false declarations.

The introduction of mandatory digital age verification is another example of Croatia expanding the use of its e-Citizens platform beyond mere public administration into everyday commercial services. Over the past decade, the platform has become a central gateway for accessing government services, digital documents and official records. Its use for online age verification reflects a broader shift towards secure digital identity solutions that are becoming increasingly common across Europe.

For consumers, the biggest change will be simple: anyone buying alcohol online in Croatia should expect to log in through e-Citizens before placing an order for alcohol, adding an extra step designed to ensure that alcohol is sold only to adults.

World.title: Zagreb Bus Station Set for Major Renovation as First Phase Gets Underway
World.content:
July the 21st, 2026 – The now quite dated and dilapidated Zagreb bus station is set to undergo a major renovation as the first phase finally gets underway.

Zagreb bus station is set to undergo a long-awaited modernisation, with the first phase of renovation focusing on improving passenger facilities and upgrading key parts of one of Croatia’s busiest transport hubs.

AKZ.hr reports that this significant investment marks the beginning of a broader effort to revitalise the station, which has served millions of passengers for decades and remains the country’s largest hub for domestic and international bus travel.

The initial phase of works will prioritise improvements that passengers use every day, including the station’s waiting areas, sanitary facilities and other public spaces that have shown signs of age after years of heavy use. Station management has claimed that the primary goal is to improve comfort, accessibility and the overall travel experience while ensuring the terminal remains fully operational throughout the renovation process.

modernising a crucial national transport hub

Opened back in 1987, Zagreb bus station handles thousands of passengers each day and connects the Croatian capital with destinations across Croatia and Europe. Despite its importance, much of the complex has remained largely unchanged for decades, prompting growing calls for refurbishment as passenger expectations and transport standards have evolved. The planned upgrades are expected to improve both the appearance and functionality of the station while extending the lifespan of the existing infrastructure.

The renovation is being presented as the first stage of a wider modernisation programme that could eventually include additional commercial spaces, energy-efficiency improvements and further infrastructure upgrades. By carrying out the work in phases, operators aim to minimise disruption while gradually bringing the station up to modern standards.

As Croatia continues investing in transport infrastructure as a whole, from railways and airports to roads and public transport, the refurbishment of Zagreb bus station represents yet another concerted effort to modernise the country’s key mobility hubs. For the millions of passengers who pass through the station each and every year, the first phase of works is expected to deliver noticeable improvements while laying the groundwork for a more comprehensive transformation in the years ahead.

World.title: Driving Licence Reform Looms in Croatia as Digital Licences Move Closer
World.content:
July the 20th, 2026 – A major driving license reform is on the horizon in Croatia as digital licenses move closer to becoming a new reality.

Croatian drivers could soon see one of the biggest changes to driving licences in very many decades as the European Union moves towards introducing a digital driving licence that will be recognised across all member states.

Poslovni reports that the aforementioned reform forms part of a broader overhaul of EU driving licence rules designed to simplify cross-border recognition, improve road safety and modernise the way motorists prove their driving entitlement. Croatia, as an EU member state, will be required to implement the new framework once it is formally adopted.

digital driving licenses will become the new norm

Under the new rules, drivers will be able to store their driving licence in a secure digital format on their smartphone through the forthcoming European Digital Identity Wallet. The digital version will become the default across the European Union, although motorists will still be able to request a traditional physical licence if they prefer. The aim is to make licences easier to renew, verify and use when travelling between EU countries.

new rules for young and older drivers

The reform package also introduces several measures intended to improve road safety. Among them is a probationary period of at least two years for newly qualified drivers, during which stricter penalties will apply for serious traffic offences such as drink driving or failing to wear a seatbelt. EU countries are also being encouraged to introduce accompanied driving schemes for seventeen-year-olds to help young motorists gain experience before driving independently.

The updated legislation also harmonises validity periods for driving licences and includes new provisions relating to medical fitness to drive, although individual member states will retain flexibility in how health assessments are carried out.

easier eu-wide recognition

One of the key objectives of the reform is to make life easier for people living, working or travelling across Europe. A standardised digital licence will allow authorities throughout the entire bloc to recognise driving entitlements more efficiently while reducing bureaucracy for drivers moving between member states.

For Croatian motorists, the changes will obviously not happen overnight. The legislation must first complete the final stages of the EU legislative process before member states begin implementing the new system. Once introduced, however, the reform will mark the most significant change to driving licences in decades, replacing paper-based administration with a digital-first system designed for an increasingly connected European Union while keeping physical licences available for those who still want them.

World.title: Fewer Foreigners Moving to Croatia as Immigration Slows in Early 2026
World.content:
July the 20th, 2026 – Fewer and fewer foreigners have been recorded as moving to Croatia as the immigration from third countries we’ve witnessed over recent years eases throughout early 2026.

Following on from several years of record immigration from distant (primarily Asian) countries driven largely by labour shortages, the number of people moving to Croatia has begun to slow. This has been concluded following a deep dive into the latest figures released by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS).

This brand new data shows that while Croatia has been continuing to record positive net migration, both immigration and emigration declined during the first half of 2026. That suggests that the rapid influx of foreign workers seen over more recent years may finally be starting to stabilise.

According to the Croatian Bureau of Statistics, fewer people moved to Croatia compared with the same period last year. Foreign workers continue to account for the vast majority of new arrivals, reflecting ongoing demand in sectors such as construction, tourism, hospitality, manufacturing and transport. However, the pace of arrivals has eased compared to the exceptional growth recorded over the past two years.

most foreigners moving to croatia so far in 2026 continue to come from the country’s immediate region

The largest number of foreign nationals relocating to Croatia continue to come from neighbouring countries and Southeast Asia. Citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Nepal remain among the biggest groups of newcomers, with workers from the Philippines and India also continuing to play an increasingly important role in Croatia’s labour market. Many are employed in industries facing persistent shortages of domestic workers, particularly seasonal tourism and construction.

croatia’s enfeebled labour market remains the main driver

Croatia has experienced a dramatic increase in labour migration since the abolition of annual foreign worker quotas and the rapid expansion of work permit approvals. A rapidly ageing population, record low unemployment and sustained demand from employers have encouraged companies to recruit workers from abroad, transforming Croatia from a country traditionally associated with emigration into one increasingly dependent on foreign labour. Although immigration has slowed, it does have to be noted that employers in several sectors continue to report difficulties filling vacancies without international recruitment.

the positive migration trend is continuing – for now

Despite the decline in arrivals, Croatia continues to record more people moving into the country than leaving it.

Demographers note that positive net migration is an important development for a country that spent decades experiencing population decline through emigration. However, they also point out that immigration alone cannot fully offset Croatia’s long-term demographic challenges, including low birth rates and an ageing population. With tourism, infrastructure projects and economic growth continuing to fuel demand for workers, foreign labour is expected to remain an essential part of Croatia’s economy, even if the pace of immigration becomes more moderate than in recent years.

World.title: Croatian Landlords Accuse Government of “Campaigning Against Them”
World.content:
July the 20th, 2026 – Croatian landlords who rent out private accommodation units to tourists are still feeling targeted and now openly accusing the government of campaigning against them.

Representatives of Croatia’s private accommodation sector have stepped up their open and clear criticism of recent government tourism reforms, arguing that a series of new regulations and taxes are placing an unfair burden on family-run rentals while doing little to solve the country’s wider housing challenges.

The comments come amid an increasingly heated national debate over the future of Croatia’s tourism model, with policymakers seeking to reduce pressure on the housing market while encouraging higher-quality and more sustainable tourism development. Ivica Brkljaca writes for Index that the centre of the dispute are the country’s hundreds of thousands of private accommodation beds, which have long formed the backbone of Croatia’s tourism industry.

a pushback from industry representatives

Kristjan Staničić, director of the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ), recently described the structure of Croatia’s accommodation sector as one of the country’s biggest tourism challenges, noting that private accommodation accounts for a particularly large share of available beds. He argued that recent government measures should be viewed as long-term reforms aimed at improving the sustainability of the tourism sector.

However, organisations representing Croatian private landlords say they feel increasingly targeted by new legislation and public rhetoric. They argue that family accommodation providers are being blamed for issues such as housing shortages and overtourism despite operating legally and contributing significantly to local economies, particularly in coastal communities. According to critics, the reforms risk discouraging ordinary households that rely on seasonal tourism income.

rising costs pose a serious issue

Among the industry’s biggest concerns are higher lump-sum taxes, additional administrative requirements and new rules affecting short-term rentals, particularly in apartment buildings. Various landlord associations argue that many family-run businesses operate only during the summer season and on relatively modest earnings, making it increasingly difficult to absorb additional financial and regulatory obligations. They warn that some owners may ultimately decide to leave the market altogether.

Supporters of the reforms argue that Croatia needs to shift away from relying overwhelmingly on private accommodation and encourage investment in hotels and higher-value tourism products. Critics disagree, saying reducing the number of private rentals through administrative measures would simply shrink accommodation capacity during peak season, potentially driving prices even higher rather than improving affordability or extending the tourist season. They also argue there is little evidence that fewer private apartments would automatically increase hotel occupancy outside the summer months.

an uncertain future lies ahead in the eyes of many

With new tourism legislation continuing to be rolled out, the debate over Croatia’s now historic accommodation model is unlikely to subside anytime soon. While the government maintains that the reforms are designed to create a more balanced and sustainable tourism sector, many small landlords remain unconvinced, insisting they are being asked to shoulder a disproportionate share of the changes despite playing a central role in Croatia’s tourism success for decades.

World.title: Iraq receives second batch of equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a second shipment of ground support equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport as building progresses, bringing the long-awaited facility closer to becoming operational.

The Ministry of Transport stated that the equipment arrived following an initial delivery in June and is part of the airport’s ongoing preparations for its opening.

Airport Director Ali Al-Ghurabi stated that the latest shipment includes commercial vehicles and operational equipment required to support aircraft and passenger services once the airport is operational.

The equipment will offer the necessary ground handling and technical support capabilities for international airport operations, assisting in the facility’s preparation for commercial flights, he added.

The airport is one of several transportation infrastructure projects being developed by Iraq as the government seeks to modernize its aviation sector, improve regional connectivity, and spur economic development beyond the country’s oil industry.

Baghdad has increased investment in airports, ports, and trains as part of a larger goal to improve transportation linkages, boost commerce and tourism, and establish Iraq as a regional logistical center linking the Gulf to Europe and Asia.

World.title: Washington approves Iraqi proposal to mediate between US and Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump has approved Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s proposal to mediate between the United States and Iran.

This diplomatic breakthrough is intended to diffuse the current crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, according to local news outlet Channel 8 News.

During their recent meeting in Washington, al-Zaidi asked Trump for approval to establish an official Iraqi mediation effort between the United States and Iran.

Trump authorized al-Zaidi to undertake the plan as part of attempts to address the continuing Strait of Hormuz issue.

According to insiders, the mediation would focus on restoring stability to marine shipping and energy flows across the key canal.

Al-Zaidi informed Trump that, while Pakistan has been involved in political and diplomatic discussions, Iraq plans to lead the economic track of mediation.

The Iraqi effort will look for answers to interruptions in commercial shipping and oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, which have led to a broader global energy and economic crisis.

According to reports, al-Zaidi plans to visit Tehran on Thursday for a series of high-level talks. He and the accompanying Iraqi officials are anticipated to return to Baghdad later that day.

World.title: Iraq receives Chinese-built ferries for Arab Gulf routes
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a fleet of Chinese-built passenger boats and ferries to be deployed on new maritime routes connecting the country to Arab Gulf states, as part of Baghdad’s efforts to modernize its transportation network and strengthen regional connectivity.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the fleet consists of 15 tourist boats, two passenger ferries capable of transporting 200 people each, and a bigger multi-purpose ferry that can transport 500 passengers and 80 vehicles every journey.

The warships will run maritime routes between Iraq and Arab Gulf nations, simplifying passenger travel while promoting commerce and tourism, according to the government.

The acquisition is part of Iraq’s overall strategy to modernize its maritime transport infrastructure and diversify its economy by expanding regional transportation links beyond its road and air networks.

According to the ministry, the new fleet would boost passenger and vehicle capacity while offering safer and more effective transportation services as regional travel demand increases.

The investment comes after Iraq announced several transportation projects, including the near completion of a new marina on the Shatt al-Arab waterway and continued development of the Grand Faw Port, as Baghdad seeks to strengthen its position as a regional transportation and logistics hub.

World.title: Iraq to open new marina for 50 boats on Shatt al-Arab
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is approaching completion of its biggest marina on the Shatt al-Arab waterway, which the government believes would stimulate tourism and upgrade the country’s waterfront infrastructure.

Ahmed Jassim, Director General of the state-owned General Company for Maritime Transport, said that the marina is under development and would be able to accommodate up to 50 boats once finished.

According to Jassim, the marina would have international-standard tourist and recreational amenities, as well as a helicopter landing pad and associated infrastructure, making it Iraq’s first of its sort.

He described the development as one of the Ministry of Transport’s flagship projects, stating that it will be inaugurated in the coming months.

The marina, located on the Shatt al-Arab in the southern city of Basra, is part of Iraq’s larger attempts to improve transportation and tourist infrastructure, as the government wants to diversify the economy beyond oil and attract private investment in the hospitality and leisure sectors.

The initiative comes as Baghdad ramps up investment in ports, logistics, and waterfront projects to cement Iraq’s position as a regional transportation center while also offering new chances for tourist and economic growth.

World.title: Halliburton wins Iraq contract to develop Bin Umar and Sindbad oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Halliburton has signed a deal with Iraq’s Basra Oil Company (BOC) to assist in the development of the Bin Umar and Sindbad oil and gas fields in southern Iraq, bolstering Baghdad’s efforts to increase crude output and decrease dependency on imported natural gas.

According to the deal, Halliburton will offer integrated field management services, as well as engineering, procurement, and construction management for the two fields.

The project involves field development planning, production optimization, digital technologies, and project management, all with the goal of speeding development and enhancing operational efficiency.

Halliburton announced that it will use its Landmark digital platform to integrate subsurface data, drilling, production operations, and business planning.

According to BOC, the initial five-year phase of the Bin Umar expansion could enhance oil output to over 150,000 barrels per day and collect around 300 million standard cubic feet of associated gas, which would be utilized to help fulfill Iraq’s domestic energy demands.

The project is part of Iraq’s wider aim to increase oil production while capturing associated gas that is now burned, decreasing reliance on gas imports to run the country’s power sector and boosting energy security.

BOC will own and operate both fields, while Halliburton will provide technical expertise and project management in collaboration with the state-owned company.

Halliburton also stated that it intends to collaborate with local resources to support workforce development and national value creation initiatives within Iraq’s Ministry of Oil.

The award is the most recent in a string of energy investments announced by Iraq as it attempts to modernize its oil and gas industry, boost production capacity, and recruit foreign expertise to utilize its huge hydrocarbon resources while enhancing the usage of associated gas.

World.title: Atlas Copco expands Iraq industrial push via local distributor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Atlas Copco of Sweden is expanding its presence in Iraq through its official distributor, Ruade Al Atlas, as demand for industrial equipment and energy-efficient technologies grows to support the country’s reconstruction and infrastructure development.

Ruade Al Atlas stated that it continues to provide Atlas Copco’s compressed air, vacuum, power, and industrial equipment solutions to clients across Iraq, serving industries such as manufacturing, construction, energy, and mining.

The company added that its partnership with Atlas Copco aims to boost productivity, reduce energy consumption, and improve operational efficiency by providing advanced industrial technologies and technical support to Iraqi businesses.

Iraq has increased attempts to upgrade its industrial base and attract international investment as the government strives to diversify the economy away from oil.

The country has announced several projects in manufacturing, energy, transportation, and infrastructure, which are expected to boost demand for industrial machinery and engineering services.

Atlas Copco, one of the world’s largest manufacturers of industrial equipment, has expanded its presence in the Middle East recently, focusing on energy-efficient technologies as industries seek to reduce operating costs and improve sustainability.

World.title: Three oil fields in northern Iraq halt operations amid regional tensions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Foreign oil firms have temporarily suspended production at three oil fields in Iraqi Kurdistan to protect workers and facilities amid fears of attacks targeting energy infrastructure.

The suspension included the Shaikan, Atrush, and Sarsang fields, which are among the major producing fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The operating companies took the decision due to mounting security concerns, although the facilities have not yet suffered direct damage.

The developments come at a time when Iraqi Kurdistan’s oil reserves are under growing threat, with worries of possible assaults on oil fields and facilities as tensions between the United States and Iran rise.

The companies confirmed that the suspension is temporary, with security conditions being assessed on a daily basis. They will resume operations as soon as safety conditions improve, ensuring the protection of employees and oil assets.

Gulf Keystone Petroleum has announced a temporary halt in production at the Sheikan field as a precautionary measure due to the worsening security situation in the region.

The firm noted that the move is consistent with the practice of other foreign oil corporations operating in Iraqi Kurdistan. It stated that all of its assets and field facilities were unharmed and that the suspension was primarily for safety concerns.

The Shaikan field’s current production rate hit 45,000 barrels per day, making it one of northern Iraq’s major producing fields.

Canada-based ShaMaran Petroleum also announced the suspension of oil production and exports from the Atrush and Sarsang fields due to the deteriorating security situation in the region.

ShaMaran Petroleum confirmed that the decision was made in collaboration with its partners to ensure the safety of employees and facilities. The company indicated that production will resume once the security situation stabilizes.

The Sarsang oil field in the northern Iraqi province of Duhok has a production capacity of approximately 30,000 barrels per day.

The Atrush oil field is located around 85 kilometers northwest of Erbil. The field’s operations commenced in July 2017, with an initial production rate of roughly 34,000 barrels per day.

According to estimates, the oil field contains up to 2.6 billion barrels of oil in its reservoirs. The Atrush oil field is among the biggest in Iraqi Kurdistan, where undiscovered oil resources are estimated at more than 40 billion barrels.

World.title: Explosive-laden drone crashes near military base in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security sources told Reuters on Monday that a drone carrying explosives crashed near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US forces.

While no injuries or damages have been reported, authorities have yet to provide any clarifications.

Harir Air Base hosts United States and international coalition forces and is located east of Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. It is known as the closest US air base to Iran.

The military base is frequently targeted by drone attacks launched by Iran and its allied militias in Iraq.

On Sunday, the three provinces of Iraqi Kurdistan—Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Duhok—were subjected to a massive wave of drone and missile assaults as Iran escalated its attacks on US objectives and civilian targets in the region.

Iranian media has already reported on Iranian strikes against Harir Air Base in recent weeks, as has been the case since the beginning of the current war.

World.title: Rahul, Kharge, Mamata, Akhilesh, Kejriwal: Opposition unites for CJP demands; Centre yet to respond
World.content:
Opposition unites for CJP demands

Which political parties are protesting



What govt said



NEW DELHI: Several opposition parties came out in support of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s protest againt paper leak of NEET-UG and other competitive exams and their demand for the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The central government is yet to respond to the demands of the protesters. The development comes a day after the CJP's "Sansad Chalo" march which witnessed police crackdown on Monday.Top Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal and several party workers staged a protest outside the prime minister's residence.The party is demanding the resignation of the prime minister and the home minister."We have marched to PM Modiâs house to demand answers from him for the brutalities against young students yesterday. The Government doesnât want to take any accountability or does it want to have a debate on it in Parliament. PM and HM must resign for destroying the future of Indiaâs youth," Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal and leader Atishi joined the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.Moreover, NCP(SP) chief Sharad Pawar and Lok Sabha member Supriya Sule also joined the protesters.Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee expressed the willingness to join the protests in Delhi if the need arises while also calling for INDIA bloc unity."We supported CJP from the beginning. If need be, I will visit Delhi and join their protest," ANI quoted her as saying."The time has come to be united under the umbrella of the INDIA Alliance against the BJP. I request all parties of the nation and the entire country, and in Bengal also," she added.Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dimple Yadav was one of the major political leaders who actively participated in the protest on Monday.Questioning the police action against the protesters, Yadav said: "These children had come all the way to the Parliament building because they wanted to tell the government that your system has fallen ill, it is not working. Those innocent children were beaten with batons, the daughters' clothes were torn."The central government has not responded to the demands of the resignations yet. However, talks were held with the CJP and the opposition to pacify the protests.Union minister Jitendra Singh reached Lok Kalyan Marg and spoke with Rahul Gandhi over Congress's protest.Union minister JP Nadda also held talks with the protesters on Monday when the CJP submitted its demands."This morning, for the first time, a proposal came from the protesters to hold talks with the government, and our discussions have been ongoing since 11.50am. The meeting took place in a cordial atmosphere. An initial verbal discussion was held in detail with their delegation, and they submitted a written petition to me around 4pm. I have requested all the protesters to end their sit-in and assist the administration in restoring normalcy," Nadda said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government acted firmly against those behind the NEET paper leak to safeguard students' futures, urging states to work with the Centre to eliminate the menace in the national interest. The remarks came at a meeting of the NDA MPs on Tuesday."At the same time, the prime minister said, to ensure that students' future was not affected, the NEET re-examination was given priority, conducted successfully, and the results were declared without delay," Union minister Kiren Rijiju said after the meeting.Protests continued at Jantar Mantar as hundreds of students and their supporters returned to Jantar Mantar a day after their march to Parliament, saying the alleged use of force by police had only reinforced their determination to press on with the agitation.The protest site remained crowded through the afternoon, with students, parents and supporters raising slogans over the alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination and reiterating their demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

World.title: CJP removes spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya, condemns 'deeply insensitive actions'
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party removes spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya

Controversial viral video

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party has removed its spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya after viral videos surfaced showing him during the police crackdown on protesters at Jantar Mantar, calling his conduct "deeply insensitive" and "unacceptable. ""We strongly condemn the deeply insensitive actions of our spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya, whose videos surfaced while peaceful protestors and our team were facing brutal police violence. Such conduct is unacceptable, shows a complete lack of judgment, and is wholly inconsistent with the values and principles of our movement," the party said in a statement.Dahiya has been removed as spokesperson and relieved of all official duties, the party said.The clip, which went viral on social media, showed Dahiya at a burger outlet in a mall near the protest site. A group of people can be heard confronting him and questioning why he wasn't with the protesters, asking: "You were eating a burger while we were protesting?"The exact timing of the video and the circumstances in which it was recorded could not be independently verified.In an Instagram video addressing the backlash, Dahiya said he had been working continuously for the movement for around one and a half months and had barely slept for the past two nights.He questioned why eating a burger had become such a major issue. In the caption, he also made a comment stating that: âBy the way, I didnt eat the burger, because I felt that it has maida and transfats, and maybe I should eat elsewhere.â"No one pays me to participate in the protest," he said, adding that he was doing what he was doing for the country. "Yes, I will eat the burger," he said.Before this incident Dahiya had also come under fire on social media for his views on transgender people and stating that most women are 'not political'.The move comes as the CJP continues its protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination irregularities. Police had earlier resorted to a baton charge and detained several protesters during a march to Parliament on Monday.

World.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: 'A tyrant must appear deeply religious. People are less likely to rebel because they think God is on his side'
World.content:
"A tyrant must appear deeply religious. People are less likely to fear injustice from a ruler they believe is pious. They are also less likely to rebel because they think God is on his side.

"

More than two millennia after his death, Aristotle continues to shape the way we understand politics and power. Among the many ideas attributed to the ancient Greek philosopher, one observation from his seminal work Politics has remained particularly enduring for its stark assessment of how tyrants sustain their rule.

The quote is a modern paraphrase rather than Aristotle's exact words, it accurately captures an argument he made in Politics more than 2,300 years ago.

Born in 384 BC in the Greek city of Stagira, Aristotle is regarded as one of the greatest philosophers in history. A student of Plato and later the teacher of Alexander the Great, he made lasting contributions to philosophy, politics, ethics, logic, biology and natural science. Many of his ideas continue to influence modern political theory, with Politics remaining one of the foundational works on the study of governments, constitutions and the exercise of power.





Written in the fourth century BC, Politics is Aristotle's comprehensive study of how states are organised and governed. Rather than proposing a single ideal system, the work examines different forms of government, including monarchy, aristocracy, democracy, oligarchy and tyranny.

Book V, from which the famous quote is derived, focuses on political instability, revolutions and the methods rulers use to preserve their authority.

The quote is a modern paraphrase of a passage found in Politics, Book V, Chapter 11.

"He should appear to be particularly earnest in the service of the Gods; for if men think that a ruler is religious and has a reverence for the Gods, they are less afraid of suffering injustice at his hands, and they are less disposed to conspire against him, because they believe him to have the very Gods fighting on his side."

According to Aristotle, if subjects believe their ruler is deeply religious and respectful of divine law, they are less likely to suspect him of acting unjustly.

They may also hesitate to conspire against him because they believe the ruler enjoys the favour and protection of the gods.

In other words, the appearance of piety can become a source of political authority, making obedience seem both morally and divinely justified.

The philosopher's point was that people often judge rulers not only by their actions but also by the image they project. A ruler who appears virtuous, just and devout is more likely to inspire trust and loyalty than one who openly relies on coercion.

Importantly, Aristotle was describing how tyrants historically maintained power, not prescribing how rulers ought to behave.

Aristotle's observation endures because it is less about religion and more about the psychology of power. His insight reminds us that throughout history, public perception has often been as important to political authority as military or legal strength.

World.title: 'If someone dies .... ': Delhi Police probes alleged chats ahead of CJP's 'Sansad Chalo' march
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

is examining alleged chat messages exchanged among participants of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) 'Sansad Chalo' march that turned violent on Monday, with some conversations suggesting preparations to maintain communication during a possible internet shutdown and others referring to sacrificing lives for the cause.

Police sources cited by news agency PTI said on Tuesday that investigators were verifying the authenticity of the chats and the identities of those involved before drawing any conclusions.

The alleged messages are being analysed along with CCTV footage, drone visuals, mobile phone videos and other electronic evidence collected during the investigation into the clashes, which left 118 police personnel and around 70 protesters injured, besides damaging 15-20 government vehicles.

Chats allegedly discussed communication during internet shutdown

According to PTI, some of the alleged messages discussed alternative ways to stay connected if internet services were disrupted during the protest.

"After reaching the protest site you might not get network in your device. Police last time also used network jammers and this time too can do so. However, it is very important to stay connected to the group you came with," one of the alleged messages read.

Investigators said participants had also shared links to applications that could reportedly function using Bluetooth signals in the absence of internet connectivity.





"Make sure all of your group have the same app installed and are already connected before entering the protest site," another alleged message stated.

Police said they were examining the applications mentioned in the chats and would take action based on the findings.

Police examining messages on 'sacrifice' and mobilisation

The alleged conversations also contained politically charged remarks and mobilisation messages.

One participant claimed the following day would be the "last day of Modi Government."

Some messages also referred to the possibility of participants sacrificing their lives during the protest.

"Dekho yarr jo jaan dene tak ko taiyaar woh ye sunlo ke kam se kam tumhara ehsan to rahega aane wali pidiyon par, aane wale bacho par (if someone died, future generations would remember such sacrifice)," one alleged message read.

Another message stated, "Bhai agar kisi ki maut hoti hai to usme to sarkar pe zyada pressure aayega (if someone dies, then it will create a lot of pressure on the government)."

Police said investigators were examining the context in which these remarks were made and were trying to determine whether they reflected personal opinions exchanged among participants or were part of any coordinated effort linked to the violence.

Forensic examination of the digital communications is underway, with cyber experts assisting in establishing the origin, circulation and authenticity of the messages.

"Every message was being subjected to technical verification before being treated as evidence," a police source said, adding that the investigation remained evidence-based and further legal action would depend on corroborative material.

Multiple FIRs registered after violence

The alleged chats surfaced as Delhi Police expanded its probe into the violence during the 'Sansad Chalo' march.

Police have so far registered four FIRs and are preparing two more in connection with the violence, vandalism, alleged conspiracy and other incidents linked to the protest.

The cases, registered at Parliament Street, Connaught Place and other police stations, invoke provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Arms Act and the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act.

Investigators are also examining CCTV footage, drone recordings, mobile phone videos, social media posts and other digital evidence to identify those involved in the clashes.

Following the violence, security has been tightened across the national capital with additional police and paramilitary personnel deployed at sensitive locations, government installations and major intersections.

World.title: Stopped at Shambhu border on way to Delhi: Why are farmers protesting again
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Farmers from Punjab heading to Delhi for a fresh protest were stopped at the Shambhu border between Punjab and

, where authorities put up barricades and deployed cement blocks to prevent them from proceeding towards the national capital.

The proposed four-hour "Kisan Mahapanchayat" was scheduled to be held at Kisan Ghat, the memorial of former Prime Minister Charan Singh, who was also a prominent farmers' leader.

Why are farmers protesting

Farmers in Punjab have been protesting against the proposed India-United States trade deal, an interim agreement for which was announced after a phone call between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump in February.

They are demanding the cancellation of the trade deal.

The farmers' primary concern is the inclusion of the agriculture and dairy sectors in the proposed agreement. They fear that unrestricted imports of cheaper US products such as maize, soybeans, cotton and dairy items could lead to a fall in domestic crop prices, causing financial losses, particularly for farmers in Punjab and Haryana.

According to farmer leader Sarwan Singh Pandher, who was leading the protesters, they are also concerned about the possible entry of genetically modified (GM) crops and agricultural products into India.





They reiterated their long-standing demand for a legal guarantee on Minimum Support Price (MSP).

Referring to Union minister

's statements on the proposed agreement, Pandher told ANI, "Piyush Goyal says there will be no compromise on the dairy and agriculture sectors, but it seems a deal has already been made."

"The White House press release mentions cotton, soybean, corn, dry fruits, apples, pears, and other agricultural products under a 'Wide Range Trade Agreement.' 'Wide range' covers everything--it is a comprehensive trade agreement. So, I believe Piyush Goyal is not being truthful with the country. The India-US trade deal seems certain," he alleged.

Goyal has been leading negotiations on behalf of India.

World.title: Kremlin says 'in touch' with New Delhi after 4 Indians killed in Ukraine ship strike
World.content:
Russia on Tuesday said it is "in touch" with its partners in New Delhi after four Indians were killed on board a merchant vessel off the coast of Ukraine.

This comes after Kyiv claimed that Russia hit the Golden Leoâa Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship manned by a crew from India and Syriaâwith three cruise missiles on Sunday, killing 10 people.

Earlier in the day, New Delhi summoned the Russian chargÃ© d'affaires over the incident, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

The Ministry of External Affairs strongly condemned the strike, saying attacks on commercial shipping and civilian crew members were unacceptable.

The MEA, in a statement, said, "As per the information available, four Indian nationals have tragically lost their lives, while one is hospitalised in a critical condition.

Our mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the situation and is making every effort to extend all possible assistance to those affected."

The government also reiterated that targeting commercial vessels, endangering civilian seafarers, and disrupting freedom of navigation and international trade were deplorable and should be avoided.

One of those killed has been identified as 26-year-old merchant navy officer Akhil Joyan from Vellarikkundu in Kerala's Kasaragod district.





His family was informed of his death by the shipping company through an email on Monday.

Akhil had recently returned home on leave, got engaged, and resumed duty only a month ago.

According to a Reuters report, Ukrainian officials said a Russian missile strike hit a ship carrying corn near the southern port of Odesa, killing 10 people.

World.title: 'Fight together': Mamata urges INDIA bloc unity against BJP, shuts down door on rebels
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief

on Tuesday urged opposition parties in West Bengal to bury their differences and unite against the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Addressing the annual July 21 Martyrs' Day rally organised near Birla Planetarium, Mamata also termed the leaders who defected from the TMC as "traitors", saying they would never be allowed to return to the party.

"I want everyone to unite under the banner of the INDIA alliance in Bengal to fight the

. I don't have any ego. I urge others also to keep aside their differences and fight together," Mamata said.

Though she did not name the Congress or the CPI(M), her remarks were seen as an appeal to the TMC's INDIA bloc partners, with whom it has maintained an uneasy relationship in West Bengal despite being part of the national opposition alliance.

During the address, Mamata also said that she has "many people" to fill the places of leaders who jumped ship after the TMC suffered a huge setback in the Assembly elections.

"I challenge the traitors to directly join the BJP and fight elections," she said, accusing them of functioning as proxies of the saffron party.

"If you want to support the BJP, go to the BJP. The more of you who leave, the happier I will be. My students and youth workers are there to fill every vacancy," Mamata said.





"Those thieves have gone to the BJP. I will never take them back," she added.

While Banerjee's faction held the Martyrs' Day programme near Birla Planetarium, the breakaway faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee organised a parallel rally on Mayo Road in central Kolkata.

The TMC chief said the rebels, with the help of the BJP, were trying to take away the party's "twin flower" symbol but could not do so as she is the founder-chairperson.

Mamata also announced that she would soon begin touring districts across West Bengal.

"After this, I will travel across the districts. I want to see who has the power to stop me," she said in an apparent swipe at the rebel camp.

The former West Bengal chief minister accused the BJP of trying to prevent her TMC camp from holding the Martyrs' Day programme, alleging that party workers had to guard the stage throughout the previous night after it was targeted.

The TMC is facing its biggest organisational crisis since its formation in 1998. Several senior leaders and MLAs have joined a rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee, with many attributing their exit to

Abhishek Banerjee

's growing influence within the party.

The rebellion has also reached Parliament, where several Lok Sabha MPs have broken away from the Mamata Banerjee-led camp. With rival factions now operating parallel organisational structures, the leadership tussle has emerged as the defining challenge facing the party.

World.title: Satish Jarkiholi urges youth to stay away from drug addiction
World.content:
Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi on Tuesday said that youth should focus on their academic goals without getting caught up in momentary attractions.

“The youth should stay away from drug addiction and work towards making their future bright. Their focus should be aimed at getting quality education and developing discipline and good morals,” he said.

He was speaking after inaugurating ‘Beda Bro’, an event to create awareness against drug addiction, in Belagavi. It was jointly organised by the Police Department and the district administration at Sangolli Rayanna College.

“Drug addiction can have a serious impact on an individual's health, education, family and society. The Police Department, educational institutions, parents and the public should work together to eradicate the drug menace from the society,” the Minister said.

He said that young people are the precious wealth of the country. A healthy and addiction-free society can be built by directing their energy and capabilities in positive ways,” he said.

Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulbarao said that an estimated 18 crore people in the country and about 17 lakh people in Karnataka were suffering from drug addiction and drug-related problems. The State government’s anti-drug abuse campaign was launched with a view to expose youth to such long-term implications of the issues. These programmes would be extended to the taluk level in the coming days, he said.

He said that students should develop good values along with education and stay away from vices like drugs so that they become good citizens.

“In the past, society and parents used to carefully prevent vices among children. But now the attitude towards cigarette consumption is seen as a normal practice which is unfortunate,” Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Roshan said, advising the youth to adopt a healthy lifestyle.

Superintendent of Police K. Ramarajan said, “The fight against drug abuse required ‘the cooperation of all sections of society. Controlling this is not only the responsibility of the Police Department, but also of parents, teachers, students and the general public,” he said.

Documentaries from the ‘Beda Bro’ and ‘Rise’ campaigns were screened at the programme to create awareness among students about the ill-effects of drugs.

MLA Asif (Raju) Sait, Vice-Chancellor of Channamma University C.M. Thyagaraja, lecturers, students and officials from various departments were present.

World.title: Statehood imperative for restoring J&K's special status: Chief Minister
World.content:
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (July 21) said statehood was the foundation for restoring the special status of the Union Territory.

Also read | Fulfil the promise: On restoring Statehood to Jammu and Kashmir

Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Abdullah said the National Conference (NC) will keep reminding the Centre of its promise to restore Jammu and Kashmir's statehood and expressed hope that the commitment would be fulfilled.

He also asserted that his protest in Delhi was "just the beginning" and not the end of the party's campaign.

The Chief Minister was in the national capital on Monday (July 20) to stage a protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir. However, police stopped him and other party leaders from moving towards the protest venue due to the heavy security deployment for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) march.

"Some people tell us to talk about [restoration of] Article 370 and J-K's special status first... I want to ask them what does Article 370 or 371 mean without statehood?" Abdullah said.

He said statehood was imperative for the restoration of special status.

"Whatever special status J&K would have, be it under Article 370 or anything else, the point is how to share the powers between the Centre and J-K. There is no sharing of powers between the Centre and a UT because a UT does not have any powers. All powers of a UT lie either with the Centre or the Lok Bhavan. All Cabinet decisions go to Lok Bhavan first," he said.

"So, what power sharing are you talking about under a special status if you do not have a state list? The issue is only that. How many state list powers, Central list or concurrent list powers are there under any special status, that is the argument?" he said.

Abdullah described statehood as the foundation for restoring special status.

"Where is the state list without the statehood? It is all Union list. That is why we say that to reach there, we have to lay a foundation, then we can build a building on that," he said.

Mr. Abdullah said the party has not forgotten the issue of special status.

"We passed the resolution [on special status] on the first day of the assembly session after government formation. It [resolution] is still alive. This resolution can be discussed only after we have statehood," he said.

He also sought to reassure the people of Jammu and Kashmir that the party remained committed to promises it had made.

"I assure my people we stand by our promises and will remain steadfast. A new strategy and programme will soon be decided by the party leadership," the Chief Minister said.

World.title: Tamil rapper Arivu detained during bid to protest against NEET near Secretariat in Chennai, CM Vijay meets him
World.content:
Popular Tamil rapper Arivu (Arivarasu Kalainesan) was detained by Greater Chennai City police after he and three others attempted to stage a protest near the Secretariat on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), demanding the abolition of the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET).

Arivu and the three protesters gathered at the entrance of the Secretariat and raised slogans demanding that NEET be scrapped. They also sought action against the police over the crackdown on protesters during the march to Parliament in Delhi.

I strongly condemn the TN Government led by @actorvijay for arresting rap singer and my dear brother 'Therukkural' Arivu for speaking out against NEET.



His voice reflects the sentiments and demands of not just Tamil Nadu, but millions of people across India.



At a time when the… pic.twitter.com/aIJyzewZAC — Udhay (@Udhaystalin) July 21, 2026

CM Vijay invites to chamber

A senior police officer said, “We picked up Arivu and three others as they were staging a protest near the Secretariat, a high-security zone. They were later released.” Subsequently, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay invited Arivu to his chamber in the Secretariat and listened to his concerns.

Arivu is best known for his Tamil independent music including the hit song Enjoy Enjaami, and for film tracks such as Vaathi Raid from Vijay-starrer Master (2021), Single Pasanga from the movie ‘Natpe Thunai’ (2019), Neeye Oli from ‘Sarpatta Parambarai’ (2021), Golden Sparrow from ‘Nilavuku En Mel Ennadi Kobam’, and Thalapathy Kacheri from ‘Jana Nayagan’ (2026), starring the Chief Minister.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: U.S. strikes Iran for 10th consecutive night as Tehran strikes tanker in the Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Iran attacked a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz early on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), forcing its crew to abandon the ship, while the United States conducted yet another round of airstrikes targeting the Islamic Republic as they struggle over control of the key waterway.

Also read: An expanding regional war

The 10 consecutive nights of U.S. airstrikes haven’t compelled Tehran to loosen its grip on the Strait, through which about a fifth of all crude oil and natural gas traded once passed in peacetime.

Even as the U.S. and Iran inch closer to all-out war again, Iran’s Interior Minister travelled to Pakistan, a key mediator in the conflict, for talks. However, it remains unclear just what new deal could be reached to end the fighting.

The interim deal signed last month that was meant to end the fighting has crumbled. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has largely stalled. And as fighting intensifies, both sides have targeted civilian infrastructure relied on by millions of people.
